blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: By the oath of that era of the Beloved (Prophet Muhammad).

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
By the oath of that era of the Beloved (Prophet Muhammad).

blocks.text: {وَالْعَصْرِ: By the oath of the era.} One opinion of the exegetes regarding the word “Asr” mentioned in this verse is that it means an era. Since an era contains extraordinary events, and the changing conditions within it become a source of admonition for the observer, and since these things point towards Allah Almighty’s power, wisdom, and Oneness, it is possible that the oath of an era is intended here.

runs.text: {وَالْعَصْرِ: By the oath of the era.} One opinion of the exegetes regarding the word “Asr” mentioned in this verse is that it means an era. Since an era contains extraordinary events, and the changing conditions within it become a source of admonition for the observer, and since these things point towards Allah Almighty’s power, wisdom, and Oneness, it is possible that the oath of an era is intended here.

blocks.text: The second opinion is that “Asr” also refers to the time before sunset. It is therefore possible that an oath was sworn by that time concerning the one who suffers loss, just as the oath of “Duha”, meaning the forenoon, was mentioned concerning the one who gains profit.

blocks.text: The third opinion is that “Asr” may refer to the Asr prayer, which is the last of the daytime acts of worship. The oath may have been sworn by it here because of its excellence.

blocks.text: The fourth opinion is this, and it is the one towards which the heart inclines: the era intended here is the particular era of the Crown of Prophethood صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ, an era of great goodness and blessings. Thus, just as Allah Almighty swore by the dwelling and place of the Radiant Beloved صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ in “لَاۤ اُقْسِمُ بِهٰذَا الْبَلَدِ”, and just as He swore by the blessed life of the Noble Prophet صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ by saying “لَعَمْرُكَ”, so here, by saying “وَالْعَصْرِ”, He swore by the sacred era of His Beloved صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ.

blocks.text: It is learned from this that the era of the Leader of the Messengers صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ is superior to all eras, the city of the Noble Messenger صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ is superior to all cities, and the blessed life of the Beloved صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ is superior to all lives. (Khazin, Surah Al-'Asr, under verse 1, 4/405; Sawi, Surah Al-'Asr, under verse 1, 6/2419, excerpted.)

blocks.text: A'la Hazrat رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ says:

runs.text: A'la Hazrat رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ says:

blocks.text:
God has bestowed on you a rank sublime,
Such as none received before, nor shall receive in time;
The Glorious Quran has sworn by your city and your speech,
O King, and by your blessed life, beyond all reach.

blocks.text: {اِنَّ الْاِنْسَانَ لَفِیْ خُسْرٍ: Indeed, mankind is surely in loss.} The summary of this verse and the verse after it is that Allah Almighty mentioned an oath and then declared that mankind is surely in loss: the lifespan that is his capital and principal wealth is decreasing at every moment. However, those who believed, performed good deeds, advised one another to have faith and perform righteous deeds, and advised one another to remain patient over the troubles and hardships that came to them in the path of religion are not in loss, by the grace of Allah Almighty. Rather, they are the ones who gain profit, because every part of their lives that passed was spent in goodness and obedience. (Ruh al-Bayan, Surah Al-'Asr, under verses 2–3, 10/505–506; Khazin, Surah Al-'Asr, under verses 2–3, 4/405, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Three matters are learned from these verses:

runs.text: Three matters are learned from these verses:

blocks.text: 1. A person’s life is his most valuable capital, and he can benefit from this capital only when he spends it in obedience and submission to Allah Almighty. If he continues spending this capital in disbelief in Allah Almighty, disobedience to Him, and sins, he will gain no benefit; rather, he will suffer a very great loss. Therefore, every person should consider his life a valuable opportunity and become engaged in obedience and worship of Allah Almighty.

blocks.text: {اِنَّاۤ اَعْطَیْنٰكَ الْكَوْثَرَ: O Beloved, We have indeed bestowed upon you countless excellences.} The exegetes have expressed various opinions concerning the exegesis of Al-Kawthar. The summary of all these opinions is that Allah Almighty says: O Beloved, We have indeed bestowed upon you countless excellences, made you superior to all creation by granting you abundant virtues, and given you both outward beauty and inward beauty, noble lineage, Prophethood, the Book, wisdom, knowledge, intercession, the Pool of Kawthar, the Station of Praise, a great number of followers, victory over the enemies of the religion, abundant conquests, and countless blessings and excellences whose end cannot be reached. (Khazin, Al-Kawthar, under verse 1, 4/413–414, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Five matters are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Five matters are learned from this verse:

blocks.text: 1. Allah Almighty has already granted Kawthar to His Beloved صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ, because it is not stated here, “We shall grant you Kawthar”; rather, it is stated, “Indeed, We have granted you Kawthar.”

blocks.text: 2. Allah Almighty's granting this gift to His Beloved صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ is not on account of His Beloved being a Prophet and Messenger; rather, it is on account of the very person of the Beloved صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ, which is the manifestation of the rank of the Beloved. This is because He said, “اَعْطَیْنٰكَ” — “We have granted you”; He did not say, “اَعْطَیْنَا الرَّسُوْلَ” — “We have granted the Messenger,” or “اَعْطَیْنَا النَّبِیَّ” — “We have granted the Prophet.”

blocks.text: 3. This gift bestowed upon the Crown of Messengership صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ was not granted because of any worship or spiritual exertion. Rather, it was granted through the immense grace and favour of Allah Almighty, because the granting of the gift is mentioned first here, while worship is mentioned afterwards.

blocks.text: {فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَ انْحَرْ: So, you should offer Salah for your Lord, and sacrifice.} This means: O Beloved صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ, Allah Almighty has granted you countless blessings of both worlds and given you a special rank that He has not granted to anyone besides you. Therefore, continue offering Salah for your Lord عَزَّوَجَلَّ, Who granted you Kawthar and honoured you with dignity and nobility, so that the idol-worshippers may be disgraced. Opposing those who sacrifice in the name of idols, sacrifice for your Lord عَزَّوَجَلَّ and in His name. One opinion concerning the exegesis of this verse is also that “Salah” refers to the Eid prayer. (Madarik, Al-Kawthar, under verse 2, p. 1378; Khazin, Al-Kawthar, under verse 2, 4/416–417, excerpted.)

blocks.text: {اِنَّ شَانِئَكَ هُوَ الْاَبْتَرُ: Indeed, he who is your enemy, only he is deprived of every goodness.} Occasion of revelation: When Sayyid al-Mursaleen's صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ son, Sayyiduna Qasim رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, passed away, the disbelievers called him “Abtar”, meaning one whose lineage had been cut off. They said that his lineage no longer remained, that after him his mention would not remain, and that all this talk would come to an end. Upon this, this blessed Surah was revealed, and Allah Almighty gave a powerful refutation of those disbelievers. In this verse, He declared: O Beloved صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ, indeed your enemy alone is deprived of every goodness, not you. Your chain will continue until the Day of Judgement, your offspring will also be numerous, and the world will be filled with those who follow you. Your mention will be raised upon the pulpits. The scholars and preachers born until the Day of Judgement will continue mentioning you along with the mention of Allah Almighty. In the Hereafter, you have that which no description can express. One possessing such a rank cannot be abtar. The nameless, unknown one deprived of every goodness is your enemy. (Madarik, Al-Kawthar, under verse 3, p. 1378; Khazin, Al-Kawthar, under verse 3, 4/417, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Indeed, We have bestowed abundant goodness upon you. What comparison is there between having one's name continue through one's children and the elevation of your mention? Millions of people with children have passed whose names no one even knows, whereas the drum of praise for you will resound throughout the corners of the world and the regions of the earth until the establishment of the Day of Judgement. The sermon in which your honoured name is mentioned will be delivered throughout the spheres of the heavens and the horizons of the earth forever and ever.

blocks.text: Your enemy is the one whose lineage has been cut off. The very sons of whom he is proud, namely Amr and Hisham رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا, will become his enemies. By entering your true religion, they will separate from his lineage because of the difference in religion and will be counted among your religious sons. Even if a person had no descendants, that alone would merely mean that his name did not continue. It is a thousand times worse for an evil name to remain. The impure name of your enemy will always be mentioned with evil and condemnation, and on the Day of Judgement he will receive the full punishment for these insolences. وَ الْعِیَاذُ بِاللّٰہ تعالٰی. (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 30/167–168)

blocks.text: {اِذَا جَآءَ نَصْرُ اللّٰهِ وَ الْفَتْحُ: When help and victory of Allah comes.} The summary of this Surah is that when the help and victory of Allah Almighty comes to you, O Beloved صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ, against your enemies, and you see that previously people were entering Islam one by one or two by two, while now they are entering the religion of Allah Almighty in hosts, then at that time glorify your Lord عَزَّوَجَلَّ while praising Him, and seek forgiveness from Him for your Ummah. Indeed, He is the One Who accepts repentance abundantly. It should be remembered that the victory mentioned in this verse may refer to the general victories of Islam, or it may refer specifically to the Conquest of Makkah. (Khazin, An-Nasr, under verses 1–3, 4/423–424; Madarik, An-Nasr, under verses 1–3, p. 1380, excerpted.)

blocks.text: 1. The number of the noble Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ was not five or seven; rather, it was in the thousands.

blocks.text: It is narrated from Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Umar رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا that this Surah was revealed at Mina during the Farewell Pilgrimage. After this, the verse “اَلْیَوْمَ اَكْمَلْتُ لَكُمْ دِیْنَكُمْ” was revealed. After its revelation, the Radiant Presence صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ remained in this world for 80 days. Then the verse “الْكَلٰلَةِؕ” was revealed, after which the Sacred Presence صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ remained in this world for 50 days. Then the verse “وَ اتَّقُوْا یَوْمًا تُرْجَعُوْنَ فِیْهِ اِلَى اللّٰهِ” was revealed, after which the Noble Presence صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ remained in this world for 21 days or 7 days. (Jalalayn ma'a Jaml, An-Nasr, under verse 3, 8/426.)

blocks.text: After the revelation of this Surah, the noble Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ understood that the religion had become complete and perfect, and that the Noble Messenger صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ would therefore not remain in this world for much longer. Thus, Sayyiduna Umar رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ wept upon hearing this Surah because of this thought. It is narrated that after the revelation of this Surah, the Sovereign of Both Worlds صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ said in a sermon: “Allah Almighty gave a bondsman the choice of whether he wished to remain in this world or accept the meeting with Him, and that bondsman chose the meeting with Allah Almighty.” Upon hearing this, Sayyiduna Abu Bakr Siddiq رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ submitted: “O Messenger of Allah صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ, may our lives, our wealth, our fathers, and our children all be sacrificed for you.” (Tafsir Kabir, An-Nasr, under verse 3, 11/346; Ruh al-Bayan, An-Nasr, under verse 3, 10/531; Madarik, An-Nasr, under verse 3, p. 1380, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Arabic: لِاِیْلٰفِ قُرَیْشٍۙ   (1)

runs.text: Arabic:
لِاِیْلٰفِ قُرَیْشٍۙ   (1)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: In order to give inclination to the Quraysh.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
In order to give inclination to the Quraysh.

blocks.text: {لِاِیْلٰفِ قُرَیْشٍ: In order to give inclination to the Quraysh.} The summary of this Surah is that the blessings of Allah Almighty are countless. One of these evident blessings is that He inspired the Quraysh every year to make two journeys and placed love for them in the hearts of people. Thus, the Quraysh would travel to Yemen in winter for trade and to Syria in summer. In every place, people would call them the people of the Sacred Precinct and would honour and respect them. They conducted their trade safely, benefited from it, and continually brought capital to Makkah Mukarramah, where there is neither agriculture nor the means of livelihood, in order to maintain their residence there. The blessing of Allah Almighty upon them is evident, and these people benefit from it. Therefore, they should, in gratitude for this blessing, worship the Lord of the Glorious Ka'bah, Who gave them food through these journeys when they had suffered hunger in their homeland because there was no agriculture before these journeys. He also granted them security from fear because of the Sacred Precinct and because they were residents of Makkah: no one opposed them, even though killing and plunder continually took place around them and in their surrounding areas, caravans were looted, and travellers were killed. Some exegetes have said that granting security from fear means that they were protected from leprosy, so that this disease would not occur in their city. Other exegetes have said that it means that, through the blessing of the Crown of Messengership صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ, they were granted safety from the greatest fear. (Khazin, Quraysh, under verses 1–4, 4/410–412.)

blocks.text: An Introduction to the Quraysh

runs.text: An Introduction to the Quraysh

blocks.text: Quraysh is the name of the tribe in which the blessed birth of the Leader of the Messengers صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ took place. Various reasons have been stated for this tribe's name. One of them is that among the forefathers of the Beloved Prophet صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ was the accomplished personality Fahr ibn Malik. His title was “Quraysh,” and his descendants were called “Qurayshi” or “Quraysh.” Fahr ibn Malik was called “Quraysh” because “Quraysh” is the name of a very powerful sea animal that devours other sea animals. This animal always remains dominant over all animals and is never overcome. Since Fahr ibn Malik was dominant over all the tribes of Arabia because of his courage and God-given strength, all the Arabs began calling him by the title “Quraysh.” (Zarqani 'ala al-Mawahib, al-Maqsad al-Awwal fi Tashrif Allah Ta'ala Lahu 'Alayhis-Salatu was-Salam, 1/143–145; Sirat-e-Mustafa, pp. 51–52.)

blocks.text: Here are three hadiths concerning the Quraysh:

runs.text: Here are three hadiths concerning the Quraysh:

blocks.text: 1. It is narrated from Sayyiduna Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ that the Noble Messenger صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ said: “Allah Almighty chose Kinanah from among the descendants of Sayyiduna Isma'il عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام, chose Quraysh from Kinanah, chose Banu Hashim from Quraysh, and chose me from Banu Hashim.” (Muslim, Book of Virtues, chapter on the excellence of the lineage of the Prophet, etc., p. 1249, hadith 1 (2276).)

blocks.text: 2. blocks.text: Providing Ease to People and Establishing Peace in Society Are Fundamental Priorities and Distinguishing Features of Islam

runs.text: Providing Ease to People and Establishing Peace in Society Are Fundamental Priorities and Distinguishing Features of Islam

blocks.text: Verse 4 mentions being given food in a state of hunger and being granted security in a state of fear. It should be remembered that hunger and fear are two things that play an extremely important and central role in increasing sins and immoral acts in society, raising the crime rate, spreading disorder, and causing unrest. On the other hand, removing hunger and dispelling fear greatly help establish a pure environment and an atmosphere of peace and security in society. In other words, wherever people are provided with facilities and sufficient arrangements are made to meet their necessities of life, the rate of sins and immoral acts will be lower. Wherever peace and security are established, the number of crimes will be negligible and people will live peaceful lives.

Wherever peace and security are established, the number of crimes will be negligible and people will live peaceful lives.

blocks.text: If the conditions of people throughout the world today are examined, it will become clear that the basic reason for the widespread occurrence of adultery, theft, robbery, looting, plunder, murder, bloodshed, disorder, unrest, anxiety, and various other crimes, sins, and fears is the lack of valuable means capable of eliminating hunger, deprivation of the basic facilities required for life, and the absence of necessary arrangements for establishing peace and security. If the commands and teachings of Islam are considered, this reality will appear clearer than daylight: eliminating people's hunger, providing them with facilities, establishing a pure society, and establishing peace are among the fundamental priorities and distinguishing features of Islam. For example, zakat has been made obligatory upon wealthy Muslims in Islam, and giving charity for certain deeds has been commanded. Those who are extremely needy and live in poverty and destitution have been made entitled to receive it, so that there is an organised means of fulfilling their needs and removing poverty and destitution.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Say you (O Beloved), 'He is Allah, He is One.'

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {قُلْ هُوَ اللّٰهُ اَحَدٌ: Say you (O Beloved), He is Allah, He is One.} There were many kinds of disbelievers in Arabia: atheists, polytheists, those who denied the attributes of Allah Almighty, and those who attributed offspring to Allah Almighty, among others. This Surah refutes all of them. The words “هُوَاللّٰهُ” refute the atheists. The word “اَحَدٌ” completely refutes the polytheists, while the remaining disbelievers are refuted in the subsequent verses. Allah Almighty states that He is One, meaning that He is described with attributes of greatness and perfection in Lordship and Divinity. He has no equal, counterpart, or likeness, and He has no partner.

blocks.text: {اَللّٰهُ الصَّمَدُ: Allah is the Independent.} Allah Almighty states that He is independent of everything. He neither eats nor drinks; He has always existed and will always remain. He is not dependent upon anyone for any matter.

runs.text: {اَللّٰهُ الصَّمَدُ: Allah is the Independent.} Allah Almighty states that He is independent of everything. He neither eats nor drinks; He has always existed and will always remain. He is not dependent upon anyone for any matter.

blocks.text: {لَمْ یَلِدْ ﳔ وَ لَمْ یُوْلَدْ: He has no offspring, nor is He born from anyone.} Allah Almighty is pure of offspring, because offspring belongs to the same kind as the father, while Allah Almighty is pure of this. Likewise, He Himself was not born from anyone, because He is Eternal, meaning that He has always existed. Being born is an attribute of something that did not exist before and then came into existence. This verse refutes the polytheists, the Jews, and the Christians alike. The polytheists used to call the angels the daughters of Allah Almighty. blocks.text: The Virtues of the Night of Decree

runs.text: The Virtues of the Night of Decree

blocks.text: The Night of Decree is a night of honour and blessing. It is called the Night of Decree because the commands for the entire year are enforced on this night, and the angels are appointed to the tasks and services of the entire year. It has also been said that it is called the Night of Decree because of its honour and rank above other nights. It is also transmitted that good deeds are accepted on this night and valued in the Divine Court, and for this reason it is called the Night of Decree. (Khazin, Al-Qadr, under verse 1, 4/395.)

It is called the Night of Decree because the commands for the entire year are enforced on this night, and the angels are appointed to the tasks and services of the entire year. It has also been said that it is called the Night of Decree because of its honour and rank above other nights. It is also transmitted that good deeds are accepted on this night and valued in the Divine Court, and for this reason it is called the Night of Decree. (Khazin, Al-Qadr, under verse 1, 4/395.)

blocks.text: Many virtues of this night have been mentioned in hadiths. It is narrated from Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever spends this night in worship, standing in prayer with faith and sincerity, Allah Almighty forgives his previous minor sins.” (Bukhari, Book of Faith, chapter on standing in prayer on the Night of Decree being part of faith, 1/25, hadith 35.)

blocks.text: It is narrated from Sayyiduna Anas ibn Malik رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ that when the month of Ramadan arrived, the Illuminated Presence ﷺ said: “Indeed, this month has come to you, and in it there is a night which is better than a thousand months. Whoever is deprived of this night is deprived of all goodness, and only the one whose lot is deprivation remains deprived.” (Ibn Majah, Book of Fasting, chapter on what has been reported concerning the virtue of the month of Ramadan, 2/298, hadith 1644.)

Whoever is deprived of this night is deprived of all goodness, and only the one whose lot is deprivation remains deprived.” (Ibn Majah, Book of Fasting, chapter on what has been reported concerning the virtue of the month of Ramadan, 2/298, hadith 1644.)

blocks.text: Therefore, every Muslim should spend this night in worship and seek forgiveness abundantly during it, as Sayyidatuna Aishah Siddiqah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا says: “I asked: ‘O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, if I come to know which night is the Night of Decree, what should I say during it?’ He said: ‘Say: اَللّٰهُمَّ اِنَّکَ عَفُوٌّ کَرِیْمٌ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّیْ “O Allah, indeed You are Most Pardoning and Most Generous; You love to pardon, so pardon my sins too.”’” (Tirmidhi, Book of Supplications, chapter 84, 5/306, hadith 3524.)

blocks.text: The Night of Decree Comes Once a Year

runs.text: The Night of Decree Comes Once a Year

blocks.text: It should be remembered that the Night of Decree comes once in the entire year. Numerous narrations establish that it occurs in the last ten days of Ramadan, and most often it is one of the odd nights among them. According to some scholars, the Night of Decree is the twenty-seventh night of Ramadan, and this is also narrated from Imam-e-A'zam رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ. (Madarik, Al-Qadr, under verse 1, p. 1364.)

blocks.text: Reasons for Keeping the Night of Decree Hidden

runs.text: Reasons for Keeping the Night of Decree Hidden

blocks.text: Imam Fakhr al-Din al-Razi رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ says that Allah عزَّوَجَلَّ has kept the Night of Decree hidden for several reasons.

runs.text: Imam Fakhr al-Din al-Razi رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ says that Allah عزَّوَجَلَّ has kept the Night of Decree hidden for several reasons.

blocks.text: 1. Just as He kept other things hidden, Allah عزَّوَجَلَّ kept His pleasure hidden among acts of obedience so that servants would desire every act of obedience. He kept His displeasure hidden among sins so that they would continue avoiding every sin. He kept His saint hidden among people so that people would honour everyone. He kept the acceptance of supplication hidden among supplications so that they would exert themselves in all supplications. He kept the Greatest Name hidden among the Names so that they would honour all the Names. He kept the middle prayer hidden among the prayers so that they would observe all the prayers regularly. He kept the acceptance of repentance hidden so that a servant would persist in all forms of repentance, and He kept the time of death hidden so that a servant would remain fearful. In the same way, He kept the Night of Decree hidden so that people would honour all the nights of Ramadan.

He kept the Greatest Name hidden among the Names so that they would honour all the Names. He kept the middle prayer hidden among the prayers so that they would observe all the prayers regularly. He kept the acceptance of repentance hidden so that a servant would persist in all forms of repentance, and He kept the time of death hidden so that a servant would remain fearful. In the same way, He kept the Night of Decree hidden so that people would honour all the nights of Ramadan.

blocks.text: 2. Therefore, I have kept it hidden.”

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O Beloved, did you not see how your Lord dealt with the People of the Elephant?

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {اَلَمْ تَرَ كَیْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِاَصْحٰبِ الْفِیْلِ: O Beloved, did you not see how your Lord dealt with the People of the Elephant?} The summary of the incident mentioned in this Surah is that when Abraha, the king of Yemen and Abyssinia, saw people preparing to perform Hajj at the House of Allah during the Hajj season, he built a church in Sana'a for the purpose that those performing Hajj would come there instead of going to Makkah and would circumambulate this church.

runs.text: {اَلَمْ تَرَ كَیْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِاَصْحٰبِ الْفِیْلِ: O Beloved, did you not see how your Lord dealt with the People of the Elephant?} The summary of the incident mentioned in this Surah is that when Abraha, the king of Yemen and Abyssinia, saw people preparing to perform Hajj at the House of Allah during the Hajj season, he built a church in Sana'a for the purpose that those performing Hajj would come there instead of going to Makkah and would circumambulate this church.

blocks.text: The people of Arabia found this extremely objectionable. A man from the tribe of Banu Kinanah found an opportunity, relieved himself in that church, and defiled it. When Abraha learned of this, he became extremely enraged and swore that he would demolish the Exalted Ka'bah. Therefore, he set out with his army for this purpose. There were many elephants in this army, and at its front was a huge, mountain-like elephant with a large body, whose name was Mahmood.

blocks.text: When Abraha reached near Makkah, he seized the animals belonging to the people of Makkah. Among them were two hundred camels belonging to Sayyiduna 'Abdul-Muttalib رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ. When Sayyiduna 'Abdul-Muttalib رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ came to Abraha, Abraha honoured him, seated him beside himself, and asked, "For what purpose have you come here, and what is your request?" He replied, "My request is that my camels be returned to me." Abraha said, "I am very astonished after hearing you. I have come here to demolish this House of the Ka'bah, which is your revered and honoured place and that of your forefathers, yet you say nothing about it and are asking for the return of your camels!" He replied, "I am the owner of the camels, so I speak regarding them; and the One Who owns the Ka'bah will Himself protect it."

blocks.text: Hearing this, Abraha returned his camels to him. Sayyiduna 'Abdul-Muttalib رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ returned and informed Quraysh of the situation. He advised them to take refuge in the valleys and peaks of the mountains, so Quraysh did so. Sayyiduna 'Abdul-Muttalib رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ went to the door of the Ka'bah and supplicated in the Divine Court for the protection of the Ka'bah. After completing his supplication, he too went to join his people.

blocks.text: When Abraha ordered his army to prepare at dawn, the condition of the elephant named Mahmood was that it would walk when they directed it elsewhere, but when they turned it towards the Ka'bah, it would sit down. Allah Almighty sent armies of birds against Abraha's army from the direction of the sea. Each bird had three pebbles: two in its two feet and one in its beak. The birds came and began striking them with stones. Thus, when a bird dropped a pebble upon a person, that pebble would break through his helmet, emerge from his head, pierce his body, pass through the elephant, and reach the ground. The name of the person who was to be killed by each pebble was written upon it. In this way, the birds reduced Abraha's soldiers to the condition of the leftover consumed straw of animals. The Noble Prophet ﷺ was born in the very year in which this incident occurred. (خازن، الفیل، تحت الآیۃ: ۱-۵، ۴ / ۴۰۷-۴۱۰، ملخصاً)

blocks.text: {تَبَّتْ یَدَاۤ اَبِیْ لَهَبٍ وَّ تَبَّ: May both the hands of Abu Lahab be destroyed, and he has been destroyed.} Abu Lahab's name was Abd al-'Uzza. He was the son of Abd al-Muttalib and the paternal uncle of the Noble Prophet ﷺ. He was a very fair and handsome man; for this reason, his kunya was Abu Lahab, and he became famous by this kunya.

blocks.text: The daughters of the Noble Prophet ﷺ, Sayyidatuna Ruqayyah and Sayyidatuna Umm Kulthum رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا, were married to his sons, 'Utbah and 'Utaybah. After this Surah was revealed, Abu Lahab caused those daughters to be divorced. The incident of 'Utbah is also highly instructive: along with divorcing the daughter of the Noble Prophet ﷺ, he insulted the Noble Prophet ﷺ. Therefore, the Beloved of both worlds ﷺ supplicated for his destruction. Consequently, despite making extensive preparations for his protection during a journey, a lion tore him apart.

blocks.text: The destruction of both hands of Abu Lahab in this verse means the destruction of his person. This blessed verse foretold Abu Lahab's destruction. Thus, he suffered a terrible death: he died one week after the Battle of Badr from a disease of black spots, called 'adasah by the Arabs. The Arabs regarded it as a contagious disease and kept far away from it. Therefore, this rejected man’s corpse remained there for three days. It swelled, burst, and began to give off a foul smell; then labourers were paid to remove it. (Ruh al-Bayan, Al-Masad, under verse 2, 10/534.)

blocks.text: {وَّ امْرَاَتُهٗؕ-حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ: And his wife (too), carrying the bundle of wood on her head.} Umm Jamil, the daughter of Harb ibn Umayyah and the sister of Abu Sufyan, held intense enmity and hostility towards the Noble Messenger ﷺ. Despite being a very wealthy woman from a prominent family, she went to such an extreme in her enmity towards the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that she would herself carry a bundle of thorns on her head and place it in the path of the Noble Messenger ﷺ, so that it would cause pain and harm to the Illuminated Presence ﷺ and his Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ. The harming of the Most Esteemed Prophet ﷺ was so dear to her that she would not even tolerate receiving anyone else's help in this work. (Baydawi, Al-Masad, under verses 4–5, 5/545; Khazin, Abu Lahab, under verse 4, 4/425, excerpted.)

blocks.text: {فِیْ جِیْدِهَا حَبْلٌ مِّنْ مَّسَدٍ: A rope made from date palm fibre is around her neck.} Umm Jamil had a rope made from date-palm fibre around her neck, with which she tied the bundle of thorns. One day, she was bringing this burden and sat upon a stone to rest because she had become tired. By Allah Almighty’s command, an angel pulled the bundle from behind her. It fell, and Umm Jamil was strangled by the rope around her neck, and she died. (Khazin, Abu Lahab, under verse 5, 4/425.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Say you (O Beloved), 'I take refuge in the One Who is the Creator of the daybreak.'

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
Say you (O Beloved), 'I take refuge in the One Who is the Creator of the daybreak.'

blocks.text: {قُلْ اَعُوْذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ: Say you (O Beloved), 'I take refuge in the One Who is the Creator of the daybreak.'} Mentioning Allah Almighty with the attribute “Lord of the daybreak” when seeking refuge is because Allah Almighty creates the morning and removes the darkness of night; therefore, He is also able to remove from the one seeking refuge the circumstances that he fears. Just as a person waits for the morning to dawn during the dark night, a frightened person likewise waits for safety and comfort. In addition, morning is the time when the prayers of the helpless and distressed are made and accepted. Thus, the meaning of this verse is: “I seek the refuge of the One Who creates the time when ease is granted to those afflicted by distress and grief and prayers are accepted.” Another opinion is that “Falaq” is a valley in Hell. (Khazin, Al-Falaq, under verse 1, 4/429–430.)

Thus, the meaning of this verse is: “I seek the refuge of the One Who creates the time when ease is granted to those afflicted by distress and grief and prayers are accepted.” Another opinion is that “Falaq” is a valley in Hell. (Khazin, Al-Falaq, under verse 1, 4/429–430.)

blocks.text: {مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ: From the evil of His entire creation.} This verse seeks refuge from the evil of every creature, whether living or lifeless, legally responsible or not legally responsible. Some commentators have said that “creation” here specifically refers to Iblis, than whom there is no creature worse. (Khazin, Al-Falaq, under verse 2, 4/430.)

blocks.text: {وَ مِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ اِذَا وَقَبَ: And from the evil of the darkness (of the night) when it sets in.} It is narrated from the Mother of the Believers, Sayyidatuna Aishah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا, that the Noble Messenger ﷺ looked towards the moon and said to her, “O Aishah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا, seek Allah Almighty’s refuge from its evil when it sets, for it becomes dark.” (Tirmidhi, Book of Tafsir, chapter on what has been reported concerning Surah Al-Mu'awwidhatayn, 5/240, hadith 3377.) This refers to the last nights of the month. When the moon disappears, the magical practices intended to make people ill are carried out at that time. (Khazin, Al-Falaq, under verse 3, 4/430.)

blocks.text: An Important Sacred-Law Ruling Concerning Amulets

runs.text: An Important Sacred-Law Ruling Concerning Amulets

blocks.text: Remember that amulets and talismans made for impermissible purposes are impermissible and unlawful. However, making a talisman for a permissible purpose, tying knots on it, and reciting verses of the Holy Quran or the Names of Allah Almighty over it and blowing upon it are permissible. The majority of the Noble Companions and the Followers رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ hold this view. (Khazin, Al-Falaq, under verse 1, 4/429, abridged.) This is also established through the blessed practice and saying of the Noble Prophet ﷺ. Accordingly, it is narrated from Sayyidatuna Aishah Siddiqah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا that she said: “Whenever anyone from the family of the Illuminated Presence ﷺ became ill, the Eminent Prophet ﷺ would recite the Mu'awwidhat (that is, Surah Al-Falaq and Surah An-Nas) and blow over him.” (Muslim, Book of Greetings, chapter on reciting the Mu'awwidhat and blowing over the sick, p. 1205, hadith 50 (2192).)

blocks.text: It is narrated from Sayyiduna Ubayd ibn Rifa'ah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ that Sayyidatuna Asma bint Umays رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا said to the Noble Messenger ﷺ, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the sons of Sayyiduna Ja'far رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ are quickly affected by the evil eye. Should I recite something and blow over them?” He said, “Yes, because if anything could overtake Divine Decree, the evil eye would certainly overtake it.” (Tirmidhi, Book of Medicine, chapter on what has been reported concerning incantation for the evil eye, 4/13, hadith 2066.)

blocks.text: {وَ مِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ اِذَا حَسَدَ: And from the evil of the envier when he envies me.} An envier is one who wishes that another person's blessing be taken away. Here, the Jews who envied the Noble Prophet ﷺ are specifically intended by “the envier”; or it refers specifically to the Jewish man Labid ibn al-A'sam. (Khazin, Al-Falaq, under verse 5, 4/430.) In general, this blessed verse is sufficient for seeking refuge from every envier. Envy is the worst quality, and it was the first sin committed in the heavens by Iblis and on earth by Cain. In contrast to envy is benevolent jealousy: this is when a person wishes for himself the same blessing that another person possesses, but does not wish for that blessing to be taken away from the other person. This blessed Surah teaches that magic and envy are among the worst crimes, since they have been mentioned specifically after the general evils.

blocks.text: {قُلْ یٰۤاَیُّهَا الْكٰفِرُوْنَ: Say you (O Beloved), 'O disbelievers!'}. Occasion of revelation: A group of Quraysh said to the Crown of Messengership صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ, “Follow our religion and we will follow your religion. Worship our gods for one year, and we will worship your God for one year.” The Noble Messenger صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ said to them, “May Allah Almighty protect me from associating anyone with Him.” The disbelievers said, “Then just touch one of our gods, and we will affirm you and worship your God.” Upon this, this blessed Surah was revealed, and the Master of both worlds صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ went to the Sacred Mosque. The group of Quraysh who had held this conversation with the Noble Prophet صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ was present there. The Illuminated Presence صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ recited this Surah to them, so they became disappointed and began causing harm to the Esteemed Presence صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ and to his Noble Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ. Remember that the disbelievers intended by this verse are those who, in the knowledge of Allah Almighty, were deprived of faith and were destined to remain upon disbelief. (Khazin, Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun, 4/417–418.)

blocks.text: The Greatness and Nobility of Man

runs.text: The Greatness and Nobility of Man

blocks.text: This also reveals the greatness and nobility of man: Allah Almighty has especially related His attribute of Lordship to him. The scholars have stated a point of wisdom here: the word “اَلنَّاسِ” occurs five times in this Surah. The wisdom is that, since a person receives nourishment and upbringing alone during childhood, the attribute of Lordship, “رَبِّ النَّاسِ”, meaning the attribute of nurturing, is mentioned first. When a person reaches youth, he becomes intoxicated with himself and strays from the way; at that time, legal restraint is needed, so “مَلِكِ النَّاسِ”, meaning the King of the people, is mentioned here. Since a person becomes occupied with worship in old age, the attribute of Allah Almighty’s Divinity and deserving of worship is mentioned in the third place, namely “اِلٰهِ النَّاسِ”. In the fourth place, “النَّاسِ” may refer to the righteous, because Satan generally tries to turn them away from worship through evil whispers. In the fifth place, “النَّاسِ” may refer to mischievous and corrupt people, because refuge from the evil of people is sought there.

blocks.text: The Difference Between Evil Whispering and Inspiration

runs.text: The Difference Between Evil Whispering and Inspiration

blocks.text: Remember that a bad thought is called a whisper, while good thoughts are called inspiration. Whispering comes from Satan, so one should recite لَا حَوْل upon it. Inspiration comes from Allah Almighty through an angel, so one should be grateful to Allah Almighty for it. Evil whispers are more frequent when the commanding self is dominant, while inspiration is more frequent when the tranquil self is dominant. Satan is such an enemy of ours that we do not see him: he sees us, but we do not see him. Therefore, seek refuge in that Powerful Lord عَزَّوَجَلَّ who sees him, while he does not see that Lord عَزَّوَجَلَّ. Seek refuge from a powerful enemy in the Powerful Lord عَزَّوَجَلَّ.

blocks.text: Seek Refuge from the Devils Among Jinn and Mankind

runs.text: Seek Refuge from the Devils Among Jinn and Mankind

blocks.text: A person should seek refuge both from the evil of the devils among the jinn and from the evil of the devils among mankind. In this regard, a beneficial devotional practice is presented here. Sayyidatuna Aishah Siddiqah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا states that when the Messenger of Allah صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ came to his blessed bed at night, he would join his two blessed hands, blow into them, recite Surah قُلْ هُوَ اللّٰهُ اَحَدٌ, قُلْ اَعُوْذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ, and قُلْ اَعُوْذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ, and then wipe his blessed hands over his entire sacred body, beginning with his blessed head and reaching as far as his blessed hands could reach. He would perform this action three times. (Bukhari, Book of the Virtues of the Quran, chapter on the virtue of the Mu'awwidhat, 3/407, hadith 5017.)

Reciting them will protect you from every evil thing.” (Sunan an-Nasa'i, Book of Seeking Refuge, chapter 1, p. 862, hadith 5438.)

blocks.text: Definition of Praise and Gratitude

runs.text: Definition of Praise and Gratitude

blocks.text: Praise means commending someone on account of their voluntary qualities, whereas gratitude means honouring someone with the tongue, heart, or limbs in return for their favour. Since we generally praise Allah Almighty with His favours in view, this praise of ours is also gratitude.

blocks.text: Many virtues of praising and glorifying Allah Almighty have been mentioned in the hadith. Three of them are given below:

runs.text: Many virtues of praising and glorifying Allah Almighty have been mentioned in the hadith. Three of them are given below:

blocks.text: 1. Sayyiduna Anas ibn Malik رَضِیَ اللہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Prophet ﷺ said, “Allah Almighty is pleased with a servant who praises Allah Almighty after eating something and praises Allah Almighty after drinking something.” (Muslim, Book of Remembrance and Supplication, chapter on the desirability of praising Allah, p. 1463, hadith 89 (2734).)

blocks.text: The Islamic Ruling Concerning Praise

blocks.text: Praising Allah is obligatory in a sermon, recommended after eating, Sunnah after sneezing, forbidden after committing a forbidden act, and disbelief in some circumstances.

blocks.text: {لِلّٰهِ: For Allah.} “Allah” is the majestic name of the Exalted Being Who encompasses all perfect attributes. Some exegetes have also stated meanings for this word. One meaning is “the One deserving worship”; another is “the Being before Whose knowledge intellects are bewildered”; a third is “the Being in Whose court tranquillity is attained”; and a fourth is “the Being Whose refuge is sought at a time of hardship.” (Baydawi, Al-Fatihah, 1/32.)

blocks.text: {اَلرَّحْمٰنْ: The Most Gracious.} Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim are two attributive names of Allah Almighty. Ar-Rahman means the Being Who bestows blessings and shows very great mercy, while Ar-Rahim means the One Who shows abundant mercy.

runs.text: {اَلرَّحْمٰنْ: The Most Gracious.} Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim are two attributive names of Allah Almighty. Ar-Rahman means the Being Who bestows blessings and shows very great mercy, while Ar-Rahim means the One Who shows abundant mercy.

blocks.text: Remember that, in reality, the Being Who bestows blessings is Allah Almighty. He alone is the Being Who does not demand compensation for His mercy. Allah Almighty alone bestows every small and great, outward and inward, physical and spiritual, worldly and Hereafter-related blessing. Whatever blessing reaches anyone in the world is from the mercy of Allah Almighty, because creating the feeling of mercy in someone's heart, granting the ability to show mercy, bringing the blessing into existence, enabling another person to benefit from it, and granting sound limbs with which to benefit are all from Allah Almighty alone.

blocks.text: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Qurtubi رَحْمَۃُاللہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ states: Allah Almighty mentioned His two attributes, Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim, after “رَبِّ الْعٰلَمِیْنَ”. The reason is that when Allah Almighty declared that He is the Lord of all the worlds, this produced fear in the heart of the listener and reader because of Allah Almighty's majesty. Along with this, His two attributes, Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim, were mentioned, and within them there is encouragement to obey Allah Almighty. Thus, both warning and encouragement were stated, so that a servant becomes properly inclined towards obeying Allah Almighty and makes a strong effort to refrain from disobeying Him. (Qurtubi, Al-Fatihah, under verse 2, 1/129, part one.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: The Owner of the Day of Recompense.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
The Owner of the Day of Recompense.

blocks.text: {مٰلِكِ یَوْمِ الدِّیْنِ: The Owner of the Day of Recompense.} The Day of Recompense refers to the Day of Judgement. On that day, righteous Muslims will receive reward, while sinners and disbelievers will receive punishment. “Owner” means one who may exercise authority over the things in his ownership as he wishes. Although Allah Almighty is the Owner of both this world and the Hereafter, the Day of Judgement has been mentioned specifically here so that its importance may settle in the heart.

blocks.text: The manifestation of Allah Almighty's ownership will also be greater in the Hereafter than in this world, because on that day no one will possess the apparent sovereignty that Allah Almighty had granted people in the world. For this reason, ownership of the Day of Judgement has been mentioned here specifically.

blocks.text: The Difference Between Worship and Reverence

runs.text: The Difference Between Worship and Reverence

blocks.text: The meaning of worship is very clear. It is enough to understand that considering someone worthy of worship and showing them any kind of reverence is called worship. If someone is not considered worthy of worship, it is merely reverence and is not worship. For example, standing with one's hands folded in prayer is worship; but standing with one's hands folded, like in prayer, before a teacher, spiritual guide, or parents is merely reverence and is not worship. The difference between the two is the one just stated.

blocks.text: Important Matters Learned from “اِیَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ”

runs.text: Important Matters Learned from “اِیَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ”

blocks.text: The verse uses plural forms, such as “we worship only You”. This indicates that prayer should be performed in congregation. Another benefit of joining others in worship is that the worship of sinners joins with the worship of beloved and accepted servants of Allah Almighty in the Divine court and attains acceptance. It is also learned that one should express one's servitude in the court of Allah Almighty before presenting one's need. Imam Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Nasafi رَحْمَۃُاللہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ states: Worship was mentioned before seeking help because presenting a means in the court of Allah Almighty before requesting a need is closer to acceptance. (Madarik, Al-Fatihah, under verse 4, p. 14.)

blocks.text: Necessary Clarification Concerning the Words “يَا مُحَمَّد” in the Hadith

runs.text: Necessary Clarification Concerning the Words “يَا مُحَمَّد” in the Hadith

blocks.text: Imam Ahmad Raza Khan رَحْمَۃُاللہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ, the highest authority, states: “The scholars explicitly state that calling the Esteemed Presence ﷺ by name is forbidden. This is truly a matter of justice: when the One Who is his Owner and Master, Blessed and Exalted, does not call him by name, what opportunity does a slave have to overstep the path of respect? Rather, Imam Zayn al-Din al-Maraghi and other verifying scholars have stated that if these words occur in a supplication that the Noble Prophet ﷺ himself taught, such as the supplication ‘يَا مُحَمَّدُ اِنِّیْ تَوَجَّہْتُ بِکَ اِلٰی رَبِّیْ’, one should nevertheless say ‘يَا رَسُوْلَ اللہ’ or ‘يَا نَبِیَّ اللہ’ in their place, even though supplication wording is not changed as far as possible. This important matter, of which most people of the age are heedless, must be preserved.” (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 30/157–158.)

blocks.text: {وَ اِیَّاكَ نَسْتَعِیْنُ: And from You alone may we seek help.} This verse states that seeking help, whether through a means or without a means, is exclusive to Allah Almighty, and that He alone is the One from Whom help should truly be sought. Imam Ahmad Raza Khan رَحْمَۃُاللہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ states:

runs.text: {وَ اِیَّاكَ نَسْتَعِیْنُ: And from You alone may we seek help.} This verse states that seeking help, whether through a means or without a means, is exclusive to Allah Almighty, and that He alone is the One from Whom help should truly be sought. Imam Ahmad Raza Khan رَحْمَۃُاللہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ states:

blocks.text: “True seeking of help means believing the one from whom help is sought to be inherently powerful, independently sovereign, and self-sufficient, so that he possesses the ability to help through his own essence without Allah Almighty's granting. Holding this belief about anyone besides Allah Almighty is polytheism according to every Muslim. No Muslim holds such a belief concerning anyone besides Allah Almighty. A Muslim believes concerning the accepted servants of Allah that they are a means and intermediary for reaching the Divine court and for needs to be fulfilled.

runs.text: “True seeking of help means believing the one from whom help is sought to be inherently powerful, independently sovereign, and self-sufficient, so that he possesses the ability to help through his own essence without Allah Almighty's granting. Holding this belief about anyone besides Allah Almighty is polytheism according to every Muslim. No Muslim holds such a belief concerning anyone besides Allah Almighty. A Muslim believes concerning the accepted servants of Allah that they are a means and intermediary for reaching the Divine court and for needs to be fulfilled.

blocks.text: “Just as true existence, meaning existing through one's own essence without anyone creating one, is exclusive to Allah Almighty, it is not polytheism to call someone existent unless true existence is intended. Similarly, true knowledge, meaning knowledge possessed through one's own essence without anyone granting it, and true teaching, meaning teaching someone independently without being in need of anything, are exclusive to Allah Almighty. Even so, calling another person knowledgeable or seeking knowledge from him is not polytheism unless those original meanings are intended. The matter of seeking help is the same: its true meaning is exclusive to Allah Almighty, while seeking a means and intermediary is established for others besides Allah Almighty and is correct. Indeed, this meaning is specific to those besides Allah, because Allah Almighty is pure of becoming a means or intermediary. Who is above Him that He would need to be a means to Him, and who besides Him is the true fulfiller of needs that another could become an intermediary between them?

blocks.text: There are so many examples of helping in the blessed life of the Crown of Messengership ﷺ that a large book could be compiled if they were all gathered. A few examples are as follows:

runs.text: There are so many examples of helping in the blessed life of the Crown of Messengership ﷺ that a large book could be compiled if they were all gathered. A few examples are as follows:

blocks.text:
1. It is mentioned in Sahih Bukhari that the Noble Prophet ﷺ fed the entire army with a small amount of food. (Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions, chapter on the Battle of the Trench, 3/51–52, hadith 4101; Al-Khasa'is al-Kubra, chapter on his miracles ﷺ in increasing food beyond what has already been mentioned, 2/85.)
2. He ﷺ gave seventy Companions to drink from one bowl of milk. (Bukhari, Book of Heart-Softening Matters, chapter on how the Prophet lived, 4/234, hadith 6452; Umdat al-Qari, Book of Heart-Softening Matters, chapter on how the Prophet lived, 15/536.)
3. He ﷺ caused springs of water to flow from his fingers and gave fourteen hundred, or even more, people to drink. (Bukhari, Book of Military Expeditions, chapter on the Battle of Hudaybiyyah, 3/69, hadith 4152–4153.)
4. He ﷺ granted many people healing through his blessed saliva. (Al-Khasa'is al-Kubra, chapter on his signs ﷺ in healing the sick, 2/115–118.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Enable us to walk the Straight Path.

blocks.text: {اِهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِیْمَ: Enable us to walk the Straight Path.} After mentioning knowledge of Allah Almighty's Essence and attributes, worshipping Him, and His being the true Helper, a supplication is taught here. blocks.text: Meaning of the Straight Path

runs.text: Meaning of the Straight Path

blocks.text: The Straight Path means the straight path of beliefs, upon which all the noble Prophets عَلَیْہِمُ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام walked. This is the path of Ahl al-Sunnah, because to this day the noble saints have belonged only to the Ahl al-Sunnah school. Allah Almighty has commanded us to follow their path and remain with them. He says:

blocks.text: Means of Gaining Guidance

runs.text: Means of Gaining Guidance

blocks.text: Remember that Allah Almighty has granted many means of gaining guidance. Some of them are:

runs.text: Remember that Allah Almighty has granted many means of gaining guidance. Some of them are:

blocks.text:
1. A person's outward and inward abilities, by using which he can gain guidance.
2. The signs in the heavens and the earth that indicate Allah Almighty's power and oneness, through reflecting upon which a person can gain guidance.
3. The Books sent down by Allah Almighty. Before the revelation of the Holy Quran, the Torah, Gospel, and Psalms were means of guidance for people; now the Holy Quran is the means by which people gain guidance.
4. The special servants sent by Allah Almighty, the noble Prophets and great Messengers عَلَیْہِمُ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام. They were means of guidance for their respective nations, while our Prophet Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ is a means of guidance for all people who will come until the Day of Judgement.

runs.text: Matters Learned from “صِرَاطَ الَّذِیْنَ اَنْعَمْتَ عَلَیْهِمْ”

blocks.text: Two matters are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Two matters are learned from this verse:

blocks.text:
1. Matters upon which the righteous elders have acted are included in the Straight Path.
2. Imam Fakhr al-Din al-Razi رَحْمَۃُاللہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ states: Some exegetes have said that mentioning “صِرَاطَ الَّذِیْنَ اَنْعَمْتَ عَلَیْهِمْ” after “اِهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِیْمَ” proves that a disciple can reach the stations of guidance and spiritual unveiling only when he follows a perfect spiritual guide who guides him towards the correct path and protects him from places of error and misguidance. Since deficiency dominates most people and their intellects are unable to understand truth and distinguish right from wrong, it is necessary to have a perfect person whom an imperfect person follows, until the light of the perfect person's intellect strengthens the imperfect person's intellect as well. In this way, he can reach the degrees of felicity and the heights of perfection. (Tafsir Kabir, Al-Fatihah, third section, 1/164.)

blocks.text: The Islamic Ruling Concerning “وَ لَا الضَّآلِّیْنَ”

runs.text: The Islamic Ruling Concerning “وَ لَا الضَّآلِّیْنَ”

blocks.text: Some people recite “وَلَا الضَّآلِّیْنَ” as “وَلَا الظَّآ لِّیْن”. This is forbidden. Imam Ahmad Raza Khan رَحْمَۃُاللہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ states: “ض، ظ، ذ، ز are all distinct and different letters, meaning letters separate from one another. Deliberately replacing one of them with another during Quranic recitation, whether in prayer or outside prayer, is categorically forbidden and a great sin; it is fabricating against Allah and altering the Noble Book.” (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 6/305.) For detailed information with proofs, study these treatises in volume six of Fatawa Razawiyyah: (1) “نِعْمَ الزَّادْ لِرَوْمِ الضَّادْ” (The best provision for pronouncing Dad); and (2) “اِلْجَامُ الصَّادْ عَنْ سُنَنِ الضَّادْ” (A discussion of the correct and incorrect ways of pronouncing Dad).

blocks.text: Islamic Rulings Concerning Ameen

runs.text: Islamic Rulings Concerning Ameen

blocks.text:
1. Ameen is not a word of the Holy Quran.
2. Whenever Surah Al-Fatihah is completed inside or outside prayer, saying Ameen afterwards is Sunnah.
3. According to the Hanafi school, Ameen is not said aloud in prayer; rather, it is said quietly.

blocks.text: {اَرَءَیْتَ الَّذِیْ یُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّیْنِ: Do you see the one who belies the religion?} Concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse, one opinion is that it was revealed about ‘As ibn Wa’il Sahmi, who denied the Day of Judgement and also used to commit evil deeds.

runs.text: {اَرَءَیْتَ الَّذِیْ یُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّیْنِ: Do you see the one who belies the religion?} Concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse, one opinion is that it was revealed about ‘As ibn Wa’il Sahmi, who denied the Day of Judgement and also used to commit evil deeds.

blocks.text: The second opinion is that this verse was revealed about Walid ibn Mughirah.

runs.text: The second opinion is that this verse was revealed about Walid ibn Mughirah.

blocks.text: The third opinion is that it was revealed about Abu Jahl. It is narrated that Abu Jahl had accepted responsibility for bringing up an orphan. One day, that orphan came to him unclothed and asked him for some of his property, but Abu Jahl pushed him out. The leaders of Quraysh told him, “Go to Muhammad (Mustafa) ﷺ; he will intercede for you.” Their purpose was to mock the Noble Prophet ﷺ, but the orphan did not know this. Thus, the orphan came to the court of the Crown of Messengership ﷺ and presented his complaint. The Leader of the Messengers ﷺ never sent a needy person away empty-handed, so he ﷺ went with the orphan to Abu Jahl.

runs.text: The third opinion is that it was revealed about Abu Jahl. It is narrated that Abu Jahl had accepted responsibility for bringing up an orphan. One day, that orphan came to him unclothed and asked him for some of his property, but Abu Jahl pushed him out. The leaders of Quraysh told him, “Go to Muhammad (Mustafa) ﷺ; he will intercede for you.” Their purpose was to mock the Noble Prophet ﷺ, but the orphan did not know this. Thus, the orphan came to the court of the Crown of Messengership ﷺ and presented his complaint. The Leader of the Messengers ﷺ never sent a needy person away empty-handed, so he ﷺ went with the orphan to Abu Jahl.

blocks.text: When Abu Jahl saw the Noble Messenger ﷺ, he welcomed him and immediately handed the orphan his property. When the people of Quraysh saw this, they reproached him and said, “You have abandoned your religion.” Abu Jahl replied, “By God, I have not abandoned my religion. The real matter is that I saw a spear to his right and left, and I feared that if I did not obey him, that spear would tear me apart.”

blocks.text: The fourth opinion is that this verse was not revealed about any particular person; rather, it includes every person who denies the Day of Judgement. The reason is that a person performs righteous deeds and refrains from forbidden things because of desire for reward and fear of punishment. When he denies the Day of Judgement itself, he will not give up any of his carnal desires and pleasures. This proves that denial of the Day of Judgement is like the foundation of disbelief and all types of sins.

blocks.text: The summary of this verse and the two verses after it is: O man! Do you recognise the person who denies reckoning and recompense despite the clear proofs? If you do not recognise him, then listen: he is the one who, because of his disbelief, pushes away, rebukes, and beats the orphan; while wronging him, he does not give him his right or his property. Because of his extreme miserliness, hardness of heart, and meanness, he does not feed the needy, nor does he encourage anyone else to feed the orphan, because he does not believe that this deed earns reward. If he believed in recompense and had conviction in the warning of punishment, these deeds would not proceed from him. (Tafsir Kabir, Al-Maun, under verses 1–3, 11/301–303; Khazin, Al-Maun, under verses 1–3, 4/412, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Arabic: فَوَیْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّیْنَۙ    (4)

runs.text: Arabic:

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: So, destruction is for those performers of Salah.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
So, destruction is for those performers of Salah.

blocks.text: {فَوَیْلٌ لِّلْمُصَلِّیْنَ: So, destruction is for those performers of Salah.} This verse and the verse after it state that destruction is for those performers of Salah who are heedless of their Salah. This refers to hypocrites: when they are alone, they do not offer Salah because they do not believe that it is obligatory; but when they are before people, they act like performers of Salah, present themselves as worshippers, and stand and sit for people to see them. In reality, these people are heedless of Salah. (Madarik, Al-Maun, under verses 4–5, p. 1377.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Irfan translation: “Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive Allah in their own supposition, and He will repay them for their deception. When they stand for Salah, they stand lazily, showing off before people, and they remember Allah only a little. They waver between the two; they are neither with these nor with those. And whoever Allah sends astray, you will never find a way for him.”

blocks.text: Remember that it is necessary to avoid being heedless of Salah in the sense of sometimes offering it and sometimes abandoning it; this is a particular quality of hypocrites. One should also strive to avoid heedlessness within Salah, such as beginning to think about other matters during Salah or accepting Satan’s whispers, although this form of heedlessness is less reprehensible.

blocks.text: {اَلَّذِیْنَ هُمْ عَنْ صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُوْنَ: Those who are heedless of their Salah.} Heedlessness of Salah has several forms, such as not offering it regularly, not offering it at the correct time, not properly performing the obligations and necessary acts, not offering it in congregation without a valid Shar‘i excuse, not caring about Salah, making it up in private and offering it before people, and so on. All these forms are included in the warning. Failing to offer it eagerly, not performing it with understanding, and not offering it attentively are also included in heedlessness of Salah; however, these forms are not included in the particular warning mentioned in the preceding verse.

blocks.text: The Definition and Condemnation of Showing Off

runs.text: The Definition and Condemnation of Showing Off

blocks.text: Showing off means displaying one’s deed with the intention that people will see it and praise one’s worship. (Qurtubi, Al-Maun, under verse 6, 10/154, twentieth part.)

runs.text: Showing off means displaying one’s deed with the intention that people will see it and praise one’s worship. (Qurtubi, Al-Maun, under verse 6, 10/154, twentieth part.)

blocks.text: Many hadith condemn showing off. Two of them are mentioned here.

runs.text: Many hadith condemn showing off. Two of them are mentioned here.

blocks.text: 1. Sayyiduna Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ states: We were discussing the Antichrist when the Noble Messenger ﷺ came and said, “Shall I not tell you of something which, in my view, is more feared for you than the Antichrist?” We said, “Yes, O Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” He ﷺ said, “It is hidden polytheism: a person stands to offer Salah and prolongs it because another person is watching him offer Salah.” (Ibn Majah, Book of Asceticism, chapter on showing off and seeking to be heard, 4/470, hadith 4204.)

It is narrated from Sayyiduna Abu Sa‘id ibn Abu Fadalah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “When Allah Almighty gathers all the earlier and later people on the Day concerning which there is no doubt, a caller will announce: ‘Whoever performed a deed for Allah عَزَّوَجَلَّ and associated someone else with Him in it should seek the reward of his deed from that associate, because Allah Almighty is completely independent of polytheism.’” (Tirmidhi, Book of Tafsir, chapter on Surah Al-Kahf, 5/105, hadith 3165.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And refuse to give (small) things of use when asked.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {وَ یَمْنَعُوْنَ الْمَاعُوْنَ: And refuse to give (small) things of use when asked.} The earlier verses described the hypocrites’ dealings with the Creator. From here, their conduct with creation is being described: if they are asked for an ordinary item used in daily life, such as a needle, cooking pot, or bowl, they refuse to give it out of miserliness. (Jalalayn, Al-Maun, under verse 7, p. 507.)

blocks.text: Sayyidatuna Aishah Siddiqah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا states: I asked, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which thing is it unlawful to withhold?” He ﷺ said, “Water, salt, and fire.” I asked, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we understand the ruling concerning water, but why is this ruling given for salt and fire?” He ﷺ said, “O Humayra رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا, whoever gives someone fire has, as if, given in charity all the food cooked with that fire; whoever gives someone salt has, as if, given in charity all the food made tasty by that salt; whoever gives a Muslim one sip of water where water is readily available has, as if, freed a slave; and whoever gives a Muslim one sip of water where water is unavailable has, as if, given him life.” (Ibn Majah, Book of Pawning, chapter on Muslims sharing three things, 3/177, hadith 2474.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Did We not expand your chest for you (O Beloved)?

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
Did We not expand your chest for you (O Beloved)?

blocks.text: {اَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ: Did We not expand your chest for you (O Beloved)?} The occasion of revelation of this Surah is that one day the Master of the universe ﷺ presented his plea in the Divine court: “O Allah Almighty! You granted Sayyiduna Ibrahim عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام the honour of being Your intimate friend, honoured Sayyiduna Musa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام by speaking with him, granted Sayyiduna Idris عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام access to a lofty place up to Paradise, made the mountains and iron obedient to Sayyiduna Dawud عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام, and made jinn, humans, and all animals subject to Sayyiduna Sulayman عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام. With which honour and miracle have You distinguished me?” Thereupon this Surah was revealed. It was as though it declared: “O Beloved ﷺ! If We made Sayyiduna Ibrahim عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام Our intimate friend, then for your sake We opened your chest with the light of knowledge, wisdom, and gnosis, so that the delight of supplication, concern for the Ummah, eagerness to attend Our court, and longing for the abode of the Hereafter might enter your heart; bearing the heavenly revelation might become easy for your heart; and you might endure the hardships that come in conveying the invitation towards Allah Almighty. Through these qualities and miracles, you attained such a rank that the honour of Sayyiduna Ibrahim عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام being Our intimate friend has no comparison with it. If We granted Sayyiduna Musa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام the honour of speaking with Us and granted Sayyiduna Idris عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام access to a lofty place, then We freed you from the grief that had weighed heavily upon your back and called you to the realm beyond place, honouring you with Our vision, until the distance between Us and you became equal to two bows, or even less, in a manner befitting Us, and your nearness and rank became renowned throughout the entire dominion of the heavens. If We gave Sayyiduna Dawud and Sayyiduna Sulayman عَلَیْہِمَا الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام authority over some things of the world, then We gave you power over the upper world, meaning the heavens: their angels attend your court like servants and fight your enemies like your soldiers, and there is nothing in the heavens that is unaware of your prophethood and messengership or that disobeys your command.” (Ruh al-Bayan, Al-Inshirah, under verse 1, 10/465; Al-Kalam al-Awdah fi Tafsir Al-Inshirah, p. 14, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Mufti Na'im al-Din Muradabadi رَحْمَۃُ اللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ writes in the commentary of this verse: “That is, O Beloved ﷺ! We expanded and enlarged your sacred chest for guidance, gnosis, admonition, prophethood, and knowledge and wisdom, to such an extent that the unseen world and the witnessed world were contained within its breadth, bodily relationships could not obstruct spiritual lights, and divinely bestowed sciences, Divine commands, Lordly gnoses, and Merciful realities became manifest in your pure chest. Some exegetes say that the outward opening of the blessed chest is intended by this verse. It is mentioned in hadith that the outward opening of the Noble Prophet’s ﷺ blessed chest occurred several times: at the beginning of his blessed life, at the beginning of the descent of revelation, and on the Night of Ascension. Its manner was that Sayyiduna Jibril Amin عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام split open the pure chest, took out the blessed heart, washed it with Zamzam water in a golden basin, filled it with light and wisdom, and placed it back in its position.” (Khazain al-Irfan, Al-Inshirah, under verse 1, p. 1110; Khazin, Al-Inshirah, under verse 1, 4/388; Ruh al-Bayan, Al-Inshirah, under verse 1, 10/461–462, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Irfan translation: “And whoever Allah wants to guide, He opens his chest for Islam; and whoever He wants to send astray, He makes his chest tight, extremely tight, as though he is climbing into the sky by force.”

blocks.text: Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Masud رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ states that when the Crown of Messengership ﷺ recited this verse, the noble Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ asked what was meant by this opening. He ﷺ said: “It means the light placed into the believer’s heart, through which his heart opens.” He ﷺ was asked whether there was a sign by which it could be recognised. He ﷺ replied: “Yes. There are three signs: (1) eagerness for the Hereafter, (2) aversion to the world, and (3) preparing for the Hereafter before death.” (Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah, Book of Asceticism, what is mentioned from our Prophet ﷺ concerning asceticism, 8/126, hadith 14.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And (We) removed that burden from you (O Beloved).

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
And (We) removed that burden from you (O Beloved).

blocks.text: {وَ وَضَعْنَا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ: And (We) removed that burden from you (O Beloved).} Regarding what is meant by this burden, one statement of the exegetes is that it refers to the grief which the Illuminated Presence ﷺ felt because the disbelievers did not accept faith. A second statement is that it refers to the grief over the sins of the Ummah, with which his blessed heart remained occupied. The meaning is: “O Beloved ﷺ! We made you one whose intercession is accepted and thereby removed the burden of grief that had broken your back.” (Tafsir Kabir, Al-Inshirah, under verses 2–3, 11/207–208; Khazin, Al-Inshirah, under verses 2–3, 4/388–389; Khazain al-Irfan, Al-Inshirah, under verse 3, p. 1110, excerpted.)

blocks.text: The Noble Prophet ﷺ began to weep. Raising his blessed hands, he supplicated: “O Allah Almighty! My Ummah, my Ummah.” Allah Almighty said to Sayyiduna Jibril: “O Jibril! Go to My Beloved ﷺ. Your Lord knows best, but ask him what is making him weep.” Sayyiduna Jibril عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام came to the court of the Noble Prophet ﷺ and asked him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed him of his plea. Allah Almighty then said to Sayyiduna Jibril: “Go to My Beloved ﷺ and tell him: ‘We shall certainly please you concerning your Ummah and shall not grieve you.’” (Muslim, Book of Faith, chapter on the Prophet’s ﷺ supplication for his Ummah, etc., p. 130, hadith 346 (202).)

blocks.text: Imam Ahmad Raza Khan رَحْمَۃُ اللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ states: “O dear brother! Have you ever heard that one who has sincere love for you becomes displeased on hearing your good condition, remains concerned with erasing it, and then what a Beloved he is: the life of faith and mine of excellence, whose world-adorning beauty has no equal anywhere, and upon whose image the pen of destiny drew its final stroke, never to write such a one again? What a Beloved he is, whom his Master sent as mercy for all the worlds; what a Beloved he is, who bore upon his person the burden of an entire world; what a Beloved he is, who abandoned the food of the day and sleep of the night because of your grief, while you remain immersed day and night in disobedience and occupied in amusement and play, and he remains weeping and sorrowful night and day for your forgiveness.”

blocks.text: “The night, which Allah جل جلاله made for comfort, has spread its wings of tranquillity. Morning is near, cool breezes are fanning the air, everyone’s work inclines towards rest, kings sleep in blissful comfort in warm beds and soft pillows, and even the needy and destitute have stretched their feet beneath a two-yard blanket. At such a pleasant time and in such cool weather, that innocent, sinless, pure and protected one leaves his comfort, turns away from sleep and rest, and places his humble forehead at the threshold of honour, saying: ‘O Lord! My Ummah is sinful; pardon them and save all their bodies from the Fire of Hell.’”

blocks.text: “When that source of comfort and mine of mercy came into existence, he prostrated in the Divine court and said, ‘My Lord, grant me my Ummah.’ When he was placed in the noble grave, his life-giving lips were moving; some Companions listened and heard him softly saying, ‘My Ummah, my Ummah.’ On the Day of Judgement, a day of astonishing severity, with a copper earth, bare feet, tongues parched with thirst, the sun above heads and no sign of shade, the anxiety of reckoning and the encounter with the Sovereign, the entire world will be occupied with its own concern, and helpless criminals will be caught in the snare of calamity. Wherever they go, they will hear no answer except ‘Myself, myself; go to someone else.’ At that time this Beloved, the comforter of the sorrowful, will be of help. The lock of intercession will open through the strength of his blessed arm. They will remove the turban from his sacred head, and he will fall in prostration and say, ‘O my Lord, my Ummah.’” (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 30/716–717.)

blocks.text: “Trees and stones, deer and monitor lizards, other living creatures, suckling children, and the idols worshipped by disbelievers will recite your proclamation of messengership with eloquent speech and sound expression, just as they will declare Our Oneness. Throughout the four corners of the world there will be a clamour of ‘لَآ اِلٰـہَ اِلَّا اللّٰہُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَّسُوْلُ اللّٰہ’. Every particle, except the wretched ones of eternity, will recite the testimony of faith. I will occupy the inhabitants of the Highest Assembly with glorifying and sanctifying Me, and I will command your praiseworthy and blessed salutations. Wherever I write ‘Allah’, upon the Throne, the Chair, the seven leaves of Sidrah, and the palaces of Paradise, I will also write ‘مُحَمَّدٌ رَّسُوْلُ اللّٰہ’. I will command My Prophets and the Messengers of firm resolve to fill their breaths with you at all times, to bring light to their eyes, coolness to their hearts, tranquillity to their hearts, and adornment to their gatherings through your remembrance. In every Book I send down, I will describe your praise, your beauty, and the perfection of your character with such explanation that the hearts of those who hear will incline towards you involuntarily, and the unseen candle of your love will blaze in their ears and breasts. If an entire world becomes your enemy and occupies itself with diminishing your rank and erasing your virtues, I am the All-Powerful; what power can anyone have against Me? The effect of this very promise was that the Jews had for hundreds of years removed your mention from their books and thrown dust upon the moon, while the people of faith recited your praise in such a loud voice that a fair-minded listener would call out spontaneously. Millions of irreligious people girded themselves to erase your virtues, but those who sought to erase them were themselves erased, while your excellence continued to advance day by day.” (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 30/718–719.)

If an entire world becomes your enemy and occupies itself with diminishing your rank and erasing your virtues, I am the All-Powerful; what power can anyone have against Me? The effect of this very promise was that the Jews had for hundreds of years removed your mention from their books and thrown dust upon the moon, while the people of faith recited your praise in such a loud voice that a fair-minded listener would call out spontaneously. Millions of irreligious people girded themselves to erase your virtues, but those who sought to erase them were themselves erased, while your excellence continued to advance day by day.” (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 30/718–719.)
