blocks.text: {فَاِذَا فَرَغْتَ فَانْصَبْ: So, when you complete Salah, strive in supplication.} One commentary of this verse is: “O Beloved ﷺ! When you complete Salah, strive in supplication for the Hereafter, because supplication after Salah is accepted.” There is disagreement concerning the supplication mentioned here. Some exegetes say it refers to the supplication made within Salah at its end, while others say it refers to the supplication made after saying salam. A second commentary is: “O Beloved ﷺ! When you complete inviting creation towards religion, occupy yourself with worshipping your Lord Almighty.” (Madarik, Al-Inshirah, under verse 7, p. 1359, abridged.)

blocks.text: 3. Preachers, exhorters, and propagators who address the public in gatherings and meetings until late at night should also strive to worship Allah Almighty after completing this work. Sadly, in the present age there are many such people who remain extremely energetic in delivering their speeches and lectures in gatherings until midnight or even later; their speeches display enthusiasm and fervour, and they recite with tears the verses and hadith concerning the punishments for leaving the congregation, missing Salah, or not offering it at all. blocks.text: {وَالتِّیْنِ وَالزَّیْتُوْنِ: By the oath of the fig and the olive.} In this verse, Allah Almighty has sworn by the fig and the olive because these things contain benefits and advantages that point to the power of their Creator, the Lord Almighty. The fig is an extremely excellent fruit. It has no waste, is digested very quickly, is highly beneficial, removes constipation, expels sand and stones from the bladder, dissolves the knots of harmful matter trapped in the liver and spleen, makes the body stout, and clears phlegm. The olive, meanwhile, is a blessed tree. Its oil is used for lighting and is also eaten like a curry; no other oil possesses this quality. Its tree grows on dry mountains in which there is no trace of moisture, flourishes without cultivation, and remains for thousands of years. (Khazin, At-Tin, under verse 1, 4/390; Ruh al-Bayan, At-Tin, under verse 1, 10/466–467, excerpted.)

Its tree grows on dry mountains in which there is no trace of moisture, flourishes without cultivation, and remains for thousands of years. (Khazin, At-Tin, under verse 1, 4/390; Ruh al-Bayan, At-Tin, under verse 1, 10/466–467, excerpted.)

blocks.text: {وَطُوْرِ سِیْنِیْنَ: And by Mount Sinai.} Tur is the mountain upon which Allah Almighty honoured Sayyiduna Musa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام by speaking with him, and Sina is the name of the place where this mountain is situated. This place is called Sina because it is beautiful or blessed. According to some exegetes, Tur Sina means a beautiful or blessed mountain. According to others, every mountain where fruit-bearing trees are abundant is called Tur Sina. (Tafsir Kabir, At-Tin, under verse 2, 11/211–212.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: We then turned him towards the lowest of the low state (i.e. old age).

blocks.text: {ثُمَّ رَدَدْنٰهُ اَسْفَلَ سٰفِلِیْنَ: We then turned him towards the lowest of the low state.} One meaning is that after creating man in the best form, Allah Almighty turns him towards old age. At that time the body becomes weak, the limbs become ineffective, the intellect becomes deficient, the back bends, the hair turns white, wrinkles appear in the skin, and he becomes dependent in fulfilling his needs. A second meaning is that when he did not give thanks for his excellent form, persisted in disobeying Allah Almighty, and did not believe, his end was that the lowest depths of Hell were made his dwelling. (Khazin, At-Tin, under verse 5, 4/391; Madarik, At-Tin, under verse 5, pp. 1360–1361, excerpted.)

If you have any doubt about being raised on the Day of Judgement, then reflect that We created you from dust, then from a drop of water, then from a clot of blood, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed, so that We may manifest Our power to you. We keep in the wombs whatever We wish for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, then (grant you life) so that you may reach your full strength. Among you are those who are called back, and among you are those who are returned to the most worthless age, so that after having knowledge they know nothing.”

blocks.text: {اِلَّا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْا: Except those who believed.} That is, those who believed and performed good deeds shall have limitless reward. Even if, because of the weakness of old age, they cannot perform as many acts of worship as they did in youth, and their deeds decrease, by the grace of Allah Almighty they will receive the same reward that they received for deeds performed during youth and strength, and the same number of deeds will be recorded for them as were recorded in their youth. The lowest depths of Hell will not be their dwelling. (Khazin, At-Tin, under verse 6, 4/391; Madarik, At-Tin, under verse 6, p. 1361, excerpted.)

runs.text: {اِلَّا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْا: Except those who believed.} That is, those who believed and performed good deeds shall have limitless reward. Even if, because of the weakness of old age, they cannot perform as many acts of worship as they did in youth, and their deeds decrease, by the grace of Allah Almighty they will receive the same reward that they received for deeds performed during youth and strength, and the same number of deeds will be recorded for them as were recorded in their youth. The lowest depths of Hell will not be their dwelling. (Khazin, At-Tin, under verse 6, 4/391; Madarik, At-Tin, under verse 6, p. 1361, excerpted.)

blocks.text: A similar matter is also mentioned in a noble hadith. Sayyiduna Abu Musa al-Ash'ari رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “When a Muslim servant becomes ill or is travelling, the reward of the deeds that he used to perform while healthy and resident is written for him, though he could not perform them because of illness or travel.” (Musnad Imam Ahmad, Musnad of the Kufans, hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, 7/177, hadith 19774.)

blocks.text: Two matters are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Two matters are learned from this verse:

blocks.text: 1. Faith precedes deeds, and no good deed is valid without faith.

items.text: Faith precedes deeds, and no good deed is valid without faith.

runs.text: Faith precedes deeds, and no good deed is valid without faith.

blocks.text: 2. Being granted a long life and having righteous deeds are great blessings. Sayyiduna Abu Bakrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ states: “A desert Arab asked in the court of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, ‘O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who is the best among people?’ He said: ‘The best person is the one whose life is long and whose deeds are righteous.’ He asked, ‘Who is the worst among people?’ He said: ‘The worst person is the one whose life is long and whose deeds are evil.’” (Tirmidhi, Book of Asceticism, chapter 22, 4/148, hadith 2337.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Now (after all these proofs), what causes you to belie the Judgement (Day)?

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {فَمَا یُكَذِّبُكَ بَعْدُ بِالدِّیْنِ: Now (after all these proofs), what causes you to belie the Judgement (Day)?} That is, O disbelieving man! Have you not reflected upon your form, the beginning of your creation, your youth, and your old age, so that you would say that the Being capable of these things is also capable of bringing me back to life after my passing, taking account of my deeds, and recompensing me for them? After this decisive proof and clear argument, what causes you to belie the Day of Judgement, and why do you deny being raised after passing, reckoning on the Day of Judgement, and recompense for deeds despite seeing these powers of Allah Almighty? (Khazin, At-Tin, under verse 7, 4/391, abridged.)

blocks.text: {اَلَیْسَ اللّٰهُ بِاَحْكَمِ الْحٰكِمِیْنَ: Is Allah not the Greatest Ruler of all rulers?} It is narrated from Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ that the Illuminated Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever recites ‘اَلَیْسَ اللّٰهُ بِاَحْكَمِ الْحٰكِمِیْنَ’ while reciting the Surah ‘وَالتِّیْنِ وَالزَّیْتُوْنِ’ should say: ‘بَلٰی وَاَنَا عَلٰی ذَالِکَ مِنَ الشَّاہِدِیْن’, meaning, ‘Why not? Indeed, He is, and I am among those who bear witness to this.’” (Tirmidhi, Book of Tafsir, chapter on Surah At-Tin, 5/230, hadith 3358.)

blocks.text: {لَمْ یَكُنِ الَّذِیْنَ كَفَرُوْا مِنْ اَهْلِ الْكِتٰبِ وَ الْمُشْرِكِیْنَ مُنْفَكِّیْنَ: The disbelieving People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to leave their religion.} That is, the disbelieving People of the Book, the Jews and Christians, and the polytheists, the idol-worshippers, were not going to leave their religions until the Leader of the Messengers, Sayyiduna Muhammad ﷺ, appeared before them. This was because, before the arrival of the Holy Prophet ﷺ, all these people used to say, “We will not leave our religion until that Prophet appears whose mention is found in the Torah and the Gospel.” When that Prophet appeared and announced his prophethood, some of them believed in him and some disbelieved in him. (Khazin, Al-Bayyinah, under verse 1, 4/398; Sawi, Al-Bayyinah, under verse 1, 6/2403–2404, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Three matters are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Three matters are learned from this verse:

blocks.text: 1. Although the People of the Book and the polytheists are all disbelievers, the rulings concerning the People of the Book are lenient because they have an association with a Prophet and a Book. If they accept faith, they receive double reward. If association with a Book and a Prophet benefits disbelievers so greatly, then what will be the state of the believer who gains a special association with the Illuminated Prophet ﷺ and the Quran?

runs.text: {رَسُوْلٌ مِّنَ اللّٰهِ: (That clear proof is) the Messenger of Allah.} That is, the clear proof is the most magnificent Messenger of Allah Almighty, who recites the Holy Quran, the pure Book that encompasses the subjects of all the Scriptures. blocks.text: The Holy Quran is pure in every respect: it came from a pure place through pure angels to a pure Prophet; it has always remained, and will always remain, in pure tongues, pure breasts, and pure hands; and it is protected from mixture and alteration. It should also be remembered that the recitation of the Noble Prophet ﷺ is a miracle, because he ﷺ recited and taught the Quran, and understood and explained it, without learning it from anyone among creation. Our recitation is not a miracle, because we learn the recitation and pronunciation of the Holy Quran, as well as its rulings and secrets, from a memoriser, reciter, scholar, and others.

blocks.text: {وَمَا تَفَرَّقَ الَّذِیْنَ اُوْتُوا الْكِتٰبَ: And the People of the Book did not dispute.} The meaning of this verse is that, before this, all of them agreed that when the Prophet whose glad tidings had been given appeared, they would believe in him. runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

And those people (i.e of the Book) were ordered to worship Allah only, believing solely in Him, being on one side purely (i.e. towards Islam only), and to establish Salah, and to pay Zakah, and this is the straight religion.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Indeed, those who believed and did good deeds; it is they who are the best of the entire creation.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
Indeed, those who believed and did good deeds; it is they who are the best of the entire creation.

blocks.text: {اُولٰٓىٕكَ هُمْ خَیْرُ الْبَرِیَّةِ: It is they who are the best of the entire creation.} This verse shows that those who believe and perform righteous deeds are superior even to the angels, because the angels are also included among all creation. There is, however, detail in this matter: among human beings, those who were granted the rank of prophethood and messengership are superior to all angels. Among the angels, those who are messengers are superior to saints and scholars, while saints and scholars are superior to ordinary angels. Ordinary angels are superior to sinful believers because angels are protected from sins. (Ruh al-Bayan, Al-Bayyinah, under verse 7, 10/490; Sharh Fiqh Akbar, p. 118, excerpted.)

blocks.text: {جَزَآؤُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ: Their reward with their Lord.} That is, the reward of those who believe and perform good deeds is Gardens of eternal dwelling with their Lord Almighty, beneath which streams flow. blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: When the earth is shaken violently with its destined tremor.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {اِذَا زُلْزِلَتِ الْاَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا: When the earth is shaken violently with its destined tremor.} Allah Almighty states that when the earth is shaken with its earthquake, no tree, building, or mountain will remain upon it. blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And (when) the earth casts out (all of) its burdens.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
And (when) the earth casts out (all of) its burdens.

blocks.text: {وَ اَخْرَجَتِ الْاَرْضُ اَثْقَالَهَا: And (when) the earth casts out (all of) its burdens.} That is, when the earth will cast out all the treasures and the dead present within it. It should be remembered that human beings and jinn are weight-bearing beings. As long as they are upon the earth, they are a burden upon it, and when they are inside the earth, they are a burden for it. For this reason, human beings and jinn are called ثَقَلَین, because whether they are dead or alive, the earth carries their burden. (Madarik, Az-Zilzal, under verse 2, p. 1368; Khazin, Az-Zilzal, under verse 2, 4/400–401, excerpted.)

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Irfan translation: “And when the earth is stretched out, and it casts out whatever is in it and becomes empty, and it listens to the command of its Lord, and it is worthy of that. O man! Indeed, you are striving towards your Lord with great effort, then you will meet Him.”

blocks.text: Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The earth will disgorge its pieces of the heart like pillars of gold and silver. The murderer will see them and say, ‘It was because of this wealth that I killed.’ The one who severed family ties will say, ‘It was because of this that I severed family ties.’ The thief will see it and say, ‘It was because of this wealth that my hand was cut off.’ Then everyone will leave that wealth, and no one will take anything from it.” (Muslim, Book of Zakah, chapter on encouraging charity before there is no one to accept it, p. 505, hadith 62 [1013].)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: On that Day, the earth will narrate (all) its news.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {یَوْمَىٕذٍ تُحَدِّثُ اَخْبَارَهَا: On that Day, the earth will narrate (all) its news.} The summary of this verse and the following verse is that when these matters occur, the earth will, by the command of Allah Almighty, tell creation its news on that Day and will describe every good and evil deed performed upon it. The purpose of this will be that the earth may complain about the disobedient and thank the obedient. Thus, it will say: “So-and-so performed prayer upon me; so-and-so paid Zakah; so-and-so fasted; and so-and-so performed Hajj. Whereas so-and-so disbelieved, so-and-so committed adultery, so-and-so stole, and so-and-so committed oppression.” Indeed, upon hearing this, the disbeliever will wish that he had been thrown into Hell. (Khazin, Az-Zilzal, under verses 4–5, 4/401; Tafsir Kabir, Az-Zilzal, under verse 4, 11/255, excerpted.)

blocks.text: The earth is a witness to our deeds

runs.text: The earth is a witness to our deeds

blocks.text: It is learned from this that the earth is a witness to our deeds, and on the Day of Judgement it will describe our deeds before us. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ states that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse, “یَوْمَىٕذٍ تُحَدِّثُ اَخْبَارَهَا”, and then said: “Do you know what its news is?” The Noble Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ submitted: “Allah Almighty and His Messenger ﷺ know best.” The Holy Prophet ﷺ said: “Its news is that it will testify concerning the deeds that every man and woman performed upon its back. It will say: ‘This person performed this deed on such-and-such day, and that person performed that deed on such-and-such day.’ This is its news.” (Tirmidhi, Book of the Description of the Day of Judgement, Softening of Hearts and Piety, chapter 7, 4/194, hadith 2437.)

blocks.text: Therefore, every person should be cautious of the earth when committing a sin. It is narrated from Sayyiduna Rabi'ah Jurashi رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Be cautious of the earth, for it is your origin. Whoever performs a good or bad deed upon it, it will report it.” (Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, chapter on the letter Ra, Rabi'ah ibn al-Ghaz al-Jurashi … etc., 5/65, hadith 4596.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: On that Day, people will return towards their Lord, in different paths, in order to be shown their deeds.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
On that Day, people will return towards their Lord, in different paths, in order to be shown their deeds.

blocks.text: {یَوْمَىٕذٍ یَّصْدُرُ النَّاسُ اَشْتَاتًا: On that Day, people will return in different groups.} One meaning of this verse is that on the Day of Judgement, after appearing at the place of reckoning, people will return from there by different routes. Some will go through the right side towards Paradise, while others will go through the left side towards Hell, so that they may be shown the recompense for their deeds. A second meaning is that on the day when the matters mentioned earlier occur, people will return from their graves towards the place of reckoning in different conditions. Some will have white faces and some will have black faces; some will be riding, while others will walk bound in chains and fetters; some will be in a state of safety, while others will be terrified, so that they may be shown their deeds. (Khazin, Az-Zilzal, under verse 6, 4/401; Ruh al-Bayan, Az-Zilzal, under verse 6, 10/493, excerpted.)

فَمَنْ یَّعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَیْرًا یَّرَهٗﭤ(7)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: So, whosoever does a good deed equal to the weight of an atom, (he) shall see it.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
So, whosoever does a good deed equal to the weight of an atom, (he) shall see it.

blocks.text: {وَ مَنْ یَّعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا یَّرَهٗ: And whoever does an evil deed equal to the weight of an atom, (he) shall see it.} Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Abbas رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا states that every believer and disbeliever will be shown his good and evil deeds on the Day of Judgement. The believer will be shown his good deeds and evil deeds; Allah Almighty will forgive his evil deeds and grant him reward for his good deeds. The good deeds of the disbeliever will be rejected because they will have been destroyed on account of his disbelief, and he will be punished for his evil deeds.

The good deeds of the disbeliever will be rejected because they will have been destroyed on account of his disbelief, and he will be punished for his evil deeds.

blocks.text: Sayyiduna Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ states that if a disbeliever performed even an atom's weight of good, he would see its recompense in this world, until, when he leaves the world, he has no good deed remaining. A believer will receive the punishment for his evil deeds in this world, so that no evil deed will remain with him in the Hereafter. Some exegetes have said that the preceding verse concerns believers, while this verse concerns disbelievers. (Khazin, Az-Zilzal, under verse 8, 4/401; Madarik, Az-Zilzal, under verse 8, p. 1368, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Even a little good is beneficial, and even a small sin is a burden

runs.text: Even a little good is beneficial, and even a small sin is a burden

blocks.text: It is learned from this verse that even a little good is beneficial, and even a small sin is a burden. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A servant sometimes says a word that pleases Allah Almighty, without paying attention to it”—that is, some words seem extremely insignificant to a person—“and Allah Almighty raises him many degrees because of it. And sometimes a person says a word that angers Allah Almighty, without considering it, and because of it he falls into Hell.” (Bukhari, Book of Softening of Hearts, chapter on guarding the tongue, 4/241, hadith 6478.)

runs.text: It is learned from this that greed for abundant wealth, and displaying pride in it and in one's children, is blameworthy. When a person becomes involved in this, he is deprived of the blessings of the Hereafter. Allah Almighty states:

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Irfan translation: Know that the life of this world is only play, amusement, adornment, boasting among yourselves, and seeking to surpass one another in wealth and children. It is like rain whose vegetation pleases the farmers; then that vegetation dries, and you see it yellow; then it becomes crushed and useless. And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness and pleasure from Allah. And the life of this world is only the provision of deception.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Irfan translation: O believers! Indeed, among your wives and children there are some who are your enemies, so beware of them. And if you pardon, overlook, and forgive, then indeed Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful. Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and with Allah is a great reward. So fear Allah as much as you are able, listen, obey, and spend in the way of Allah; this is better for your souls. And whoever is protected from the greed of his own soul, it is they who are successful.

The Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “The son of Adam says, ‘My wealth, my wealth.’ O son of Adam! Your wealth is only what you have eaten and consumed, what you have worn and worn out, or what you have given in charity and sent ahead.” (Muslim, Book of Asceticism and Heart-Softening Matters, p. 1582, hadith 3 [2958].)

blocks.text: The reality of wealth and children

runs.text: The reality of wealth and children

blocks.text: Remember that the wealth whose increase people desire, and the children about whom they display pride and arrogance, remain with a person only as long as the soul remains in his body. As soon as the soul separates from his body and he is buried in the grave, that wealth and those children leave him. Only his deeds go with him into the grave. Therefore, instead of striving to increase wealth and boasting about one's children, every intelligent person should strive to increase righteous deeds, so that they may be his best companions in the grave.

His family, wealth, and deeds accompany him. His family and wealth return, while his deeds remain with him.” (Bukhari, Book of Heart-Softening Matters, chapter on the agonies of death, 4/250, hadith 6514.)

blocks.text: Sayyidatuna Aishah Siddiqah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا says that one day the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked the Noble Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ: “Do you know what the example of you, your family, your wealth, and your deeds is?” The Noble Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ submitted: “Allah Almighty and His Messenger ﷺ know best.” He ﷺ said: “The example of you, your family, your wealth, and your deeds is like that of a man who has three brothers. When the time of his death draws near, he calls all three brothers and says to one of them, ‘You see my condition; tell me, what can you do for me?’ He replies, ‘I can care for you now, remain with you, fulfil your needs and necessities, and then, when you pass away, wash you, shroud you, and carry your funeral with the people, sometimes carrying one side and sometimes letting another person carry it. When I return after burying you, I will mention your good qualities to anyone who asks about you.’ This brother is in fact the man's family. After saying this, the Radiant Prophet ﷺ asked the Noble Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ, ‘What do you think of this?’ They submitted, ‘We find no good in it.’

blocks.text: {كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُوْنَ: Yes, certainly! You will soon come to know.} The summary of this verse and the five verses after it is: O people! Yes, certainly, at the time of the agony of death you will soon learn the evil result of greed for abundant wealth and pride and arrogance regarding children. Then, certainly, you will soon learn it in the graves. Indeed, if you knew the consequence of greed for wealth with certain knowledge, you would not become involved in greed for wealth and thereby become neglectful of the Hereafter. Certainly, after your passing away you will surely see Hell; then you will surely see it with the sight of certainty. Then, on the Day of Judgement, you will surely be questioned about the blessings Allah Almighty granted you, such as health, leisure, security, comfort, and wealth, through which you enjoyed pleasures in the world. You will be asked: For what purpose did you spend these things? How did you show gratitude for them? And you will be punished for abandoning gratitude for these blessings. (Khazin, At-Takathur, under verses 3–8, 4/404; Madarik, At-Takathur, under verses 3–8, p. 1371; Jalalayn, At-Takathur, under verses 3–8, p. 506, excerpted.)

Yes, certainly, at the time of the agony of death you will soon learn the evil result of greed for abundant wealth and pride and arrogance regarding children. Then, certainly, you will soon learn it in the graves. Indeed, if you knew the consequence of greed for wealth with certain knowledge, you would not become involved in greed for wealth and thereby become neglectful of the Hereafter. Certainly, after your passing away you will surely see Hell; then you will surely see it with the sight of certainty. Then, on the Day of Judgement, you will surely be questioned about the blessings Allah Almighty granted you, such as health, leisure, security, comfort, and wealth, through which you enjoyed pleasures in the world. You will be asked: For what purpose did you spend these things? How did you show gratitude for them? And you will be punished for abandoning gratitude for these blessings. (Khazin, At-Takathur, under verses 3–8, 4/404; Madarik, At-Takathur, under verses 3–8, p. 1371; Jalalayn, At-Takathur, under verses 3–8, p. 506, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Reprehensible Forms of Accumulating and Repeatedly Counting Wealth

runs.text: Reprehensible Forms of Accumulating and Repeatedly Counting Wealth

blocks.text: Remember that accumulating wealth and repeatedly counting it is bad in several circumstances:

runs.text: Remember that accumulating wealth and repeatedly counting it is bad in several circumstances:

blocks.text:
1. Wealth is accumulated through unlawful means.
2. The religious rights due from the accumulated wealth are not fulfilled.
3. A person becomes so occupied with accumulating wealth that he forgets Allah Almighty.
4. Instead of relying upon Allah Almighty, a person regards wealth alone as the means of removing afflictions.

blocks.text: {یَحْسَبُ اَنَّ مَالَهٗۤ اَخْلَدَهٗ: Does he think that his wealth will keep him on earth forever?} The summary of this verse and the six verses after it is that the person who finds fault with people to their faces, speaks ill of them behind their backs, accumulates wealth and repeatedly counts it thinks that his wealth will keep him in this world forever and will not let him pass away. Because of this, he is intoxicated with love for wealth and does not turn towards righteous deeds. This can never be so. Rather, he will certainly be thrown into the crushing compartment of Hell, where the Fire will break his bones and ribs. And what do you know what the crushing one is? It is the Fire kindled by Allah, which will never become cold. Its nature is that it will burn the outer parts of the body, reach into the inside of the body, and burn the hearts as well. Indeed, after they are cast into the Fire, its doors will be closed, and the doors will be reinforced with fiery iron pillars so that they never open. Some exegetes have explained this to mean that, after the doors are closed, their hands and feet will be bound with fiery pillars. (Khazin, Al-Humazah, under verses 3–9, 4/406, excerpted.)

blocks.text: The Fire of Hell Is Not Like Other Fires

runs.text: The Fire of Hell Is Not Like Other Fires

blocks.text: It is learned from verse 6 of Surah Al-Humazah that the Fire of Hell is not like other fires. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “The Fire of Hell was kindled for a thousand years until it became red. Then it was kindled for another thousand years until it became white. Then it was kindled for another thousand years until it became black. Thus, it is now black and dark.” (Tirmidhi, Book of the Description of Hell, chapter 8, 4/266, hadith 2600.)

blocks.text: {اَلَّتِیْ تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْاَفْـٕدَةِ: Which will climb on to the hearts.} Hearts are such things that cannot bear even a little heat. So when the Fire of Hell climbs upon them and there is no death, what will their condition be at that time? The hearts are burned because they are the places of disbelief, false beliefs and corrupt intentions. (Khazin, Al-Humazah, under verse 7, 4/406–407; Madarik, Al-Humazah, under verse 7, p. 1373, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Three Types of Glorification

runs.text: Three Types of Glorification

blocks.text: Glorification is of three kinds:

runs.text: Glorification is of three kinds:

blocks.text:
1. The glorification of creation. Every thing's very being and its creation point to the power and wisdom of the Creator, the Omnipotent Lord, to His Oneness, and to His being pure from every defect and shortcoming.
2. The glorification of knowledge. Allah Almighty, through His kindness and grace, places knowledge of Himself in creation, and creation declares Him pure.
3. Essential glorification. Allah Almighty causes every substance to glorify Him, and every substance glorifies Him even without knowledge of Him. (Madarik, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 1, p. 1239, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: It is He Who has sent in the unlettered people a (great) Messenger from amongst themselves who recites His verses to them and purifies them, and gives them the knowledge of the Book and wisdom. runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

It is He Who has sent in the unlettered people a (great) Messenger from amongst themselves who recites His verses to them and purifies them, and gives them the knowledge of the Book and wisdom. And indeed, before this, they were definitely in open error.

blocks.text: {هُوَ الَّذِیْ بَعَثَ فِی الْاُمِّیّٖنَ رَسُوْلًا مِّنْهُمْ: It is He Who sent a Messenger from among the unlettered people.} Allah Almighty sent among the unlettered people a Messenger from among them, whose noble lineage and distinction they knew well. His blessed name is Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ. He recites before them the verses of the Holy Quran, which explain prophethood, the lawful and unlawful, and truth and falsehood. He purifies them from false beliefs, blameworthy morals, the impurities of the Age of Ignorance and evil deeds, and gives them knowledge of the Book and wisdom, that is, the Quran, Sunnah and jurisprudence; the commands of the Sacred Law and the secrets of the spiritual path. Indeed, before the advent of the Noble Prophet ﷺ, the people were in manifest error: they were caught in polytheism, false beliefs and vile deeds, and were in great need of a perfect spiritual guide. (Khazin, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 2, 4/264; Madarik, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 2, p. 1239, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Three Reasons for the Description “Unschooled Prophet”

runs.text: Three Reasons for the Description “Unschooled Prophet”

blocks.text: The Leader of the Messengers ﷺ is described as the “Unschooled Prophet” for many reasons. Three are mentioned here:

runs.text: The Leader of the Messengers ﷺ is described as the “Unschooled Prophet” for many reasons. Three are mentioned here:

blocks.text:
1. He was sent to the unlettered community. The Book of Isaiah states that Allah Almighty says: “I shall send an unschooled one among the unlettered, and I shall seal prophethood through him.”
2. His advent took place in Umm al-Qura, meaning Makkah al-Mukarramah.
3. The Luminous Master ﷺ neither wrote nor read from a book, and this was his excellence: because of his perfect retention of knowledge, he had no need of it. Writing is a mental craft produced through a bodily instrument. If a being has the Supreme Pen under his command, what need has he of this writing? The fact that the Noble Prophet ﷺ did not write, yet was an expert in writing, is a magnificent miracle. He taught scribes the knowledge and methods of writing, taught craftsmen their trades, and Allah Almighty made him more knowledgeable than all creation in every perfection of this world and the Hereafter. (Khazain-ul-Irfan, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 2, p. 1023, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Five Lessons from Verse 62:2

runs.text: Five Lessons from Verse 62:2

blocks.text: Five matters are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Five matters are learned from this verse:

blocks.text:
1. Purity of the heart is attained through the gracious gaze of the Most Revered Prophet ﷺ; faith and righteous deeds are means of purification.
2. The Quran and Hadith are not so simple that everyone can understand them merely through personal reason; otherwise the Luminous Master ﷺ would not have been sent to teach them.
3. Hadith is also necessary for guidance.
4. The Holy Quran must not be understood merely through personal reason; it must be understood through the teaching of the Noble Prophet ﷺ, otherwise one will go astray.
5. The Crowned Messenger ﷺ was not anyone's student in this world, because at the time of his advent ordinary people were ignorant.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And he (i.e. the Beloved Prophet Muhammad) also purifies and bestows knowledge to others amongst them who have not yet joined the former ones; and only He is the Most Honourable, the Wise.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
And he (i.e. the Beloved Prophet Muhammad) also purifies and bestows knowledge to others amongst them who have not yet joined the former ones; and only He is the Most Honourable, the Wise.

blocks.text: {وَ اٰخَرِیْنَ مِنْهُمْ: And others from among them.} This verse is connected with the preceding verse and mentions further people whom the Noble Messenger ﷺ purifies and teaches. “Others” among the unlettered may mean non-Arabs, or it may mean all those who enter Islam after the Noble Prophet ﷺ until the Day of Judgement. Their not joining the former people means that they did not live in their time but came after them. (Madarik, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 3, p. 1239; Khazin, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 3, 4/264.)

Their not joining the former people means that they did not live in their time but came after them. (Madarik, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 3, p. 1239; Khazin, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 3, 4/264.)

blocks.text: A blessed hadith indicates that non-Arabs are meant by “others.” Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ states: When Surah Al-Jumu'ah was revealed, we were present in the blessed court of the Noble Prophet ﷺ. When he recited, “And others among them who have not yet joined them,” a man asked, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who are those who have not yet joined the former ones?” The Prophet ﷺ did not answer until the man asked two or three times. Sayyiduna Salman al-Farsi رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ was among us. The Noble Prophet ﷺ placed his hand upon Sayyiduna Salman and said: “By the One in Whose power is my life, even if religion were near the Pleiades, the sons of Persia would go there and attain it.” (Muslim, Book of the Virtues of the Companions, chapter on the virtue of Persia, p. 1378, hadith 230–231 (2546).)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: The example of those who were entrusted with the Tawrah, they then did not carry out its commands, is like the example of a donkey carrying books on its back; what an evil example it is of the people who belied the verses of Allah; and Allah does not guide the unjust.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

The example of those who were entrusted with the Tawrah, they then did not carry out its commands, is like the example of a donkey carrying books on its back; what an evil example it is of the people who belied the verses of Allah; and Allah does not guide the unjust.

blocks.text: {مَثَلُ الَّذِیْنَ حُمِّلُوا التَّوْرٰىةَ: The example of those upon whom the Torah was placed.} The preceding verses stated that the Most Revered Prophet ﷺ was sent to the unlettered. The Jews objected that the Leader of the Messengers ﷺ had been sent only to the Arabs and not to them. Allah Almighty presents their example here. Those who were commanded to follow the rulings of the Torah did not act upon it and thus did not bear its responsibility; despite finding in it the praise and description of the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ, they did not believe in him. Their example is like a donkey carrying books on its back, gaining nothing beyond the burden and knowing nothing of the knowledge within them. Such is the state of these Jews: they carry the Torah, memorise its words, gain no benefit from it and do not act according to it. What an evil example are those who deny Allah Almighty's verses; and Allah Almighty does not guide those whom He knows to be unjust. (Tafsir Kabir, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 5, 10/539; Khazin, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 5, 4/265; Madarik, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 5, p. 1240, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Reasons for Comparing the Jews to a Donkey

runs.text: Reasons for Comparing the Jews to a Donkey

blocks.text: The Jews are compared to a donkey rather than another animal for several reasons. First, a donkey carries more load than a horse or mule. Second, ignorance and foolishness are more associated with a donkey than with other animals. Third, customarily a donkey is regarded as more contemptible than other animals. (Tafsir Kabir, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 5, 10/540, excerpted.)

blocks.text: The Example of Those Who Neither Understand nor Act upon the Quran

runs.text: The Example of Those Who Neither Understand nor Act upon the Quran

blocks.text: Allamah Ali ibn Muhammad Khazin, may Allah have mercy upon him, says that the example given in this verse of the Jews who did not act upon the Torah also applies to those who do not understand the meanings of the Holy Quran, do not act upon it and turn away from it. (Khazin, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 5, 4/265.) Therefore every Muslim should try to understand the Holy Quran and act upon its commands, so that this example does not apply to him.

blocks.text: Five Warnings against Failing to Act upon Knowledge

runs.text: Five Warnings against Failing to Act upon Knowledge

blocks.text:
1. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “On the Day of Judgement, the scholar who received no benefit from his knowledge will suffer the most severe punishment among people.” (Al-Mu'jam al-Saghir, chapter Al-Ta, under Tahir, p. 182, part 1.)
2. Sayyiduna al-Walid ibn Uqbah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Most Revered Prophet ﷺ said: “Some people of Paradise will see some people of Hell and ask them, ‘Why did you enter Hell when we entered Paradise through the very knowledge we learned from you?’ They will reply, ‘We did not do what we used to say.’” (Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, chapter Alif, under Ahmad, 1/41, hadith 99.)
3. Sayyiduna Abu Darda رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ says that the Noble Prophet ﷺ said to him: “O Uwaymir! What will be your condition when, on the Day of Judgement, you are asked: Did you acquire knowledge or remain ignorant? If you say, ‘I acquired knowledge,’ you will be asked: How much did you act upon your knowledge? If you say, ‘I remained ignorant,’ you will be asked: What was your excuse for remaining ignorant? Why did you not acquire knowledge?” (Ibn Asakir, letter Meem, 8793—Abu Muhammad al-Kalbi, 67/181.)
4. Sayyiduna Hudhayfah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Crowned Messenger ﷺ said: “Destruction is for the one who does not acquire knowledge, and destruction is also for the one who acquires knowledge and then does not act upon it.” (Kanz al-Ummal, letter Ain, Book of Knowledge, section of sayings, chapter 2, 5/86, part 10, hadith 29036.)
5. Sayyiduna Umar al-Faruq رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “I fear for you every knowledgeable hypocrite who speaks words of wisdom but acts upon sins.” (Kanz al-Ummal, letter Ain, Book of Knowledge, section of sayings, chapter 2, 5/86, part 10, hadith 29040.)

blocks.text: {قُلْ یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ هَادُوْا: Say (O Beloved), “O Jews!”} The Jews used to say, “We are Allah Almighty's sons and beloved ones. If you are truthful in this claim, wish for death, so that death may take you to that destination, because the Hereafter is better than the world for Allah Almighty's friends.” (Ruh al-Bayan, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 6, 9/518; Khazin, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 6, 4/265, excerpted.)

blocks.text: The Sacred Ruling on Wishing for Death

runs.text: The Sacred Ruling on Wishing for Death

blocks.text: The hadith prohibit wishing for death. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None of you should wish for death. A righteous person should not wish for it, because he may perform more good deeds; and a sinner should not wish for it, because he may repent.” (Bukhari, Book of Patients, chapter on a patient's wishing for death, 4/13, hadith 5673.)

runs.text: The hadith prohibit wishing for death. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None of you should wish for death. A righteous person should not wish for it, because he may perform more good deeds; and a sinner should not wish for it, because he may repent.” (Bukhari, Book of Patients, chapter on a patient's wishing for death, 4/13, hadith 5673.)

blocks.text: He also narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “None of you should wish for death, nor should he pray for it before it comes, because when he passes away his deeds end, while a believer's life only increases him in goodness.” (Muslim, Book of Remembrance and Supplication, chapter on the dislike of wishing for death because of harm, p. 1441, hadith 13 (2682).)

blocks.text: However, if someone is compelled to wish for death, the blessed hadith also gives its method. Sayyiduna Anas رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Crowned Messenger ﷺ said: “None of you should wish for death because of an affliction that has befallen him. If he must do so, let him say: ‘O Allah, عزوجل, keep me alive as long as life is better for me, and give me death when death is better for me.’” (Bukhari, Book of Patients, chapter on a patient's wishing for death, 4/13, hadith 5671.)

The manner in which supplication is permitted is extremely beautiful, because it includes the good and evil of religion and the world. Thus one has expressed the wish for death, but according to the proper rule; the aim is achieved and the prohibition is also obeyed. (Miraat al-Manajih, Book of Funerals, chapter on wishing for death and its mention, first section, 2/421, under hadith 1513.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Say you (O Beloved), 'The death from which you (are trying to) flee will definitely meet you, then you will be returned to Him Who knows all the unseen and the seen, He will then inform you of what you did.'

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

Say you (O Beloved), 'The death from which you (are trying to) flee will definitely meet you, then you will be returned to Him Who knows all the unseen and the seen, He will then inform you of what you did.'

blocks.text: {قُلْ اِنَّ الْمَوْتَ الَّذِیْ تَفِرُّوْنَ مِنْهُ: Say (O Beloved), “The death from which you flee.”} O Beloved ﷺ, tell these Jews: You cannot escape the death from which you flee because of the consequences of your disbelief. It will certainly come to you, and this flight will not benefit you. After passing away, you will be returned to Allah Almighty, Who knows every unseen and visible matter; no state of yours is hidden from Him. He will then inform you of your deeds, meaning what you did in the world, and punish you for them. (Tafsir Kabir, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 8, 10/541; Ruh al-Bayan, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 9, 9/519–520, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Three Ways Deeds Will Be Shown on the Day of Judgement

runs.text: Three Ways Deeds Will Be Shown on the Day of Judgement

blocks.text: People will be informed of their deeds on the Day of Judgement in various ways. Three are mentioned here:

runs.text: People will be informed of their deeds on the Day of Judgement in various ways. Three are mentioned here:

blocks.text:
1. Their deeds will be shown by presenting their records. Allah Almighty says: “وَ وُضِعَ الْكِتٰبُ فَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِیْنَ مُشْفِقِیْنَ مِمَّا فِیْهِ وَ یَقُوْلُوْنَ یٰوَیْلَتَنَا مَالِ هٰذَا الْكِتٰبِ لَا یُغَادِرُ صَغِیْرَةً وَّ لَا كَبِیْرَةً اِلَّاۤ اَحْصٰىهَاۚ-وَ وَجَدُوْا مَا عَمِلُوْا حَاضِرًاؕ-وَ لَا یَظْلِمُ رَبُّكَ اَحَدًا” (Al-Kahf: 49). Translation: “And the Book of Deeds will be placed, so you will see the sinners fearful of what is in it and saying, ‘Alas for us! What is the matter with this Book that it has left nothing small or great unrecorded?’ And they will find all their deeds present before them; and your Lord does not wrong anyone.”
2. A person's limbs will testify to his deeds. Allah Almighty says: “یَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَیْهِمْ اَلْسِنَتُهُمْ وَ اَیْدِیْهِمْ وَ اَرْجُلُهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوْا یَعْمَلُوْنَ” (An-Nur: 24). Translation: “The Day when their tongues, hands and feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do.” He also says: “اَلْیَوْمَ نَخْتِمُ عَلٰۤى اَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَ تُكَلِّمُنَاۤ اَیْدِیْهِمْ وَ تَشْهَدُ اَرْجُلُهُمْ بِمَا كَانُوْا یَكْسِبُوْنَ” (Ya-Sin: 65). Translation: “Today We shall seal their mouths, their hands will speak to Us and their feet will testify concerning what they used to earn.”
3. The earth will relate people's deeds. Allah Almighty says: “یَوْمَىٕذٍ تُحَدِّثُ اَخْبَارَهَاۙ(۴) بِاَنَّ رَبَّكَ اَوْحٰى لَهَا” (Az-Zilzal: 4–5). Translation: “On that Day it will narrate its news, because your Lord has commanded it.”

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O believers! When the call for Salah is given on the day of Jumu'ah (i.e. Friday), so hurry towards the remembrance of Allah, and stop buying and selling; this is better for you if you know.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
O believers! When the call for Salah is given on the day of Jumu'ah (i.e. Friday), so hurry towards the remembrance of Allah, and stop buying and selling; this is better for you if you know.

blocks.text: {یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْۤا اِذَا نُوْدِیَ لِلصَّلٰوةِ مِنْ یَّوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ: O believers! When the call to prayer is given on Friday.} This verse explains the rulings of the Friday prayer. Three matters related to it are noted here:

runs.text: {یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْۤا اِذَا نُوْدِیَ لِلصَّلٰوةِ مِنْ یَّوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ: O believers! When the call to prayer is given on Friday.} This verse explains the rulings of the Friday prayer. Three matters related to it are noted here:

blocks.text:
1. “The call” in this verse means the first call, not the second call connected with the sermon. Although the first call was added during the era of Sayyiduna Uthman Ghani رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, the obligation to prepare for the prayer and abandon buying and selling is connected with it.
2. “Hurry” does not mean run. It means to begin preparing for the prayer. According to the majority of scholars, “the remembrance of Allah” means the sermon.
3. This verse establishes the obligation of Friday prayer, the prohibition of worldly occupations such as buying and selling, the obligation of making effort for the prayer, and the sermon. (Khazain-ul-Irfan, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 9, p. 1025, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Why Friday Is Called Jumu'ah

runs.text: Why Friday Is Called Jumu'ah

blocks.text: In Arabic, this day was called Arubah; later it was named Jumu'ah. The first person to call it Jumu'ah was Ka'b ibn Lu'ayy. There are various explanations for the name; one is that it is called Jumu'ah because congregations gather on this day for prayer. (Khazin, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 9, 4/265.)

blocks.text: The First Friday Prayer of the Crowned Messenger ﷺ

runs.text: The First Friday Prayer of the Crowned Messenger ﷺ

blocks.text: Historians of the Prophetic biography state that when the Most Revered Prophet ﷺ migrated and reached Madinah Tayyibah, he stopped at Quba on Monday, 12 Rabi al-Awwal, at forenoon. He stayed there from Monday through Thursday and laid the foundation of the mosque. On Friday he set out for Madinah Tayyibah. When Friday time came in the valley of Banu Salim ibn Awf, the people made that place a mosque, and the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ performed the Friday prayer and delivered the sermon there. This was the first Friday prayer that the Noble Prophet ﷺ performed with his Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ. (Khazin, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 9, 4/266.)

blocks.text: Four Virtues of Friday

runs.text: Four Virtues of Friday

blocks.text: Many hadith mention the virtues of Friday. Four are presented here:

runs.text: Many hadith mention the virtues of Friday. Four are presented here:

blocks.text:
1. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Crowned Messenger ﷺ said: “The best day upon which the sun has risen is Friday. On it, Sayyiduna Adam عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام was created, on it he entered Paradise, on it he was commanded to descend from Paradise, and the Day of Judgement will be established on Friday.” (Muslim, Book of Friday, chapter on the virtue of Friday, p. 425, hadith 18 (854).)
2. Sayyiduna Abu Darda رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Leader of the Messengers ﷺ said: “Send abundant blessings upon me on Friday, for it is a witnessed day; angels attend it, and whoever sends blessings upon me, they will be presented to me.” Sayyiduna Abu Darda asked, “And after passing away?” He replied: “Indeed, Allah Almighty has forbidden the earth from consuming the bodies of the Prophets. Allah Almighty's Prophet is alive and provided sustenance.” (Ibn Majah, Book of Funerals, chapter on mentioning his passing away and burial ﷺ, 2/291, hadith 1637.)
3. Sayyiduna Abu Lubabah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Friday is the master of all days and the greatest in Allah Almighty's sight. It is greater in His sight than Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr. It contains five qualities: (1) Allah Almighty created Sayyiduna Adam عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام on it; (2) He sent him down to earth on it; (3) He called him back on it; (4) there is an hour on it in which a servant asks Allah Almighty for anything and He gives it, provided he does not ask for something unlawful; and (5) the Day of Judgement will be established on it. 4. blocks.text: The Hour in Which Supplication Is Accepted on Friday

runs.text: The Hour in Which Supplication Is Accepted on Friday

blocks.text: There is an hour on Friday in which Allah Almighty especially accepts supplication, as mentioned in the third hadith above. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Crowned Messenger ﷺ said: “There is an hour in it when a Muslim servant finds it while standing and praying; whatever he asks Allah Almighty for will be granted.” He indicated with his hand that the time is very short. (Bukhari, Book of Friday, chapter on the hour on Friday, 1/321, hadith 935.)

blocks.text: Two Virtues of the Friday Prayer

runs.text: Two Virtues of the Friday Prayer

blocks.text:
1. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Most Revered Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever performs ablution properly, comes on Friday, listens and remains silent, will be forgiven the sins committed between that Friday and the next, along with three additional days. Whoever touches pebbles has engaged in vain activity.” (Muslim, Book of Friday, chapter on the virtue of listening and remaining silent during the sermon, p. 427, hadith 27 (857).) That is, while listening to the sermon, even moving a pebble that has fallen is included in vain activity.
2. Sayyiduna Abu Sa'id رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah Almighty will record as a person of Paradise whoever does five things in one day: (1) visits a sick person; (2) attends a funeral; (3) fasts; (4) goes to Friday prayer; and (5) frees a slave.” (Al-Ihsan in the arrangement of Sahih Ibn Hibban, Book of Prayer, chapter on Friday prayer, 3/191, part 4, hadith 2760.)

blocks.text: Warnings for Abandoning Friday Prayer

runs.text: Warnings for Abandoning Friday Prayer

blocks.text:
1. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah and Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Umar رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا narrate that the Most Revered Prophet ﷺ said: “People must stop abandoning Friday, or Allah Almighty will seal their hearts, and then they will become among the heedless.” (Muslim, Book of Friday, chapter on the stern warning for abandoning Friday, p. 430, hadith 40 (865).)
2. Sayyiduna Usamah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Messenger ﷺ said: “Whoever abandons three Fridays without an excuse will be recorded among the hypocrites.” (Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, Musnad al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, chapter on what is narrated concerning the evil woman, 1/170, hadith 422.)

blocks.text: Three Islamic Rulings Concerning the Obligation of Friday Prayer

runs.text: Three Islamic Rulings Concerning the Obligation of Friday Prayer

blocks.text:
1. Friday prayer is an individual obligation, and its obligation is more emphatic than that of Zuhr. Whoever denies it is a disbeliever. (Bahar-e-Shariat, part 4, chapter on Friday, fiqh rulings, 1/762.)
2. There are six conditions for performing Friday prayer. If even one is absent, Friday prayer is not valid: (1) the place where it is performed must be a city or its surrounding area; (2) the one conducting it must be the Islamic Sultan or his deputy whom he has authorised to establish Friday prayer; (3) it must be Zuhr time, meaning the prayer must be completed within Zuhr time. If Asr time begins during the prayer, even after the sitting for testimony, Friday becomes invalid and Zuhr must be performed as a make-up prayer; (4) a sermon must be delivered; (5) there must be a congregation of at least three men besides the Imam; and (6) general permission must be given, meaning the mosque door is open so that any Muslim who wishes may come and no one is stopped.
3. There are eleven conditions for Friday prayer to be obligatory. If even one is absent, it is not obligatory, although if the person performs it, it is valid: (1) residing in a city; (2) health, meaning it is not obligatory for a sick person who cannot reach the congregational mosque, or who could reach it only at the cost of worsening the illness or delaying recovery; (3) being free; (4) being male; (5) being sane; (6) being an adult; (7) having sight, meaning not being blind; (8) being able to walk; (9) not being imprisoned; (10) having no fear of a ruler, thief or other oppressor; and (11) there must not be such rain, wind, hail or cold that there is a genuine fear of harm.

blocks.text: {فَاِذَا قُضِیَتِ الصَّلٰوةُ: Then when the prayer is completed.} When the prayer has been completed, it is permissible for you to engage in earning a livelihood, acquire good deeds by seeking knowledge, visiting the sick, attending funerals, visiting scholars and engaging in similar activities. A drum was beaten to announce it according to custom, so the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went towards it until no one remained in the mosque except twelve men. I, Sayyiduna Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Sayyiduna Umar al-Faruq رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا were among those twelve. This verse was then revealed. (Muslim, Book of Friday, chapter concerning His statement, “And when they see trade or sport, they disperse towards it,” p. 429, hadith 38 (863).)

blocks.text: The meaning of this verse is: O Beloved ﷺ, when they learned of some trade or heard of some amusement, they went towards it and left you standing on the pulpit while delivering the sermon. Say to them: The reward of prayer and the blessing and good fortune of remaining in the presence of the Noble Prophet ﷺ, which is in reality with Allah Almighty, is better than sport and trade. Since Allah Almighty is the Best Provider, go towards Him and seek provision from Him. (Ruh al-Bayan, Al-Jumu'ah, under verse 11, 9/528.)

blocks.text: It should be remembered that at the time this incident occurred there was great hardship and inflation. The Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ left out of fear that goods might run out and they would fail to obtain them; in such circumstances this is natural. Moreover, before this verse was revealed they had not been prohibited from such an act. Since the command had not yet been revealed, doing this was not a sin. Therefore Allah Almighty did not condemn them in this verse; rather, He instructed them that such conduct was not worthy of their station. No objection can be made against their action.

blocks.text: {اِذَا جَآءَكَ الْمُنٰفِقُوْنَ: When the hypocrites present themselves before you.} This blessed Surah describes various conditions of the hypocrites. runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {اِتَّخَذُوْۤا اَیْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً: They made their oaths a shield.} The hypocrites made their oaths a shield so that, through them, they would remain safe from being killed or imprisoned. They swear with their tongues, but their action is that they prevent people, by creating various doubts and suspicions in their minds, from believing in the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ and striving in the way of Allah Almighty. Indeed, they commit extremely evil deeds: they come to the august court with hypocrisy, outwardly display faith in order to deceive, prevent people from the way of Allah Almighty, and choose disbelief over faith. (Khazin, Al-Munafiqun, under verse 2, 4/271; Madarik, Al-Munafiqun, under verse 2, p. 1242, excerpted.)

blocks.text: {ذٰلِكَ بِاَنَّهُمْ اٰمَنُوْا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوْا: This is because they believed and then disbelieved.} The reason for these evil deeds of the hypocrites is that they professed faith with their tongues and then became disbelievers in their hearts. The disbelief in their hearts became apparent to people, and because of these actions a seal was set upon their hearts. How, then, can faith enter their hearts now?

blocks.text: {وَ اِذَا رَاَیْتَهُمْ تُعْجِبُكَ اَجْسَامُهُمْ: And when you see them, their bodies please you.} Abdullah ibn Ubayy was a healthy, handsome and eloquent man, and the hypocrites accompanying him were much the same. When these people attended the Noble Prophet’s ﷺ blessed assembly, they spoke very attractively, in a way that pleased the listener. Therefore, this verse reveals their reality to Muslims: O Muslims! When you see hypocrites such as Abdullah ibn Ubayy and others, their bodies please you, and if they speak, you listen carefully to their speech. In reality, however, they are like pieces of wood propped against a wall: lifeless forms, with neither the spirit of faith nor the intellect that considers the outcome of matters. They regard every loud voice as being directed against them. When someone calls another person, searches for something lost, or raises his voice in the army for some purpose, they think, because of the foulness of their souls and their evil suspicion, that something has been said about them. They fear that a passage may be revealed concerning them which exposes their secrets. They are enemies, harbouring intense enmity in their hearts, and they convey information to the disbelievers and spy for them. So beware of them and do not be deceived by their outward condition. May Allah destroy them; where are they being turned away, and how do they turn away from the truth despite clear proofs having been established? (Khazin, Al-Munafiqun, under verse 4, 4/271; Madarik, Al-Munafiqun, under verse 4, p. 1243, excerpted.)

blocks.text: 1. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “In the latter days, there will be people who will earn worldly benefit through religion by means of deception and fraud. To show gentleness to people, they will wear the skin of sheep; their tongues will be sweeter than sugar, while their hearts will be the hearts of wolves. Allah Almighty will say to them: ‘Are you deceiving Me or being bold against Me? I swear by Myself that I shall certainly send upon those people a trial from among themselves that will leave even their intelligent ones bewildered and distressed.’” (Tirmidhi, Book of Asceticism, chapter 60, 4/181, hadith 2412.)

blocks.text: {وَ اِذَا قِیْلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْا: And when it is said to them, “Come.”} Occasion of revelation: When the Noble Prophet ﷺ stopped along the way after returning from the Battle of Muraysi, an incident took place there. Jihjah al-Ghifari, the employee of Sayyiduna Umar رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, and Sinan ibn Dabr al-Juhani, an ally of Abdullah ibn Ubayy, quarrelled. Jihjah called the Muhajirun and Sinan called the Ansar. At that time, the hypocrite Abdullah ibn Ubayy spoke extremely insolent and indecent words concerning the Holy Prophet ﷺ. He said, “When we reach Madinah Tayyibah, those of us who possess honour will expel the humiliated ones,” and he told his people, “If you do not give them your leftover food, they will not ride upon your necks, so do not spend anything on them now, so that they flee Madinah.”

He said, “When we reach Madinah Tayyibah, those of us who possess honour will expel the humiliated ones,” and he told his people, “If you do not give them your leftover food, they will not ride upon your necks, so do not spend anything on them now, so that they flee Madinah.”

blocks.text: When Sayyiduna Zayd ibn Arqam رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ heard this disgraceful speech, he could not bear it and said to him, “By Allah! You are the humiliated one and the one who sows enmity among his people, whereas Allah Almighty has granted the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ honour and strength, and he is beloved to the Muslims.” Abdullah ibn Ubayy said, “Be quiet. I was only saying this jokingly.” Sayyiduna Zayd ibn Arqam رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ conveyed the report to the Presence of Light ﷺ. Sayyiduna Umar رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ asked permission to kill Abdullah ibn Ubayy, but the Noble Prophet ﷺ forbade him and said, “People will say that Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ kills his own companions.” The Noble Prophet ﷺ asked Abdullah ibn Ubayy whether he had said these things. He denied it and swore that he had said nothing. His companions who were present in the blessed assembly began saying that Abdullah ibn Ubayy was an old man and that what he said must be correct; perhaps Sayyiduna Zayd ibn Arqam رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ had been mistaken and had not remembered correctly.

blocks.text: Then, when the verses above were revealed and Abdullah ibn Ubayy’s lie became clear, he was told, “Go and ask the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ to seek Allah Almighty’s forgiveness for you.” On hearing this, he turned his neck and said, “You said, ‘Believe,’ so I believed; you said, ‘Give zakat,’ so I gave zakat; now all that remains is that I prostrate to Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ.” Upon this, this noble verse was revealed.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: They are the ones who say, 'Do not spend upon those who are with Allah's Messenger until they become distressed.' And only to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not have sense.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

They are the ones who say, 'Do not spend upon those who are with Allah's Messenger until they become distressed.' And only to Allah belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not have sense.

blocks.text: {هُمُ الَّذِیْنَ یَقُوْلُوْنَ: They are the ones who say.} The hypocrites tell people, “Do not spend on the Muhajir Companions present with Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, so that poverty distresses them and they leave of their own accord and no longer remain with you ﷺ.” Yet all the treasures of the heavens and earth belong to Allah Almighty alone. In reality, He alone gives sustenance to everyone. If people stop spending on them, what of it? Allah Almighty will grant them sustenance. But the hypocrites do not understand this, which is why they utter such absurdities. They know that their sustenance depends not on servants, but on the generosity of their Lord, and they place complete trust in their Lord عزوجل.

blocks.text: The Love of the Messenger ﷺ Shown by the Son of Abdullah ibn Ubayy

runs.text: The Love of the Messenger ﷺ Shown by the Son of Abdullah ibn Ubayy

blocks.text: The son of Abdullah ibn Ubayy was also named Abdullah. He was a firm Muslim and a true lover of the Messenger ﷺ. On the return from the battle, he stood outside illuminated Madinah with his sword drawn and said to his father, “I will not let you enter Madinah until you acknowledge that you are humiliated and that Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ is honourable.” The son had always treated his father well, so his father was greatly astonished. Yet, when it came to the father opposing the Presence of Light ﷺ, no honour or love for his father remained in the son’s heart. At last, his father was compelled to acknowledge, “By Allah, I am humiliated and Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ is honourable.” Only then was he able to enter Madinah. (Sirat Halabiyyah, chapter on his campaigns ﷺ, the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq, 2/393; Madarij al-Nubuwwah, section three, chapter five, 2/157, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Lessons Learned from “And Honour Belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the Believers”

runs.text: Lessons Learned from “And Honour Belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the Believers”

blocks.text: Four matters are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Four matters are learned from this verse:

blocks.text:
1. Every believer possesses honour. It is unlawful to consider a Muslim nation humiliated or to call it lowly.
2. A believer’s honour comes from faith and righteous deeds, not from money.
3. A believer’s honour is everlasting, not temporary. This is why honour is shown even to a believer’s body and grave.
4. Whoever considers a believer humiliated is himself humiliated in the sight of Allah Almighty. A poor, needy believer possesses honour, while a wealthy disbeliever is worse.

runs.text: Types of Hypocrisy and the Signs of Practical Hypocrites

blocks.text: The discussion of the hypocrites has ended. Three hadith concerning the types of hypocrisy and the signs of practical hypocrites are now presented. Sadr al-Shariah Mufti Amjad Ali Azmi رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ states concerning hypocrisy:

runs.text: The discussion of the hypocrites has ended. Three hadith concerning the types of hypocrisy and the signs of practical hypocrites are now presented. Sadr al-Shariah Mufti Amjad Ali Azmi رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ states concerning hypocrisy:

blocks.text: Hypocrisy means claiming Islam with the tongue while denying Islam in the heart. This too is pure disbelief, and such people will be in the lowest level of Hell. In the blessed era of the Noble Prophet ﷺ, some people became known by this name because the Quran openly testified to their inward disbelief. The Prophet ﷺ recognised each one through his vast knowledge and declared that he was a hypocrite. In the present age, however, no particular person may be called a hypocrite with certainty. Whoever professes Islam before us will be regarded as a Muslim until a statement or action contrary to faith issues from him. A branch of hypocrisy is nevertheless found in this age: many misguided people call themselves Muslims, yet alongside their claim to Islam they deny essentials of religion. (Bahar-e-Shariat, Part One, The Discussion of Faith and Disbelief, 1/182.)

blocks.text: Practical hypocrisy means doing something unworthy of Muslims and characteristic of hypocrites. Two hadith are presented here:

runs.text: Practical hypocrisy means doing something unworthy of Muslims and characteristic of hypocrites. Two hadith are presented here:

blocks.text: 1. blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O believers! Let not your wealth or your children (or) anything cause you to neglect the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does this, so it is they who are in loss.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
O believers! Let not your wealth or your children (or) anything cause you to neglect the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does this, so it is they who are in loss.

blocks.text: {یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْا: O believers!} The preceding verses described the conditions of the hypocrites. From here, the believers are advised: O believers! Do not let your wealth and children, like those of the hypocrites, make you heedless of Allah Almighty’s remembrance. Whoever becomes so occupied with the world that he forgets religion, neglects his own condition out of love for wealth, and remains heedless of the comfort of the Hereafter for the sake of his children’s happiness is among those who suffer loss, because such people preferred the perishing world to the everlasting blessings of the home of the Hereafter. (Khazin, Al-Munafiqun, under verse 9, 4/274; Madarik, Al-Munafiqun, under verse 9, p. 1245, excerpted.)

blocks.text: A blessed hadith concerning worldly wealth is noted here. Sayyiduna Hakim ibn Hizam رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ states: I asked the Noble Messenger ﷺ for some wealth and pleaded repeatedly. He said: “O Hakim! Why do you ask so excessively? O Hakim! Indeed, this wealth is green and sweet, yet it is also the dirt from people’s hands. Allah Almighty’s hand is above the hand of the giver; the giver’s hand is above the hand of the recipient; and the hand of the recipient is the lowest.” (Musnad Imam Ahmad, Musnad of the Makkans, Musnad of Hakim ibn Hizam, 5/228, hadith 15321.)

blocks.text: {وَ اَنْفِقُوْا مِنْ مَّا رَزَقْنٰكُمْ: And spend some of what We have provided you.} O believers! blocks.text: This verse mentions the Chasht prayer. Therefore, three virtues of the Chasht prayer are noted here.

runs.text: This verse mentions the Chasht prayer. Therefore, three virtues of the Chasht prayer are noted here.

blocks.text: 1. Sayyiduna Abu Dharr رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Messenger ﷺ said: “There is a charity due from a person for every joint of his body; there are three hundred and sixty joints. Every glorification is charity, every praise is charity, saying لَا اِلٰـہَ اِلَّا اللّٰہ is charity, saying اَللّٰہُ اَکْبَرْ is charity, enjoining good is charity and forbidding evil is charity; and two rak'ats of Chasht suffice for all of this.” (Muslim, Book of the Prayer of Travellers and its Shortening, chapter on the recommendation of the Duha prayer, p. 363, hadith 84 (720))

blocks.text: 2. Sayyiduna Anas ibn Malik رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Radiant Presence ﷺ said: “Whoever offers twelve rak'ats of Chasht, Allah Almighty will build a palace of gold for him in Paradise.” (Tirmidhi, Book of Witr, chapter on what has been reported concerning the Duha prayer, 2/17, hadith 472.)

blocks.text: 3. Sayyiduna Abu Darda رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Whoever offers two rak'ats of Chasht will not be recorded among the heedless. Whoever offers four rak'ats will be recorded among the worshippers. Whoever offers six rak'ats will be granted sufficiency for that day by Allah Almighty. Whoever offers eight rak'ats will be recorded by Allah Almighty among the obedient. Whoever offers twelve rak'ats, Allah Almighty will build a palace for him in Paradise. There is no day or night in which Allah Almighty does not bestow favour and charity upon His servants, and no one has received a greater favour than the servant to whom He inspired His remembrance.” (At-Targhib wat-Tarhib, Book of Voluntary Prayers, encouragement towards the Duha prayer, 1/318, hadith 1011)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: That your Lord has neither abandoned you (O Beloved), nor did He dislike you.

blocks.text: {مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَ مَا قَلٰى: That your Lord has neither abandoned you nor did He dislike you.} In response to the disbelievers' objection, the Exalted Imam Ahmad Raza Khan رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ says that the Almighty declared: “By the forenoon and by the night when it casts its darkness; or, O Beloved, by your radiant countenance and by your locks when they spread over your shining cheeks: your Lord has neither abandoned you nor made you an enemy.” These wretched people also understand well in their hearts what mercy Allah has bestowed upon you. They burn when they see that mercy, and out of envy and enmity they construct this storm and burst the blisters of their burning hearts. Yet they do not know that “And indeed, the latter is better for you than the former”: certainly, the Hereafter is better for you than the world. There, you will receive blessings which no eye has seen, no ear has heard and which have not occurred to the imagination of any human or angel. Their brief description is: “And indeed, it is close that your Lord will give you so much that you will be pleased.” Soon it will be clear to friends and enemies alike that no one was as beloved as you.

Their brief description is: “And indeed, it is close that your Lord will give you so much that you will be pleased.” Soon it will be clear to friends and enemies alike that no one was as beloved as you.

blocks.text: In any case, if these blind people do not believe in the Hereafter today, then, O Beloved, the magnificent, majestic, abundant and immense blessings and mercies of Allah upon you are not only of today; they have existed from ancient times. Did they not see your earlier states and gain certainty from them that the gracious attention upon you is not of a kind that can ever change? “Did He not find you (O Beloved as) an orphan, then provided you with a place? And He found you profoundly engrossed in His love, so He gave you a way towards Himself. And found you in need, then made you prosperous. Therefore, do not put pressure on an orphan. And do not scold a beggar. And publicise well the bounty of your Lord.” (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 30/165–166, abridged.)

blocks.text: This objection of the disbelievers shows that they knew the Noble Prophet ﷺ to be Allah Almighty's Messenger, for if they had not known this, they would not have made such an objection. It also shows that the Holy Quran is not speech composed by the Noble Prophet ﷺ himself; rather, it is the Word of Allah Almighty, revealed by Him to the Crown of Messengership ﷺ. If the Holy Quran had been his own speech, his speech would have continued without interruption and there would have been no pause in it, leaving the disbelievers no opportunity to object that Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ had been abandoned and disliked by his Lord عزوجل.

blocks.text: Allah Almighty's gracious promise to His Beloved ﷺ includes the blessings He bestowed upon him in this world: perfection of the soul, knowledge of the first and the last, the manifestation of the command, the supremacy of the religion, the victories achieved during his blessed era and those achieved during the era of the Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ and which will continue to come to Muslims until the Day of Judgement, the universality of his invitation, the spread of Islam in the east and west, the superiority of his Ummah over all communities, and such miracles and perfections of his that Allah Almighty alone knows. The promise also includes the honour and veneration of the Hereafter: Allah Almighty granted him general and particular intercession, the Praiseworthy Station and other magnificent blessings. (Ruh al-Bayan, Ad-Duha, under verse 5, 10/455; Khazin, Ad-Duha, under verse 5, 4/386, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Did He not find you (O Beloved as) an orphan, then provided you with a place?

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
Did He not find you (O Beloved as) an orphan, then provided you with a place?

blocks.text: {اَلَمْ یَجِدْكَ یَتِیْمًا فَاٰوٰى: Did He not find you as an orphan, then provided you with a place?} The father of the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ passed away in Madinah Tayyibah when he was still in his mother's blessed womb and the pregnancy was two months along. His father left neither wealth nor a home. After his passing, his grandfather Abdul-Muttalib took responsibility for him. When he was four or six years old, his mother also passed away. When he was eight, his grandfather Abdul-Muttalib passed away as well. Before his passing, he instructed his son Abu Talib, who was the Noble Prophet's ﷺ paternal uncle, to care for and supervise him. Abu Talib continued to serve him until he announced his Prophethood by the command of Allah Almighty.

runs.text: {اَلَمْ یَجِدْكَ یَتِیْمًا فَاٰوٰى: Did He not find you as an orphan, then provided you with a place?} The father of the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ passed away in Madinah Tayyibah when he was still in his mother's blessed womb and the pregnancy was two months along. His father left neither wealth nor a home. After his passing, his grandfather Abdul-Muttalib took responsibility for him. When he was four or six years old, his mother also passed away. When he was eight, his grandfather Abdul-Muttalib passed away as well. Before his passing, he instructed his son Abu Talib, who was the Noble Prophet's ﷺ paternal uncle, to care for and supervise him. Abu Talib continued to serve him until he announced his Prophethood by the command of Allah Almighty.

blocks.text: Another meaning given by the exegetes is that “orphan” can mean unique and matchless, as in the phrase “the unique pearl.” On this interpretation, the verse means that Allah Almighty found the Noble Prophet ﷺ unique and matchless in honour and nobility, gave him a place in nearness, raised him under His protection among his enemies, and honoured him with Prophethood, Messengership and being His chosen bondsman. (Khazin, Ad-Duha, under verse 6, 4/386; Jaml, Ad-Duha, under verse 6, 8/347; Ruh al-Bayan, Ad-Duha, under verse 6, 10/456–457, excerpted.)
