blocks.text: “وَ لَا تُؤْتُوا السُّفَهَآءَ اَمْوَالَكُمُ الَّتِیْ جَعَلَ اللّٰهُ لَكُمْ قِیٰمًا وَّ ارْزُقُوْهُمْ فِیْهَا وَ اكْسُوْهُمْ وَ قُوْلُوْا لَهُمْ قَوْلًا مَّعْرُوْفًا(۵)وَ ابْتَلُوا الْیَتٰمٰى حَتّٰۤى اِذَا بَلَغُوا النِّكَاحَۚ-فَاِنْ اٰنَسْتُمْ مِّنْهُمْ رُشْدًا فَادْفَعُوْۤا اِلَیْهِمْ اَمْوَالَهُمْۚ-وَ لَا تَاْكُلُوْهَاۤ اِسْرَافًا وَّ بِدَارًا اَنْ یَّكْبَرُوْاؕ-وَ مَنْ كَانَ غَنِیًّا فَلْیَسْتَعْفِفْۚ-وَ مَنْ كَانَ فَقِیْرًا فَلْیَاْكُلْ بِالْمَعْرُوْفِؕ-فَاِذَا دَفَعْتُمْ اِلَیْهِمْ اَمْوَالَهُمْ فَاَشْهِدُوْا عَلَیْهِمْؕ-وَ كَفٰى بِاللّٰهِ حَسِیْبًا” (An-Nisa: 5–6)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Irfan translation: “And do not give the foolish their wealth, which Allah has made a means of support for you; provide them food and clothing from it and speak good words to them. Keep testing the orphans until they reach the age of marriage. Then, if you find sound judgement in them, hand over their wealth to them. Do not consume it extravagantly and hastily, fearing that they will grow up. Whoever is wealthy should abstain, and whoever is poor may eat according to what is fair. When you hand over their wealth to them, take witnesses over them; and Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner.”

Encouragement to support an orphan: Sayyiduna Sahl ibn Sa'd رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Messenger ﷺ said: “I and the one who cares for an orphan, whether the orphan is his own or another's, will be like this in Paradise.” He then indicated with his index and middle fingers and kept a slight space between them. (Bukhari, Book of Divorce, chapter on Li'an, 3/497, hadith 5304)

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {وَ اَمَّا السَّآىٕلَ فَلَا تَنْهَرْ: And do not scold a beggar.} O Beloved ﷺ, when a beggar comes to your generous door and asks for something, do not scold him in any way. Rather, give him something, or explain your excuse for not giving with good manners and gentleness. (Khazin, Ad-Duha, under verse 10, 4/388; Madarik, Ad-Duha, under verse 10, p. 1357, excerpted.)

blocks.text: {وَ اَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ: And publicise well the bounty of your Lord.} “Bounty” here refers to the blessings Allah Almighty bestowed upon His Beloved ﷺ and also to those blessings which Allah Almighty promised him. blocks.text: Three matters are learned from this verse.

runs.text: Three matters are learned from this verse.

blocks.text: 1. Muslims should keep their appearance and conduct Islamic, because this displays the great blessing of Islam bestowed by Allah Almighty.

items.text: Muslims should keep their appearance and conduct Islamic, because this displays the great blessing of Islam bestowed by Allah Almighty.

blocks.text: 2. Celebrating the blessed Mawlid, Giyarhwin Sharif and the Urs of the righteous elders are excellent deeds, because these personalities are blessings of Allah Almighty, and the Mawlid and Urs publicise the birth of the Radiant Presence ﷺ and the lives of Allah Almighty's saints.

blocks.text: 3. Praising the Noble Prophet ﷺ is an excellent act of worship, because his blessed qualities are also blessings of Allah Almighty for us. Therefore, mentioning the qualities and perfections of the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ is publicising the bounties of Allah Almighty.

runs.text: Mufti Ahmad Yar Khan Naeemi رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ explained some beautiful points from this verse:

blocks.text: 1. It is clear that the rank of warriors is extremely high, because Allah Almighty swore by their horses.

items.text: It is clear that the rank of warriors is extremely high, because Allah Almighty swore by their horses.

runs.text: It is clear that the rank of warriors is extremely high, because Allah Almighty swore by their horses.

blocks.text: 2. When a warrior's horse carries him on its back, the horse's rank rises. Therefore, when Sayyiduna Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ carried the Leader of the Messengers صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ on his shoulder on the night of the Migration; when Sayyiduna Ali al-Murtada كَرَّمَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی وَجْہَہُ الْکَرِیْم laid the Radiant Presence صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ on his knee at Sahba; and when Sayyidatuna Aishah Siddiqah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا took the blessed head of the Noble Presence صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّمَ onto her chest at the time of his passing away, then what must be the rank of that gentle lady Aminah and the foster mother Halimah who nursed the Noble Presence صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ in their laps?

blocks.text: {وَ اِنَّهٗ لِحُبِّ الْخَیْرِ لَشَدِیْدٌ: And indeed, he definitely loves wealth to the extreme.} The summary of this verse and the three verses after it is that man is extremely strong in his love and pursuit of wealth, while he is weak in worshipping Allah Almighty and giving thanks for His blessings. Does the person afflicted by love of wealth not know that when those in the graves are raised and presented before Allah Almighty, and what is in the chests is disclosed, Allah Almighty will recompense them for their good and bad deeds? Indeed, their Lord عزَّوَجَلَّ is fully informed, as He has always been, of their deeds, intentions, obedience and disobedience on the Day of Judgement, which is the Day of Decision. (Tafsir Kabir, Al-Adiyat, under verse 8, 11/262; Samarqandi, Al-Adiyat, under verses 8–11, 3/503–504; Madarik, Al-Adiyat, under verses 8–11, p. 1369, excerpted)

blocks.text: The heedless person's hard heart

runs.text: The heedless person's hard heart

blocks.text: Nur al-Irfan states that the heedless person is hard-hearted because of love of wealth, since love of wealth causes hardness of the heart, whereas love of the Noble Prophet صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّم is a cause of softness of the heart. Consider Yazid, Pharaoh and Shaddad: they were harder-hearted than animals, merely because of their love of wealth. Alternatively, the heedless person is hard-hearted regarding wealth but soft regarding religion, meaning that he cannot bear difficulty in religion. This is why people generally endure hardships for the world which they do not endure for religion.

blocks.text: Love of wealth has four forms

runs.text: Love of wealth has four forms

blocks.text: Remember that love of wealth is of four kinds:

runs.text: Remember that love of wealth is of four kinds:

blocks.text:
1. Faith-based love, such as wanting wealth for Hajj and similar purposes.
2. Self-based love, such as desiring wealth for one's own comfort and ease.
3. Rebellious love, such as loving wealth merely to accumulate it and leave it behind.
4. Satanic love, meaning love of wealth for sin and disobedience.

blocks.text: The last two forms are intended here. The first kind of love is worship. Sayyiduna Sulayman عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام said: “اِنِّیْۤ اَحْبَبْتُ حُبَّ الْخَیْرِ”. The Noble Prophet صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہ وَ سَلَّم had great love for the horses of jihad. Since wealth is a great means of goodness, it was called “good”. In the view of the Sufis, love of a blessing is blameworthy when it fills the heart so completely that no room remains for love of the Bestower. This is what is meant here: the heart should contain only the love of the Beloved, with no place for others, while other loves should remain outside the heart. A ship remains safe when the water is outside it; if water enters the ship, it sinks.

It was given this name because, due to its terror, dread and severity, the hearts of all people will tremble. Some exegetes say that the Day of Judgement is called Qariah because of the voice of Sayyiduna Israfil عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام. When he blows the Trumpet, all creation will perish from the intensity of the sound of his blowing. (Khazin, Al-Qariah, under verse 1, 4/403)

blocks.text: {فَاَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِیْنُهٗ: So, as for the one whose scales (of good deeds) are heavy.} After mentioning the state of the Day of Judgement, two groups of creation on the Day of Judgement are described here. The summary of this verse and the five verses after it is that the scales of the one whose good deeds are heavy because he followed the truth, and whose weighty good deeds are greater in number, will be in a desirable life in Paradise. The scales of the one whose good deeds become light because he used to follow falsehood will be light; his abode will be Hawiyah. And what have you understood what it is? It is a blazing fire of extreme heat and intensity.

runs.text: Two matters concerning the weighing of deeds should be kept in mind:

blocks.text: 1. Regarding the weighing of deeds, one opinion is that on the Day of Judgement the good deeds of a believer will be brought in a beautiful form and placed in the Scale. If they prevail, Paradise is for him. The evil deeds of a disbeliever will be brought in the ugliest form and placed in the Scale, and his weighing will be light because the deeds of disbelievers are false and have no weight; therefore, they will be admitted into Hell. Another opinion is that only the deeds of believers will be weighed on the Day of Judgement. If a believer's good deeds prevail over his evil deeds, he will enter Paradise. blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O (Beloved) Prophet! (Tell the believers) when you people divorce women, so divorce them (when they are in the state of purity, with one divorce) at (the start of) their prescribed period, and keep (an accurate) calculation of their 'Iddah (i.e. waiting period). And (O Muslims) fear Allah, your Lord, Do not banish them from their (husband's) homes, nor should they leave themselves during the 'Iddah period unless this that they commit any open indecency (i.e. fornication, or theft, etc.). And these are the limits of Allah; and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah, indeed he has done wrong to himself. You do not know, maybe Allah will send a new command afterwards (so that you may take her back if that was the first or second divorce).

blocks.text: {یٰۤاَیُّهَا النَّبِیُّ اِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَآءَ فَطَلِّقُوْهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ: O Prophet! When you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed period.} The occasion of revelation of this verse is that Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Umar رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا divorced his wife during her menstrual period. The Sovereign of both worlds صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ commanded him to take her back. Then, if he wished to divorce her, he was to divorce her during the days of purity. Sahih Bukhari relates from Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Umar رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا that, during the blessed era of the Noble Prophet صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ, he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Sayyiduna Umar Farooq رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ asked the Noble Messenger صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ about it, and he said: “Command him to take her back so that she remains with him until she becomes pure, then menstruates and becomes pure again. Thereafter, if he wishes, he may keep her, and if he wishes, he may divorce her before touching her. This is the waiting period regarding which Allah Almighty has commanded that women be divorced in this manner.” (Bukhari, Book of Divorce, chapter on the saying of Allah Almighty: یایّہا النبی اذا طلّقتم النسائ۔۔۔ الخ, 3/478, hadith 5251)

blocks.text: Five religious rulings concerning divorce

runs.text: Five religious rulings concerning divorce

blocks.text: The following five religious rulings concerning divorcing women are noted here.

runs.text: The following five religious rulings concerning divorcing women are noted here.

blocks.text: 1. The women mentioned in this verse are those with whom their husbands have consummated the marriage and whose waiting period is calculated through menstruation. If such a woman is to be divorced, one divorce should be given during a period of purity in which intercourse has not taken place, and no revocation should be made until the waiting period ends. This is called Talaq-e-Ahsan.

blocks.text: 2. If a woman is divorced during menstruation, or during a period of purity in which intercourse took place, or if two or three divorces are given together or separately during one period of purity, even if intercourse did not take place in that period, all these forms are Talaq-e-Bid'at. Talaq-e-Bid'at is disliked, but it takes effect, and the person who gives such a divorce is sinful.

blocks.text: 3. Women who do not menstruate, such as a young girl, a pregnant woman, or an aged woman whose menstruation has stopped, are not included under the ruling of this verse.

blocks.text: 4. A woman with whom her husband has not consummated the marriage, and with whom he has not been alone in a way that intercourse could have taken place, has no waiting period. As for other women who do not menstruate, their waiting period is not calculated through menstruation.

Remember that both the man and woman will count the waiting period, but men are specifically addressed here because women often become heedless in this matter.

blocks.text: {لَا تُخْرِجُوْهُنَّ مِنْۢ بُیُوْتِهِنَّ: Do not remove them from their homes.} During the waiting period, do not remove women from their homes, nor should they leave their residence themselves. blocks.text: Five rulings concerning completing the waiting period at home

runs.text: Five rulings concerning completing the waiting period at home

blocks.text: 1. A woman must complete her waiting period in her husband's home. It is not permissible for the husband to remove a divorced woman during the waiting period, nor is it permissible for her to leave, because this residence is not merely the husband's right that can be waived with his consent; it is also a right established by the Shariah.

blocks.text: {لَا تَدْرِیْ: You do not know.} The person giving divorce is encouraged here to give a revocable divorce, meaning one divorce followed by separation. You do not know: perhaps after the divorce Allah Almighty will create affection for the woman in the husband's heart, he will regret his action and become inclined to revoke it. If he gave a revocable divorce, revocation will then be easy; or, if he gave fewer than three irrevocable divorces, he may return to her through a new marriage.

Hence, when they are about to reach their appointed term (nearing completion of 'Iddah), so hold them back with kindness or separate from them with kindness, and make two credible men amongst you as witnesses, and establish testimony for the sake of Allah; whosoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, he is advised with this; and whosoever fears Allah, Allah will create for him a way of salvation.

blocks.text: {فَاِذَا بَلَغْنَ اَجَلَهُنَّ: When they are about to reach their appointed term.} This verse explains the rulings concerning taking back a divorced woman. When the woman divorced according to the method described above approaches the end of her waiting period, you have a choice: if you wish to live with her in good companionship, take her back and do not intend to divorce her again; and if you do not hope to live with her properly, separate from her after paying what is due to her, such as her dower. Do not harm her by taking her back at the end of the waiting period and then divorcing her, thereby lengthening her waiting period and causing her distress. In both cases, whether taking her back or separating, appoint two just Muslims from among your people as witnesses, to remove accusations and prevent disputes. The witnesses should be legally acceptable, and their appointment should be for the sake of Allah Almighty, with no corrupt purpose besides establishing the truth and obeying Allah's command. This is the counsel given to one who believes in Allah Almighty and the Last Day: if he divorces according to the Sunnah, does not harm the woman observing her waiting period, does not remove her from her residence, and appoints Muslims as witnesses according to Allah's command, Allah Almighty will create a path of deliverance for him through which he will be freed from the troubles of this world and the Hereafter and protected from every difficulty and distress. (Madarik, At-Talaq, under verse 2, p. 1251, abridged)

blocks.text: Four rulings concerning taking back a divorced woman

runs.text: Four rulings concerning taking back a divorced woman

blocks.text: 1. Keeping a woman who has received a revocable divorce in the original marriage during the waiting period is called ruju, or taking her back.

items.text: Keeping a woman who has received a revocable divorce in the original marriage during the waiting period is called ruju, or taking her back.

runs.text: Keeping a woman who has received a revocable divorce in the original marriage during the waiting period is called ruju, or taking her back.

blocks.text: 2. The Sunnah method of ruju is to use words indicating that he has taken her back, appoint two just men as witnesses, and inform the woman so that she does not marry someone else after the waiting period. If she unknowingly marries another man after her husband has taken her back, she must be separated from the second man, even if he has consummated the marriage, because that marriage was invalid. If the husband says the words of ruju without appointing witnesses, or appoints witnesses without informing the woman, the ruju is valid but disliked and contrary to the Sunnah. If he takes her back through an action, such as intercourse or kissing her with desire, the ruju takes effect but is disliked; therefore, he should repeat the words of ruju before witnesses.

blocks.text: {وَ یَرْزُقْهُ مِنْ حَیْثُ لَا یَحْتَسِبُ: And He will provide him sustenance from where he could not imagine.} The final part of the preceding verse gave a glad tiding to the one who fears Allah Almighty. Here he is given a further glad tiding: Allah Almighty will provide him sustenance from a place he could not imagine. Whoever relies upon Allah Almighty and entrusts all his affairs to Him, Allah Almighty is sufficient for him in both worlds. Indeed, Allah Almighty completes His command and has appointed a measure for everything. Therefore, whether you rely upon Him or not, you will receive only what has been decreed; so why abandon reliance and deprive yourself of its reward? (Madarik, At-Talaq, under verse 3, pp. 1251–1252)

blocks.text: Encouragement to rely upon Allah

runs.text: Encouragement to rely upon Allah

blocks.text: This verse teaches that every Muslim should rely upon Allah Almighty and place trust in Him in all affairs. Sayyiduna Umar Farooq رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Messenger of Allah صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ said: “If you relied upon Allah as reliance upon Him truly requires, you would be given provision as birds are given provision: they leave hungry in the morning and return satiated in the evening.” (Tirmidhi, Book of Zuhd, chapter on reliance upon Allah, 4/154, hadith 2351)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And for those of your women who have no hope of menstruation, if you have any doubt (about the ruling of their waiting period), so their 'Iddah is three (lunar) months, and (three lunar months is) also for those who have not yet had menstruation; and the appointed period for the pregnant women is this that they deliver their burden (i.e. give birth). And whoever fears Allah, Allah will create ease for him in his matters.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

And whoever fears Allah, Allah will create ease for him in his matters.

blocks.text: {وَ اﻼ یَىٕسْنَ مِنَ الْمَحِیْضِ مِنْ نِّسَآىٕكُمْ: Those of your women who have no hope of menstruation.} The Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ asked the Noble Messenger صَلَّی اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ: “We know the waiting period of women who menstruate; what is the waiting period of those who do not menstruate?” This verse was revealed in response. It means: women whose menstruation has stopped because of old age, if there is any doubt concerning their ruling, know that their waiting period is three months. The same applies to those who have not yet menstruated because of their young age. The waiting period of pregnant women ends when they give birth. Whoever fears Allah Almighty, Allah Almighty creates ease for him in his affair. (Madarik, At-Talaq, under verse 4, p. 1252)

blocks.text: Four rulings concerning women who do not menstruate

runs.text: Four rulings concerning women who do not menstruate

blocks.text: 1. When menstruation stops because of old age, this is the age of menopause, and the waiting period of a woman who reaches this age is three months.

items.text: When menstruation stops because of old age, this is the age of menopause, and the waiting period of a woman who reaches this age is three months.

runs.text: When menstruation stops because of old age, this is the age of menopause, and the waiting period of a woman who reaches this age is three months.

blocks.text: 2. Whether a girl is a minor or has reached the age of maturity but menstruation has not yet begun, the waiting period of both is three months.

items.text: Whether a girl is a minor or has reached the age of maturity but menstruation has not yet begun, the waiting period of both is three months.

runs.text: Whether a girl is a minor or has reached the age of maturity but menstruation has not yet begun, the waiting period of both is three months.

blocks.text: 3. The waiting period of pregnant women is the delivery of the child, whether the waiting period follows divorce or the husband's passing away.

items.text: The waiting period of pregnant women is the delivery of the child, whether the waiting period follows divorce or the husband's passing away.

runs.text: The waiting period of pregnant women is the delivery of the child, whether the waiting period follows divorce or the husband's passing away.

blocks.text: 4. No particular duration is fixed for the waiting period ending with childbirth. Whenever the child is born after death or divorce, the waiting period ends, even if this occurs one minute later. Likewise, if a miscarriage occurs after the child's limbs have formed, the waiting period ends; if it occurs before the child's limbs have formed, the waiting period does not end.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: House the women (in 'Iddah) where you reside, according to your means, and do not harass them to make it difficult for them; and if they are pregnant, so give them provision till their child is born; then if they suckle the child for you, so pay them its due compensation; and consult with each other in a reasonable manner; and if you mutually find it difficult, so it is likely that another (woman) may be found to suckle him.

blocks.text: {اَسْكِنُوْهُنَّ مِنْ حَیْثُ سَكَنْتُمْ مِّنْ وُّجْدِكُمْ: House the women where you reside, according to your means.} This verse explains the rulings concerning a woman's residence during her waiting period, her expenses, and breastfeeding the child if she gives birth. Its summary is that divorced women should be housed where you live, according to your ability. Do not harm them by surrounding their dwelling and making it narrow, or by lodging an unsuitable person with them. Do not trouble them in a way that forces them to leave the home. If the divorced women are pregnant, continue spending on them according to the Shariah until they give birth, because their waiting period ends only at childbirth. If they breastfeed the child for you, pay them their due compensation. Consult one another properly about the payment, ensuring that neither the man falls short of the woman's right nor the woman becomes harsh in this matter. If you cannot settle the matter, for example because the mother demands more than another woman would receive and the father does not wish to pay more, then another woman may be arranged to breastfeed the child. (Madarik, At-Talaq, under verse 6, p. 1253; Khazin, At-Talaq, under verse 6, 4/280, excerpted)

blocks.text: Two rulings concerning residence and maintenance during the waiting period

runs.text: Two rulings concerning residence and maintenance during the waiting period

blocks.text: 1. It is obligatory for the husband to provide a divorced woman with a dwelling suitable to his means until her waiting period ends. It is also obligatory to provide her expenses during the waiting period.

blocks.text: 2. Just as maintenance is obligatory for a pregnant woman, it is obligatory for a non-pregnant woman as well, whether she received a revocable or an irrevocable divorce.

blocks.text: Rulings concerning breastfeeding a child

runs.text: Rulings concerning breastfeeding a child

blocks.text: 1. Breastfeeding a child is not ordinarily obligatory upon the mother; it is the father's responsibility to arrange breastfeeding by paying compensation. However, if the child will not drink the milk of any woman other than the mother, or if the father is poor, breastfeeding becomes obligatory upon the mother. While the child's mother remains in the father's marriage or observes the waiting period of a revocable divorce, she may not take payment for breastfeeding; after the waiting period, she may take payment.

blocks.text: {لِیُنْفِقْ ذُوْ سَعَةٍ مِّنْ سَعَتِهٖ: The one who has means should spend according to his means.} A person with financial means should spend according to his ability, while a person in difficulty should spend according to his condition on divorced women and women breastfeeding children. Allah Almighty places upon each person only the burden corresponding to the provision He has given him. A poor person should not fear spending; soon Allah Almighty will grant him ease after financial difficulty.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And (the people of) many a town rebelled against the command of their Lord and His Messengers; so, We took severe account from them and punished them with a horrible punishment.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
And (the people of) many a town rebelled against the command of their Lord and His Messengers; so, We took severe account from them and punished them with a horrible punishment.

blocks.text: {وَ كَاَیِّنْ مِّنْ قَرْیَةٍ: And how many a town there was.} This verse warns people against disobeying the commands of Allah Almighty. Its summary is that many townspeople rebelled against the command of their Lord and the commands of His Messengers عَلَیْہِمُ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام, so We took a severe account from them for their deeds and punished them with a terrible punishment. The severe account refers to the reckoning of the Hereafter. Since it will certainly occur, it is expressed in the past tense. The terrible punishment may refer to the punishment of Hell, or to worldly calamities such as famine and killing. (Ruh al-Bayan, At-Talaq, under verse 8, 10/39–40; Madarik, At-Talaq, under verse 8, p. 1254; Khazin, At-Talaq, under verse 8, 4/281–282, excerpted)

blocks.text: {فَذَاقَتْ وَبَالَ اَمْرِهَا: So they tasted the evil result of their doing.} The people of those towns tasted the consequence of their disbelief and rebellion through the severe account and terrible punishment. The outcome of their deeds was loss: they were deprived of benefit and afflicted by punishment. (Ruh al-Bayan, At-Talaq, under verse 9, 10/40)

blocks.text: Arabic: رَّسُوْلًا یَّتْلُوْا عَلَیْكُمْ اٰیٰتِ اللّٰهِ مُبَیِّنٰتٍ لِّیُخْرِ جَ الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْا وَ عَمِلُوا الصّٰلِحٰتِ مِنَ الظُّلُمٰتِ اِلَى النُّوْرِؕ-وَ مَنْ یُّؤْمِنْۢ بِاللّٰهِ وَ یَعْمَلْ صَالِحًا یُّدْخِلْهُ جَنّٰتٍ تَجْرِیْ مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْاَنْهٰرُ خٰلِدِیْنَ فِیْهَاۤ اَبَدًاؕ-قَدْ اَحْسَنَ اللّٰهُ لَهٗ رِزْقًا(11)

blocks.text: Arabic: اَللّٰهُ الَّذِیْ خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمٰوٰتٍ وَّ مِنَ الْاَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّؕ-یَتَنَزَّلُ الْاَمْرُ بَیْنَهُنَّ لِتَعْلَمُوْۤا اَنَّ اللّٰهَ عَلٰى كُلِّ شَیْءٍ قَدِیْرٌ ﳔ وَّ اَنَّ اللّٰهَ قَدْ اَحَاطَ بِكُلِّ شَیْءٍ عِلْمًا۠    (12)

runs.text: Arabic:

اَللّٰهُ الَّذِیْ خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمٰوٰتٍ وَّ مِنَ الْاَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّؕ-یَتَنَزَّلُ الْاَمْرُ بَیْنَهُنَّ لِتَعْلَمُوْۤا اَنَّ اللّٰهَ عَلٰى كُلِّ شَیْءٍ قَدِیْرٌ ﳔ وَّ اَنَّ اللّٰهَ قَدْ اَحَاطَ بِكُلِّ شَیْءٍ عِلْمًا۠    (12)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: It is Allah Who has created the seven heavens and the same number of earths as them; the command descends within them so that you may come to know that Allah can do all things and Allah's knowledge encompasses everything.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

It is Allah Who has created the seven heavens and the same number of earths as them; the command descends within them so that you may come to know that Allah can do all things and Allah's knowledge encompasses everything.

blocks.text: {اَللّٰهُ الَّذِیْ خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمٰوٰتٍ وَّ مِنَ الْاَرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ: Allah is He Who created seven heavens and the same number of earths.} Allah Almighty created seven heavens and seven earths through His perfect power. His command runs and takes effect throughout all of them, so that you may know that Allah Almighty has power over everything and that His knowledge encompasses everything. Therefore, bringing the dead to life and taking account of the entire creation are not difficult for Him. (Ruh al-Bayan, At-Talaq, under verse 12, 10/43; Madarik, At-Talaq, under verse 12, pp. 1254–1255, excerpted)

blocks.text: Arabic: یٰۤاَیُّهَا النَّبِیُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَاۤ اَحَلَّ اللّٰهُ لَكَۚ-تَبْتَغِیْ مَرْضَاتَ اَزْوَاجِكَؕ-وَ اللّٰهُ غَفُوْرٌ رَّحِیْمٌ(1)

runs.text: Arabic:
یٰۤاَیُّهَا النَّبِیُّ لِمَ تُحَرِّمُ مَاۤ اَحَلَّ اللّٰهُ لَكَۚ-تَبْتَغِیْ مَرْضَاتَ اَزْوَاجِكَؕ-وَ اللّٰهُ غَفُوْرٌ رَّحِیْمٌ(1)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O Conveyor of the unseen news (i.e. Prophet), why are you making unlawful for yourself that thing which Allah has made lawful for you; you wish to please (some of your) wives. And Allah is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

O Conveyor of the unseen news (i.e. Prophet), why are you making unlawful for yourself that thing which Allah has made lawful for you; you wish to please (some of your) wives. And Allah is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.

blocks.text: {یٰۤاَیُّهَا النَّبِیُّ: O Prophet!} Sayyidatuna Aishah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا states that the Noble Prophet ﷺ used to drink honey at the home of the Mother of the Believers, Sayyidatuna Zaynab bint Jahsh رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا, and would remain there somewhat longer. Sayyidatuna Hafsah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا and I agreed that whichever of us he ﷺ visited should say to him: “Have you eaten maghafir? I smell the odour of maghafir from your blessed mouth.” When this was said and the Noble Prophet ﷺ understood their intention, he ﷺ said: “No, but I drank honey at Zaynab bint Jahsh’s home. I shall never drink it again,” and he ﷺ swore this oath. He ﷺ also said, “Do not tell anyone about this.” (Bukhari, Book of Tafsir, Surah At-Tahrim, chapter “O Prophet, why do you make unlawful what Allah has made lawful for you?”, 3/359, hadith 4912.) This noble verse was revealed concerning this incident.

Sayyidatuna Hafsah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا and I agreed that whichever of us he ﷺ visited should say to him: “Have you eaten maghafir? I smell the odour of maghafir from your blessed mouth.” When this was said and the Noble Prophet ﷺ understood their intention, he ﷺ said: “No, but I drank honey at Zaynab bint Jahsh’s home. I shall never drink it again,” and he ﷺ swore this oath. He ﷺ also said, “Do not tell anyone about this.” (Bukhari, Book of Tafsir, Surah At-Tahrim, chapter “O Prophet, why do you make unlawful what Allah has made lawful for you?”, 3/359, hadith 4912.) This noble verse was revealed concerning this incident.

blocks.text: At the end of the verse, Allah Almighty states that He is Forgiving and Merciful. He forgave the shortcoming of these two blessed wives and prescribed expiation for the oath, thereby making the matter easy for the entire Ummah.

runs.text: At the end of the verse, Allah Almighty states that He is Forgiving and Merciful. He forgave the shortcoming of these two blessed wives and prescribed expiation for the oath, thereby making the matter easy for the entire Ummah.

blocks.text: Two points are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Two points are learned from this verse:

blocks.text:
1. When a person swears an oath, the thing concerning which he swore becomes unlawful for him in the sense that, if he uses it, expiation becomes necessary.
2. The Noble Prophet ﷺ declared honey unlawful for himself only to please his purified wives, not because of ignorance. The odour of something in one’s own mouth is not unseen; it is perceived. Therefore, misguided people cannot use this verse as evidence of ignorance on the part of the Radiant Prophet ﷺ.

blocks.text: Arabic: قَدْ فَرَضَ اللّٰهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ اَیْمَانِكُمْۚ-وَ اللّٰهُ مَوْلٰىكُمْۚ-وَ هُوَ الْعَلِیْمُ الْحَكِیْمُ(2)

runs.text: Arabic:
قَدْ فَرَضَ اللّٰهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ اَیْمَانِكُمْۚ-وَ اللّٰهُ مَوْلٰىكُمْۚ-وَ هُوَ الْعَلِیْمُ الْحَكِیْمُ(2)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Indeed, Allah has ordained expiation for you for your oaths; and Allah is your Master; and Allah is the All-Knowing, and the Wise.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
Indeed, Allah has ordained expiation for you for your oaths; and Allah is your Master; and Allah is the All-Knowing, and the Wise.

blocks.text: {قَدْ فَرَضَ اللّٰهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ اَیْمَانِكُمْ: Indeed, Allah has ordained expiation for you for your oaths.} “Undoing the oath” means that Allah Almighty has prescribed expiation for it. Thus, the Noble Prophet ﷺ could resume serving Sayyidatuna Mariyah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا or drink honey. According to some exegetes, undoing the oath means saying “if Allah wills” after making an oath, so that doing the contrary does not constitute breaking it.

runs.text: {قَدْ فَرَضَ اللّٰهُ لَكُمْ تَحِلَّةَ اَیْمَانِكُمْ: Indeed, Allah has ordained expiation for you for your oaths.} “Undoing the oath” means that Allah Almighty has prescribed expiation for it. Thus, the Noble Prophet ﷺ could resume serving Sayyidatuna Mariyah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا or drink honey. According to some exegetes, undoing the oath means saying “if Allah wills” after making an oath, so that doing the contrary does not constitute breaking it.

blocks.text: As to whether the Noble Prophet ﷺ offered expiation, it is narrated from Muqatil that the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ freed a slave as expiation for declaring Sayyidatuna Mariyah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا unlawful for himself. It is narrated from Sayyiduna Hasan رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ that the Radiant Prophet ﷺ did not offer expiation because he ﷺ is forgiven, while the command of expiation was given to teach the Ummah. (Madarik, At-Tahrim, under verse 2, pp. 1256–1257.)

It is narrated from Sayyiduna Hasan رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ that the Radiant Prophet ﷺ did not offer expiation because he ﷺ is forgiven, while the command of expiation was given to teach the Ummah. (Madarik, At-Tahrim, under verse 2, pp. 1256–1257.)

blocks.text: Two matters are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Two matters are learned from this verse:

blocks.text:
1. Declaring a lawful thing unlawful for oneself is also a type of oath. The reverse, declaring an unlawful thing lawful for oneself, is not an oath. For example, saying, “If I do this, my wife is unlawful for me,” is an oath, whereas saying, “If I do such-and-such, I will eat pork,” is not an oath.
2. Expiation for an oath exists only in this religion. It did not exist in earlier laws. Therefore, Allah Almighty did not command Sayyiduna Ayyub عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام to offer expiation; rather, He showed him a way to fulfil his oath by striking his wife with a broom.

blocks.text: {وَ اللّٰهُ مَوْلٰىكُمْ: And Allah is your Master.} This means: O my Beloved and his household, Allah Almighty is your Helper. Therefore, He Himself manages your household and teaches you its manners. He knows your interests and is Wise in His acts and commands. He commands and forbids you only according to your strength. (Nur-ul-Irfan, At-Tahrim, under verse 2, p. 894; Ruh-ul-Bayan, At-Tahrim, under verse 2, 10/50, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Arabic: وَ اِذْ اَسَرَّ النَّبِیُّ اِلٰى بَعْضِ اَزْوَاجِهٖ حَدِیْثًاۚ-فَلَمَّا نَبَّاَتْ بِهٖ وَ اَظْهَرَهُ اللّٰهُ عَلَیْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهٗ وَ اَعْرَضَ عَنْۢ بَعْضٍۚ-فَلَمَّا نَبَّاَهَا بِهٖ قَالَتْ مَنْ اَنْۢبَاَكَ هٰذَاؕ-قَالَ نَبَّاَنِیَ الْعَلِیْمُ الْخَبِیْرُ(3)

runs.text: Arabic:

وَ اِذْ اَسَرَّ النَّبِیُّ اِلٰى بَعْضِ اَزْوَاجِهٖ حَدِیْثًاۚ-فَلَمَّا نَبَّاَتْ بِهٖ وَ اَظْهَرَهُ اللّٰهُ عَلَیْهِ عَرَّفَ بَعْضَهٗ وَ اَعْرَضَ عَنْۢ بَعْضٍۚ-فَلَمَّا نَبَّاَهَا بِهٖ قَالَتْ مَنْ اَنْۢبَاَكَ هٰذَاؕ-قَالَ نَبَّاَنِیَ الْعَلِیْمُ الْخَبِیْرُ(3)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And when the Prophet (Muhammad) disclosed a matter in confidence to one of his wives, then when she happened to mention it and Allah made it known to the Prophet, so the Prophet told her part of it and held back a part; then when the Prophet informed her about it (i.e. disclosing the secret), she said, 'Who informed your respected self?' He said, 'The All-Knowing, the All-Aware has informed me.'

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

And when the Prophet (Muhammad) disclosed a matter in confidence to one of his wives, then when she happened to mention it and Allah made it known to the Prophet, so the Prophet told her part of it and held back a part; then when the Prophet informed her about it (i.e. disclosing the secret), she said, 'Who informed your respected self?' He said, 'The All-Knowing, the All-Aware has informed me.'

blocks.text: {وَ اِذْ اَسَرَّ النَّبِیُّ اِلٰى بَعْضِ اَزْوَاجِهٖ حَدِیْثًا: And when the Prophet disclosed a matter in confidence to one of his wives.} The summary of the incident mentioned here is that the Noble Prophet ﷺ told his wife, Sayyidatuna Hafsah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا, a secret consisting of two matters and instructed her not to disclose it. She then informed Sayyidatuna Aishah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا of it. Allah Almighty made her action known to His Beloved ﷺ through the words of Sayyiduna Jibra'il عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام. The Noble Prophet ﷺ mentioned one of the two matters to Sayyidatuna Hafsah, telling her that she had disclosed it, but did not mention the other. This was an expression of his ﷺ noble character: he ﷺ overlooked one matter instead of taking her to task. When he ﷺ informed her of it, she asked, “Who told you?” He ﷺ replied, “The All-Knowing, All-Aware Allah Almighty told me, from whom nothing is hidden.” (Khazin, At-Tahrim, under verse 3, 4/284–285; Madarik, At-Tahrim, under verse 3, p. 1257, excerpted.)

runs.text: {وَ اِذْ اَسَرَّ النَّبِیُّ اِلٰى بَعْضِ اَزْوَاجِهٖ حَدِیْثًا: And when the Prophet disclosed a matter in confidence to one of his wives.} The summary of the incident mentioned here is that the Noble Prophet ﷺ told his wife, Sayyidatuna Hafsah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا, a secret consisting of two matters and instructed her not to disclose it. She then informed Sayyidatuna Aishah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا of it. Allah Almighty made her action known to His Beloved ﷺ through the words of Sayyiduna Jibra'il عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام. The Noble Prophet ﷺ mentioned one of the two matters to Sayyidatuna Hafsah, telling her that she had disclosed it, but did not mention the other. This was an expression of his ﷺ noble character: he ﷺ overlooked one matter instead of taking her to task. When he ﷺ informed her of it, she asked, “Who told you?” He ﷺ replied, “The All-Knowing, All-Aware Allah Almighty told me, from whom nothing is hidden.” (Khazin, At-Tahrim, under verse 3, 4/284–285; Madarik, At-Tahrim, under verse 3, p. 1257, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Three matters concerning this verse are also worth noting:

runs.text: Three matters concerning this verse are also worth noting:

blocks.text:
1. Although Sayyiduna Jibra'il عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام is included among the angels, he is mentioned separately because he is the leader of all the angels.
2. The Noble Prophet ﷺ is the helper of the Muslims like a king is the helper of his subjects, while believers are helpers of the Noble Prophet ﷺ like servants and soldiers are helpers of a king. Therefore, this verse cannot be used to say that the Radiant Prophet ﷺ is dependent upon Muslims.
3. Sayyiduna Jibra'il عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام and righteous Muslims are called masters, meaning helpers, while the angels are called supporters. This proves that the servants of Allah Almighty are helpers. Wherever help from other than Allah is negated, real and independent help is intended; thus, there is no contradiction between the verses.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: If he divorces you, it is close that his Lord will give him wives better than you in your place; submissive, believing, obedient, repenting, worshiping, fasting, widows and virgins.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {اِنْ طَلَّقَكُنَّ: If he divorces you.} O the wives of my Beloved ﷺ, if he divorces you, his Lord is powerful enough to grant him wives better than you: women obedient to Allah Almighty, sincere in believing in His Oneness, obedient to Allah Almighty and His Messenger ﷺ and desirous of their pleasure, frequently repentant, devoted to worship, fasting, widowed and virgin. (Tafsir Kabir, At-Tahrim, under verse 5, 10/571; Khazin, At-Tahrim, under verse 5, 4/286; Madarik, At-Tahrim, under verse 5, pp. 1257–1258, excerpted.)

blocks.text: In saying this, the purified wives were in fact warned that if they hurt the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ and he ﷺ divorced them, Allah Almighty would grant him ﷺ better wives through His grace and kindness. They were affected by this warning, considered the honour of serving the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ greater than every blessing, and placed his ﷺ comfort and pleasure first. Therefore, he ﷺ did not divorce them. (Khazain-ul-Irfan, At-Tahrim, under verse 5, p. 1037, abridged.)

blocks.text: Qualities of a Good Wife

runs.text: Qualities of a Good Wife

blocks.text: This verse teaches that a good wife obeys Allah Almighty and His Beloved ﷺ, obeys her husband, worships Allah and avoids sins, even if she is poor. Thus, when choosing a wife, one should not look only at beauty and wealth; her religious commitment should be considered and given preference.

blocks.text: Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A woman is married for four reasons: wealth, family status, beauty and religion. Give preference to the religious woman.” (Bukhari, Book of Marriage, chapter on compatibility in religion, 3/429, hadith 5090.)

blocks.text: Sayyiduna Anas ibn Malik رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Crown of Messengership ﷺ said: “Whoever marries a woman because of her honour, Allah Almighty will increase his disgrace; whoever marries her because of her wealth, Allah Almighty will only increase his poverty; whoever marries her because of her lineage, He will increase his lowliness. But whoever marries so that he does not look elsewhere, so that he may remain chaste, or in order to maintain family ties, Allah Almighty will place blessing in that woman for the man and in that man for the woman.” (Al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, chapter alif, Ibrahim, 2/18, hadith 2342.)

blocks.text: Islamic Education of One’s Family Is Obligatory

runs.text: Islamic Education of One’s Family Is Obligatory

blocks.text: This verse teaches that just as a Muslim must reform himself, he must also provide Islamic education and upbringing to his family. Every Muslim should teach and remind his wife, children and all those under his care of Islamic commands and raise them under Islamic teachings so that they too remain safe from the Fire of Hell.

blocks.text: Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Umar رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا narrates that the Crown of Messengership ﷺ said: “Every one of you is a guardian, and every one of you will be questioned about those under your care. A woman is a guardian in her husband’s home and will be questioned about it. A servant is a guardian over his master’s property and will be questioned about it. A man is a guardian over his father’s property and will be questioned about it. In short, every one of you is a guardian and will be questioned about those under your care.” (Bukhari, Book of Friday, chapter on Friday in villages and cities, 1/309, hadith 893.)

blocks.text: A Soul Fled Out of Fear of Hell

runs.text: A Soul Fled Out of Fear of Hell

blocks.text: Sayyiduna Mansur ibn Ammar رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ relates: I performed Hajj and stayed at an inn in Kufah during the journey. One dark night, I went outside and, at midnight, heard a voice full of pain saying: “O Allah Almighty, by Your honour and majesty, I did not knowingly disobey and oppose You. Whenever I disobeyed You, I was not unaware of it, but my misfortune helped me to err, and hope in Your concealment of faults encouraged me to sin. I disobeyed and opposed You because of my ignorance. Who will save me from Your punishment now? If You cut off the rope of Your mercy and grace from me, whose rope will I hold?”

runs.text: Sayyiduna Mansur ibn Ammar رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ relates: I performed Hajj and stayed at an inn in Kufah during the journey. One dark night, I went outside and, at midnight, heard a voice full of pain saying: “O Allah Almighty, by Your honour and majesty, I did not knowingly disobey and oppose You. Whenever I disobeyed You, I was not unaware of it, but my misfortune helped me to err, and hope in Your concealment of faults encouraged me to sin. I disobeyed and opposed You because of my ignorance. Who will save me from Your punishment now? If You cut off the rope of Your mercy and grace from me, whose rope will I hold?”

blocks.text: When he finished supplicating, I recited this verse of the Holy Quran:

runs.text: When he finished supplicating, I recited this verse of the Holy Quran:

blocks.text: “قُوْۤا اَنْفُسَكُمْ وَ اَهْلِیْكُمْ نَارًا وَّ قُوْدُهَا النَّاسُ وَ الْحِجَارَةُ عَلَیْهَا مَلٰٓىٕكَةٌ غِلَاظٌ شِدَادٌ لَّا یَعْصُوْنَ اللّٰهَ مَاۤ اَمَرَهُمْ وَ یَفْعَلُوْنَ مَا یُؤْمَرُوْنَ”

runs.text: “قُوْۤا اَنْفُسَكُمْ وَ اَهْلِیْكُمْ نَارًا وَّ قُوْدُهَا النَّاسُ وَ الْحِجَارَةُ عَلَیْهَا مَلٰٓىٕكَةٌ غِلَاظٌ شِدَادٌ لَّا یَعْصُوْنَ اللّٰهَ مَاۤ اَمَرَهُمْ وَ یَفْعَلُوْنَ مَا یُؤْمَرُوْنَ”

blocks.text: I then heard a violent movement, after which there was no further sound. The next day, when I returned to my lodging, I saw a bier. An old woman who did not know me told me that a man had passed by during the night while her son was praying. The man recited a Quranic verse, and upon hearing it her son had passed away. (Mustadrak, Book of Tafsir, interpretation of Surah At-Tahrim, another account concerning fear of Allah Almighty, 3/318, hadith 3882.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O believers! Repent to Allah with such repentance which becomes advice for the future; it is close that your Lord may remove your sins and admit you into Gardens beneath which rivers flow on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and the believers along with him; their light will be running ahead of them and (running) on their right; they will submit, 'O our Lord, complete our light for us, and forgive us; indeed, You have power over all things.'

blocks.text: Encouragement to Repent Sincerely

runs.text: Encouragement to Repent Sincerely

blocks.text: In the present age, committing sins has become extremely easy, while avoiding them and performing good deeds has become difficult. Every Muslim should therefore strive fully to avoid sins and perform good deeds, and should sincerely repent of sins already committed. Sincere repentance erases sins from a person’s record. Allah Almighty states:

runs.text: In the present age, committing sins has become extremely easy, while avoiding them and performing good deeds has become difficult. Every Muslim should therefore strive fully to avoid sins and perform good deeds, and should sincerely repent of sins already committed. Sincere repentance erases sins from a person’s record. Allah Almighty states:

blocks.text: Sayyiduna Anas رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Messenger ﷺ said: “When a servant repents from his sins, Allah Almighty makes the recording angels forget his sins, makes his limbs forget them, and erases their traces from the earth. blocks.text: May Allah Almighty grant us the ability to sincerely repent of previous sins and continue avoiding future sins. Ameen.

blocks.text: Five matters are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Five matters are learned from this verse:

blocks.text:
1. Repentance is a means of forgiveness and of becoming deserving of Paradise.
2. A pious believer will be with the Noble Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Judgement.
3. The Day of Judgement will be a day of honour for the Noble Prophet ﷺ and those with him, and a day of disgrace for the disbelievers.
4. Although a believer may be sinful, he will, if Allah wills, remain safe from disgrace in the Hereafter. Even if he is punished, he will not be disgraced.
5. At first, the hypocrites will have light on the Bridge, but when they reach its middle, their light will be extinguished.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Allah explains the example of the disbelievers; the wife of Nooh and the wife of Loot; they were bound in marriage to two of Our bondsmen deserving Our closeness, then they (i.e. the wives of these Prophets) betrayed them, so they (both) did not benefit from them (i.e. these two Prophets) against (the punishment of) Allah in the least. And it was stated that 'Both of you women enter Hell along with others who enter (Hell).'

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

Allah explains the example of the disbelievers; the wife of Nooh and the wife of Loot; they were bound in marriage to two of Our bondsmen deserving Our closeness, then they (i.e. the wives of these Prophets) betrayed them, so they (both) did not benefit from them (i.e. these two Prophets) against (the punishment of) Allah in the least. And it was stated that 'Both of you women enter Hell along with others who enter (Hell).'

blocks.text: {ضَرَبَ اللّٰهُ مَثَلًا لِّلَّذِیْنَ كَفَرُوا امْرَاَتَ نُوْحٍ وَّ امْرَاَتَ لُوْطٍ: Allah explains the example of the disbelievers: the wife of Nooh and the wife of Loot.} Allah Almighty presents the wives of Sayyiduna Nooh and Sayyiduna Loot عَلَیْہِمَا الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام as examples for the disbelievers. They were married to two righteous, close servants of Allah, but they committed treachery in the matter of religion by choosing disbelief. Those two honoured servants could not benefit them at all before Allah Almighty. At their death, or on the Day of Judgement, they will be told: “Enter Hell with the disbelievers of your peoples.” Their marital relationship with the Prophets عَلَیْہِمُ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام did not remain beneficial because of their disbelief. Likewise, O disbelievers of Makkah, your relationship with my Beloved ﷺ will not benefit you while you remain in disbelief. (Madarik, At-Tahrim, under verse 10, p. 1259; Khazin, At-Tahrim, under verse 10, 4/288, excerpted.)

blocks.text: The name of Sayyiduna Nooh’s wife was Wahilah. She used to tell her people that Sayyiduna Nooh عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام was insane. The name of Sayyiduna Loot’s wife was Wa'ilah, and she concealed her hypocrisy. (Khazin, At-Tahrim, under verse 10, 4/288.)

blocks.text: This verse teaches that the companionship of the pious will not benefit a person in the Hereafter without faith. It also teaches that a prophet’s relationship or lineage does not benefit a disbeliever, and that on the Day of Judgement every person will be with the one whom he loved in the world.

blocks.text: Arabic: وَ ضَرَبَ اللّٰهُ مَثَلًا لِّلَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوا امْرَاَتَ فِرْعَوْنَۘ-اِذْ قَالَتْ رَبِّ ابْنِ لِیْ عِنْدَكَ بَیْتًا فِی الْجَنَّةِ وَ نَجِّنِیْ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَ عَمَلِهٖ وَ نَجِّنِیْ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظّٰلِمِیْنَۙ    (11)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And Allah explains an example of the Muslims; the wife of Fir'awn; when she prayed, 'O my Lord! Build a house for me in Your closeness in Paradise, and rescue me from Fir'awn and his actions, and rescue me from the unjust people.'

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

And Allah explains an example of the Muslims; the wife of Fir'awn; when she prayed, 'O my Lord! Build a house for me in Your closeness in Paradise, and rescue me from Fir'awn and his actions, and rescue me from the unjust people.'

blocks.text: {وَ ضَرَبَ اللّٰهُ مَثَلًا لِّلَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوا امْرَاَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ: And Allah explains an example of the Muslims: the wife of Fir'awn.} The previous verse gave an example for disbelievers; this verse gives an example for Muslims, showing that another person’s sin does not harm them.

runs.text: {وَ ضَرَبَ اللّٰهُ مَثَلًا لِّلَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوا امْرَاَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ: And Allah explains an example of the Muslims: the wife of Fir'awn.} The previous verse gave an example for disbelievers; this verse gives an example for Muslims, showing that another person’s sin does not harm them.

blocks.text: When Sayyiduna Musa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام defeated the magicians, Fir'awn’s wife, Sayyidatuna Asiyah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا, accepted faith in him. When Fir'awn learned of this, he severely punished her, had her hands and feet tied to four stakes, placed a heavy millstone on her chest and left her in the intense heat. When his cruelty increased, Sayyidatuna Asiyah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا supplicated: “O my Lord, build a house for me with You in Paradise.” Allah Almighty showed her the house prepared for her in Paradise, and the joy of seeing it made Fir'awn’s cruelty easy for her to bear. She then supplicated: “Save me from Fir'awn, his disbelief, polytheism and oppression, and save me from the oppressive people who follow Fir'awn’s religion.” Her supplication was accepted, and Allah Almighty took her soul. Thus, just as Fir'awn’s disbelief did not harm Sayyidatuna Asiyah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا or cause her punishment, the disbelief of their relatives will not harm Muslims or cause them to be punished. (Khazin, At-Tahrim, under verse 11, 4/288; Jalalayn, At-Tahrim, under verse 11, p. 466, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Three matters are learned from the words “When she said, ‘My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise’”:

runs.text: Three matters are learned from the words “When she said, ‘My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise’”:

blocks.text:
1. The house in Paradise is of a higher rank when the servant has greater closeness to Allah Almighty.
2. Out of love for Allah Almighty and longing to meet Him, it is permissible to desire and supplicate for death.
3. Seeking refuge with Allah Almighty, supplicating before Him and asking Him for relief from difficulties and calamities is the way of the righteous.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And (the example) of Maryam; the daughter of 'Imraan who guarded her chastity, We henceforth breathed into her (through Jibra'eel) a spirit from Ourselves, and she testified the Words of her Lord and His Books, and was amongst the obedient.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

And (the example) of Maryam; the daughter of 'Imraan who guarded her chastity, We henceforth breathed into her (through Jibra'eel) a spirit from Ourselves, and she testified the Words of her Lord and His Books, and was amongst the obedient.

blocks.text: {وَ مَرْیَمَ ابْنَتَ عِمْرٰنَ الَّتِیْۤ اَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا: And the example of Maryam, daughter of Imraan, who guarded her chastity.} The previous verse presented an example of a woman who had a husband; this verse presents an example of a woman who did not. Allah Almighty presented Sayyidatuna Maryam رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا, daughter of Sayyiduna Imraan رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, as an example. She protected her chastity and no man touched her. Allah Almighty breathed into her, through Sayyiduna Jibra'il عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام, a spirit from Himself. She confirmed the words of her Lord and His Books and was among the obedient. “The words of her Lord” means the religious commands Allah Almighty prescribed for His servants, while “His Books” means the Books revealed to the noble Prophets عَلَیْہِمُ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام. (Ruh-ul-Bayan, At-Tahrim, under verse 12, 10/70; Khazin, At-Tahrim, under verse 12, 4/288; Madarik, At-Tahrim, under verse 12, p. 1259, excerpted.)

blocks.text: The Excellence of Sayyidatuna Maryam رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا

runs.text: The Excellence of Sayyidatuna Maryam رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا

blocks.text: Sayyidatuna Maryam رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا has the distinction that, apart from her, no woman’s name is mentioned in the Holy Quran. She will also have the distinction of being among the wives of the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ in Paradise. The Radiant Prophet ﷺ counted her among the perfect women. Sayyiduna Abu Musa Ashari رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “Many men attained perfection, while among women, Asiyah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا and Maryam bint Imraan رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا attained perfection. The excellence of Aishah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا over women is like the excellence of tharid over all foods.” (Bukhari, Book of the Stories of the Prophets, chapter on the statement of Allah Almighty “And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Fir'awn,” 2/445, hadith 3411.)

The excellence of Aishah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا over women is like the excellence of tharid over all foods.” (Bukhari, Book of the Stories of the Prophets, chapter on the statement of Allah Almighty “And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Fir'awn,” 2/445, hadith 3411.)

blocks.text: Three matters are learned from the words “We breathed into her a spirit from Ourselves”:

runs.text: Three matters are learned from the words “We breathed into her a spirit from Ourselves”:

blocks.text:
1. Sayyiduna Jibra'il عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام blew, yet Allah Almighty said, “We breathed.” This proves that the action of the accepted servants of Allah Almighty is, in reality, Allah Almighty’s action.
2. Blowing for the purpose of conveying benefit is the practice of angels. This noble verse is the basis of the blowing and prayers of the spiritual guides, and blowing is also established by many sound hadith.
3. Sayyiduna Isa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام is called Ruhullah because his birth occurred through the blowing of Ruh-ul-Amin.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O believers! Do not befriend My enemies and your enemies, you inform them (about your secrets) out of friendship; whereas, they deny that truth which has come to you. It is they who separate the Messenger and you from your homes on this basis that you believed in your Lord Allah. If you have come out to fight in My path and to gain My contentment, so do not befriend them. You send them secret messages of friendship, and I know well what you hide and what you disclose. And whoever amongst you does this, he has indeed gone astray from the straight path.

blocks.text: The summary of the verse is: O believers! Do not befriend the disbelievers who are My enemies and your enemies. Because of friendship, you convey the hidden news of the Noble Messenger ﷺ to them, although they deny the truth that has come to you, namely Islam and the Holy Quran. They expel the Noble Messenger ﷺ and you from Makkah because you believe in your Lord, Allah Almighty. If you left your homeland to strive in My path and seek My pleasure, then do not befriend these disbelievers. You send them secret messages of love, although you know well that I know everything you conceal and everything you reveal. Remember that whoever among you befriends them has certainly strayed from the straight path. (Madarik, Surah Al-Mumtahanah, p. 1230; Khazin, under verse 1, 4/255–256, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Lessons from “O believers! Do not befriend My enemies and your enemies”

runs.text: Lessons from “O believers! Do not befriend My enemies and your enemies”

blocks.text: Five matters are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Five matters are learned from this verse:

blocks.text:
1. The disbelievers of Makkah were enemies of the Muslims, but Allah Almighty also called them His enemies. This shows that the enemy of Allah Almighty’s righteous servants is also the enemy of Allah Almighty.
2. Informing disbelievers of the Muslims’ secrets is treachery and rebellion against the religion and the nation.
3. A sin was committed by Sayyiduna Hatib رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, yet Allah Almighty called him a believer. This shows that committing a major sin does not make a person a disbeliever.
4. The enemy of faith is more dangerous than the enemy of one’s life.
5. Striving in the way of Allah Almighty is possible only when the heart of the fighter is filled with love for believers and enmity for disbelievers. If even a little inclination towards a disbeliever enters the fighter’s heart, remaining a fighter in the way of Allah becomes difficult.

blocks.text: The virtues of friendship and enmity for Allah Almighty’s pleasure

runs.text: The virtues of friendship and enmity for Allah Almighty’s pleasure

blocks.text:
1. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “On the Day of Judgement, Allah Almighty will say: ‘Where are those who loved one another for the sake of My Majesty? Today I shall place them under My shade, on the day when there is no shade besides the shade of My Throne.’” (Muslim, Book of Righteousness, Maintaining Relations and Good Manners, chapter on the virtue of love for Allah, p. 1388, hadith 37 (2566).)
2. Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “A man went to another region to meet his brother. Allah Almighty placed an angel on his path. When he came to the angel, he asked, ‘Where do you intend to go?’ He replied, ‘I have a brother in this region whom I am going to visit.’ The angel asked, ‘Do you have a favour over him which you are going to collect?’ He replied, ‘No. I only love him for Allah Almighty’s sake.’ The angel said, ‘Allah Almighty sent me to you to inform you that He loves you just as you loved him for Allah Almighty’s sake.’” (Muslim, Book of Righteousness, Maintaining Relations and Good Manners, chapter on the virtue of love for Allah, p. 1388, hadith 38 (2567).)
3. Sayyiduna Abu Umamah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever loves someone for Allah Almighty, bears enmity towards someone for Allah Almighty, gives for Allah Almighty and withholds for Allah Almighty has perfected his faith.” (Abu Dawud, Book of Sunnah, chapter on evidence for increase and decrease of faith, 4/290, hadith 4681.)
4. Sayyiduna Abu Dharr رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ narrates that the Noble Messenger ﷺ said: “Do you know which deed is most beloved to Allah Almighty?” Someone said, “Prayer and zakat,” and someone said, “Striving.” The Radiant Prophet ﷺ said: “The deed most beloved to Allah Almighty is love and hatred for Allah Almighty.” (Musnad Imam Ahmad, Musnad of the Ansar, hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, 8/68, hadith 21361.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: If they find you, so they will be your (open) enemies and will extend their hands and their tongues towards you with evil, and their wish is that somehow you become disbelievers.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
If they find you, so they will be your (open) enemies and will extend their hands and their tongues towards you with evil, and their wish is that somehow you become disbelievers.

blocks.text: {اِنْ یَّثْقَفُوْكُمْ یَكُوْنُوْا لَكُمْ اَعْدَآءً: If they find you, they will be your enemies.} The enmity of the disbelievers is such that no matter how you deal with them, whenever they find an opportunity they will not reduce their hostility towards you. They will extend their hands towards you to beat and kill you, and extend their tongues by abusing and insulting you. Their wish is that somehow you become disbelievers. Therefore, such people should never be befriended, goodness should not be expected from them, and their enmity should not be overlooked. (Khazin, Al-Mumtahanah, under verse 2, 4/256; Madarik, Al-Mumtahanah, under verse 2, p. 1231, excerpted.)

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

Neither your relations nor your offspring (left behind in Makkah because of whose safety, you keep friendship with the disbelievers) will ever benefit you, on the Day of Judgement. (Allah) will separate you from them; and Allah is seeing your deeds.

blocks.text: {لَنْ تَنْفَعَكُمْ اَرْحَامُكُمْ وَ لَاۤ اَوْلَادُكُمْۚۛ-یَوْمَ الْقِیٰمَةِ: Neither your relations nor your offspring will benefit you on the Day of Judgement.} O believers! The relatives and children because of whom you befriend the disbelievers and maintain relations of affection will never benefit you on the Day of Judgement. Allah Almighty will separate you from them on that day: the obedient will be in Paradise and the disbelieving disobedient in Hell. Remember that Allah Almighty sees your deeds and will reward you according to them. (Khazin, Al-Mumtahanah, under verse 3, 4/257; Madarik, Al-Mumtahanah, under verse 3, p. 1231–1232, excerpted.)

The relatives and children because of whom you befriend the disbelievers and maintain relations of affection will never benefit you on the Day of Judgement. Allah Almighty will separate you from them on that day: the obedient will be in Paradise and the disbelieving disobedient in Hell. blocks.text: Arabic: قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ اُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ فِیْۤ اِبْرٰهِیْمَ وَ الَّذِیْنَ مَعَهٗۚ-اِذْ قَالُوْا لِقَوْمِهِمْ اِنَّا بُرَءٰٓؤُا مِنْكُمْ وَ مِمَّا تَعْبُدُوْنَ مِنْ دُوْنِ اللّٰهِ٘-كَفَرْنَا بِكُمْ وَ بَدَا بَیْنَنَا وَ بَیْنَكُمُ الْعَدَاوَةُ وَ الْبَغْضَآءُ اَبَدًا حَتّٰى تُؤْمِنُوْا بِاللّٰهِ وَحْدَهٗۤ اِلَّا قَوْلَ اِبْرٰهِیْمَ لِاَبِیْهِ لَاَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ وَ مَاۤ اَمْلِكُ لَكَ مِنَ اللّٰهِ مِنْ شَیْءٍؕ-رَبَّنَا عَلَیْكَ تَوَكَّلْنَا وَ اِلَیْكَ اَنَبْنَا وَ اِلَیْكَ الْمَصِیْرُ(4)

runs.text: Arabic:

قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ اُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ فِیْۤ اِبْرٰهِیْمَ وَ الَّذِیْنَ مَعَهٗۚ-اِذْ قَالُوْا لِقَوْمِهِمْ اِنَّا بُرَءٰٓؤُا مِنْكُمْ وَ مِمَّا تَعْبُدُوْنَ مِنْ دُوْنِ اللّٰهِ٘-كَفَرْنَا بِكُمْ وَ بَدَا بَیْنَنَا وَ بَیْنَكُمُ الْعَدَاوَةُ وَ الْبَغْضَآءُ اَبَدًا حَتّٰى تُؤْمِنُوْا بِاللّٰهِ وَحْدَهٗۤ اِلَّا قَوْلَ اِبْرٰهِیْمَ لِاَبِیْهِ لَاَسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ وَ مَاۤ اَمْلِكُ لَكَ مِنَ اللّٰهِ مِنْ شَیْءٍؕ-رَبَّنَا عَلَیْكَ تَوَكَّلْنَا وَ اِلَیْكَ اَنَبْنَا وَ اِلَیْكَ الْمَصِیْرُ(4)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Indeed, there was a good example for you to follow in Ibrahim and those with him, when they said to their people 'Indeed, we are disgusted with you and what you worship other than Allah. We have rejected you, and enmity and hatred has surfaced between us and you forever until you accept faith in the One Allah.' Except for the saying of Ibrahim to his (figurative) father, 'I will definitely seek forgiveness for you. And I do not possess any power to benefit you against Allah.' (Ibrahim and his followers said) 'O our Lord, we have relied upon only You, and only towards You we have turned and only towards You is the (final) return.'

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

Indeed, there was a good example for you to follow in Ibrahim and those with him, when they said to their people 'Indeed, we are disgusted with you and what you worship other than Allah. blocks.text: {قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ اُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ فِیْۤ اِبْرٰهِیْمَ وَ الَّذِیْنَ مَعَهٗ: Indeed, there was a good example for you to follow in Ibrahim and those with him.} This verse addresses Sayyiduna Hatib رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ and the other believers, commanding all of them to follow Sayyiduna Ibrahim عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام in matters of religion, including his manner with relatives. The meaning is that the life of Sayyiduna Ibrahim عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام and those who believed in him contained an excellent example: they said to their polytheist people, “We are free from you and from the idols you worship besides Allah Almighty. We reject your religion, and enmity and hatred have appeared between us and you forever until you believe in Allah Almighty alone.”

runs.text: {قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ اُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ فِیْۤ اِبْرٰهِیْمَ وَ الَّذِیْنَ مَعَهٗ: Indeed, there was a good example for you to follow in Ibrahim and those with him.} This verse addresses Sayyiduna Hatib رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ and the other believers, commanding all of them to follow Sayyiduna Ibrahim عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام in matters of religion, including his manner with relatives. The meaning is that the life of Sayyiduna Ibrahim عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام and those who believed in him contained an excellent example: they said to their polytheist people, “We are free from you and from the idols you worship besides Allah Almighty. We reject your religion, and enmity and hatred have appeared between us and you forever until you believe in Allah Almighty alone.”

blocks.text: However, the statement of Sayyiduna Ibrahim عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام to his figurative father, “I shall certainly seek forgiveness for you,” is not an example to follow. It was based on a promise; when it became clear to him that his father would remain upon disbelief, he expressed his disassociation from him. Therefore, it is not permissible for anyone to seek forgiveness for a disbelieving relative. (Khazin, Al-Mumtahanah, under verse 4, 4/257; Madarik, under verse 4, p. 1232, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Note: Muslims must follow the Noble Prophet ﷺ absolutely, whereas following the other noble Prophets عَلَیْہِمُ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام concerns particular deeds, because many rulings of the laws of earlier Prophets were abrogated. Thus this verse does not oppose the verse of Surah Al-Ahzab, “لَقَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ فِیْ رَسُوْلِ اللّٰهِ اُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ”. Here, following is commanded in particular circumstances and particular matters, while the verse of Surah Al-Ahzab commands absolute following.

runs.text: Lessons from “Indeed, there was a good example for you to follow in Ibrahim”

blocks.text: Three matters are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Three matters are learned from this verse:

blocks.text:
1. The practice of the noble Prophets عَلَیْہِمُ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام is to make their faith apparent through their words and deeds.
2. Enmity towards disbelievers is as necessary as love for Muslims.
3. By Allah Almighty’s permission, the noble Prophets عَلَیْہِمُ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام will remove punishment from sinful believers, and punishment will be removed through their intercession. Therefore, this verse cannot be used as evidence that there is no intercession for believers.

blocks.text: {عَسَى اللّٰهُ اَنْ یَّجْعَلَ بَیْنَكُمْ وَ بَیْنَ الَّذِیْنَ عَادَیْتُمْ مِّنْهُمْ مَّوَدَّةً: It is near that Allah may create friendship between you and those amongst them who are your enemies.} Occasion of revelation: When the preceding verses were revealed, the Companions became very severe in their enmity towards their relatives and dear ones and became completely disassociated from them. Allah Almighty then revealed this verse, giving them hope that the condition of those disbelievers would change.

runs.text: {عَسَى اللّٰهُ اَنْ یَّجْعَلَ بَیْنَكُمْ وَ بَیْنَ الَّذِیْنَ عَادَیْتُمْ مِّنْهُمْ مَّوَدَّةً: It is near that Allah may create friendship between you and those amongst them who are your enemies.} Occasion of revelation: When the preceding verses were revealed, the Companions became very severe in their enmity towards their relatives and dear ones and became completely disassociated from them. Allah Almighty then revealed this verse, giving them hope that the condition of those disbelievers would change.

blocks.text: The summary is: O believers! It is near that Allah Almighty will create such love between you and those people among the disbelievers of Makkah with whom you have become enemies that He will grant them the ability to accept faith. Allah Almighty is All-Powerful over changing hearts, changing conditions and making the causes of love easy. He forgives and shows mercy to those among the polytheists who accept faith. Allah Almighty did exactly this: after the conquest of Makkah, a great number of them accepted faith, became friends and brothers of the believers, and their love for one another increased. (Madarik, Al-Mumtahanah, under verse 7, p. 1233; Khazin, under verse 7, 4/257, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Allah does not forbid you  from those who did not fight against you on account of (your) religion and (they) did not drive you out from your homes, that you may be favourable towards them and deal with them fairly; indeed, the just ones are the beloveds of Allah.

blocks.text: The summary of the verses is that doing good and dealing fairly with disbelievers with whom Muslims have a peace treaty, or with protected disbelievers, is permitted. With others, it is prohibited. The meaning of qist and the details of birr and qist follow.

blocks.text: What does birr, meaning goodness and good treatment, entail?

runs.text: What does birr, meaning goodness and good treatment, entail?

blocks.text: Imam Ahmad Raza Khan رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ described three forms of birr and kind treatment towards disbelievers:

runs.text: Imam Ahmad Raza Khan رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ described three forms of birr and kind treatment towards disbelievers:

blocks.text:
1. The highest form is to intentionally benefit and do good to a disbeliever without any valid personal purpose. This is forbidden even with a musta'min, a disbeliever who enters an Islamic state under a guarantee of safety, and with a mu'ahid, a disbeliever with whom a treaty exists, because a guarantee and treaty are intended to prevent harm, not to knowingly benefit the enemies of Allah Almighty.
2. The middle form is to act for a personal benefit, such as giving a disbeliever something in return for what he gave, or dealing financially with him while considering family ties. This is permissible with a disbeliever who has a treaty with the Muslims, but prohibited with one who has no treaty.
3. The lowest form is to give something as a military stratagem for the benefit of Islam and the Muslims. This is permissible even with a harbi disbeliever, one with whom there is no treaty.

blocks.text: The meaning of qist

runs.text: The meaning of qist

blocks.text: Exegetes have mentioned three meanings of qist, meaning justice. The first is not to oppress them. In this meaning, the command applies to every disbeliever, whether a harbi or a treaty-holder: it is not permissible to oppress even a harbi. This is an obligation, not merely a concession.

runs.text: Exegetes have mentioned three meanings of qist, meaning justice. The first is not to oppress them. In this meaning, the command applies to every disbeliever, whether a harbi or a treaty-holder: it is not permissible to oppress even a harbi. This is an obligation, not merely a concession.

blocks.text: The second is to fulfil a treaty made with disbelievers. This too is obligatory, not merely permitted. However, completing the treaty period is not obligatory: if there is a benefit, it is permissible to announce the matter and terminate the treaty before its expiry.

blocks.text: The third meaning is to give them some of one’s wealth, which is the same as birr, goodness. Thus birr and qist would be one matter in this meaning.

blocks.text: Imam Ahmad Raza Khan عَلَیْہِ الرَّحْمَۃ explained that a distinction may be made between the two words: qist means giving the disbeliever the equivalent of what he gave, such as giving an item worth one thousand rupees in return for an item worth one thousand. If he gave nothing and a Muslim gives him an item worth one thousand because of kinship or another benefit, or if he gave an item worth one thousand and the Muslim gives him something worth more, this is birr: doing good and showing favour. (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 14/471, summarised.)

blocks.text: Forms and rulings of friendship with disbelievers

runs.text: Forms and rulings of friendship with disbelievers

blocks.text: Verse 9 prohibits friendship with disbelievers. The summary of the words of Imam Ahmad Raza Khan رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ concerning friendship with them is as follows.

runs.text: Verse 9 prohibits friendship with disbelievers. The summary of the words of Imam Ahmad Raza Khan رَحْمَۃُاللّٰہِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ concerning friendship with them is as follows.

blocks.text: There are two forms of muwalat, meaning friendship with disbelievers:

runs.text: There are two forms of muwalat, meaning friendship with disbelievers:

blocks.text:
1. Real muwalat: its lowest form is an inclination of the heart. This is absolutely forbidden with every disbeliever in every situation. An involuntary natural inclination, such as towards parents, children or a beautiful wife, is not included in this ruling. Nevertheless, one must suppress this inclination as far as possible, to the point of eliminating it if necessary, while remembering that they are enemies of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ and that friendship with them is forbidden. The arrival of the inclination was involuntary, but keeping it is within one’s control; retaining it would therefore amount to choosing friendship, which is categorically forbidden. This is why a person has no acceptable excuse for an involuntary matter whose initial causes he created by choice: losing one’s reason after drinking wine is not within one’s control, but because drinking was chosen, the loss of reason and everything resulting from it is also attributed to his choice.
2. Outward muwalat: the heart has no inclination towards a disbeliever, but one behaves in a way that outwardly indicates love and inclination. In necessity and compulsion, this is permitted only to the extent of the necessity. If it is enough merely not to display enmity, one should stop at that. If expressing love is necessary, one should speak indirectly as far as possible; explicit expression is not permitted. If there is no escape without it and the heart is firm upon faith, explicit expression is permitted as a concession, although the proper course remains not to do so. (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 14/465–467, summarised.)

blocks.text: The summary of the two verses under discussion is: Allah Almighty does not forbid you from doing good and dealing fairly with those disbelievers who did not fight you on account of religion, did not expel you from your homes, and did not support your opponents in expelling you. Indeed, Allah Almighty loves those who deal fairly. He only forbids you from befriending those disbelievers who fought you on account of religion, expelled you from your homes, and supported your opponents in expelling you. Whoever befriends them is among the wrongdoers. (Khazin, Al-Mumtahanah, under verses 8–9, 4/258.)
