blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O believers! When Muslim women leave the land of disbelief and migrate towards you, so examine them (by taking an oath from them); Allah knows more about their faith; so if you find the women to be believers, do not therefore send them back to the disbelievers; neither are they (i.e. the believing women) lawful for the disbelieving (men), nor are the disbelieving (men) lawful for them (i.e. the believing women); and give back to their disbelieving husbands what they had spent (on these believing women e.g. dowry); and there is no sin upon you to marry them (i.e. these believing women) when you give them their dowry; and (O Muslims) do not continue the marriage with disbelieving women, and ask back (from the disbelievers) what you had spent, and the disbelievers may ask for what they had spent (on the believing women); this is Allah's command, He judges between you, and Allah is All Knowing, the Wise.

blocks.text: {یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْۤا اِذَا جَآءَكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنٰتُ مُهٰجِرٰتٍ: O believers! When Muslim women leave their homes and come to you.} Seven rulings concerning Muslim women who migrate are given in this verse.

runs.text: {یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْۤا اِذَا جَآءَكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنٰتُ مُهٰجِرٰتٍ: O believers! When Muslim women leave their homes and come to you.} Seven rulings concerning Muslim women who migrate are given in this verse.

blocks.text:
1. When Muslim women leave the land of disbelief and come to you, examine them to determine whether their migration is purely for religion, rather than because of enmity towards their husbands or another worldly reason. The examination is for your knowledge; Allah Almighty knows their faith better than you. Their examination is carried out by making them swear that they did not leave because of enmity towards their husbands or any worldly reason, but migrated only for their religion and faith. This is reported from Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Abbas رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا.
2. If, after examination, they appear to be believers, do not return them to their disbelieving husbands. These Muslim women are not lawful for those disbelieving men, nor are those disbelieving men lawful for them. This shows that when a disbelieving man’s disbelieving wife accepts faith and migrates, she leaves his marriage.
3. Give their disbelieving husbands the dowries they paid to those women. Occasion of revelation: This verse was revealed after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. The treaty contained the condition that any man from Makkah who accepted faith and came to the Noble Prophet ﷺ could be taken back by the people of Makkah. This verse clarified that the condition concerned men only; women were not specified in the treaty and could not be included in it, because a Muslim woman is not lawful for a disbeliever. Some exegetes said that this part abrogated the earlier command not to return them to their disbelieving husbands.

blocks.text: Two legal matters concerning this dowry are worth noting: the dowry is given when the disbelieving husband demands it; if he does not demand it, nothing is given to him. Likewise, if the disbeliever had not paid a dowry to the emigrant woman, he receives nothing.

runs.text: Two legal matters concerning this dowry are worth noting: the dowry is given when the disbelieving husband demands it; if he does not demand it, nothing is given to him. Likewise, if the disbeliever had not paid a dowry to the emigrant woman, he receives nothing.

blocks.text:
4. There is no sin in marrying these emigrant women after giving them their dowries, even if they have husbands in the land of war, because accepting Islam made them unlawful for those husbands and removed them from their marriages. Giving the dowry here means making it obligatory upon oneself, even if it is not paid immediately. This also proves that a new dowry is obligatory when marrying these women; the amount paid to their former husbands is not counted as it. Thus two amounts are involved: one for the former disbelieving husband and another as the woman’s dowry.
5. Do not continue marriage with disbelieving women. This means that women who remained in the land of war, or who became apostates and went to the land of war, should not remain wives. After this verse was revealed, the Companions of the Noble Prophet ﷺ divorced the disbelieving women who were in Makkah. If, God forbid, a Muslim’s wife becomes an apostate, she does not leave his marriage immediately; however, after she returns to Islam, a new marriage contract with the same husband is required.
6. Recover from the disbelievers the dowries that you paid to the women who left you.
7. The disbelievers may ask the Muslims who married women who migrated to the Islamic land to pay what they had spent on those women.

blocks.text: Arabic: وَ اِنْ فَاتَكُمْ شَیْءٌ مِّنْ اَزْوَاجِكُمْ اِلَى الْكُفَّارِ فَعَاقَبْتُمْ فَاٰتُوا الَّذِیْنَ ذَهَبَتْ اَزْوَاجُهُمْ مِّثْلَ مَاۤ اَنْفَقُوْاؕ-وَ اتَّقُوا اللّٰهَ الَّذِیْۤ اَنْتُمْ بِهٖ مُؤْمِنُوْنَ(11)

runs.text: Arabic:

وَ اِنْ فَاتَكُمْ شَیْءٌ مِّنْ اَزْوَاجِكُمْ اِلَى الْكُفَّارِ فَعَاقَبْتُمْ فَاٰتُوا الَّذِیْنَ ذَهَبَتْ اَزْوَاجُهُمْ مِّثْلَ مَاۤ اَنْفَقُوْاؕ-وَ اتَّقُوا اللّٰهَ الَّذِیْۤ اَنْتُمْ بِهٖ مُؤْمِنُوْنَ(11)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And if any of your wives go away from the custody of Muslims to the disbelievers (by becoming apostates, and you did not get back the money you have spent on them), then you should punish the disbelievers (in war, those who provided custody for them), give from the spoils of war, as much as they had spent, to the Muslims whose wives went away (to the land of disbelief having become apostates); and fear Allah in Whom you believe.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

And if any of your wives go away from the custody of Muslims to the disbelievers (by becoming apostates, and you did not get back the money you have spent on them), then you should punish the disbelievers (in war, those who provided custody for them), give from the spoils of war, as much as they had spent, to the Muslims whose wives went away (to the land of disbelief having become apostates); and fear Allah in Whom you believe.

blocks.text: {وَ اِنْ فَاتَكُمْ شَیْءٌ مِّنْ اَزْوَاجِكُمْ اِلَى الْكُفَّارِ: And if any of your wives go away from the custody of Muslims to the disbelievers.} After the preceding verse was revealed, the Muslims paid the dowries of the emigrating women to their disbelieving husbands, but the disbelievers refused to pay the dowries of the apostate women to the Muslims. This verse was revealed concerning that situation: if some women leave you as apostates and go to the disbelievers, then you fight and punish the disbelievers and gain spoils from them, give from the spoils to those whose wives became apostates and went to the land of war an amount equal to what they spent on the women, and fear Allah Almighty in Whom you believe.

The Noble Prophet ﷺ gave their husbands the amount of their dowries from the spoils of war. (Khazin, Al-Mumtahanah, under verse 11, 4/259–260; Madarik, under verse 11, p. 1234, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Note: The rulings in these verses concerning examining emigrant women, paying the disbelievers what they spent on their wives after the wives migrated, recovering from disbelievers what Muslims spent on their wives after those wives became apostates and joined the disbelievers, and paying from the spoils to those whose wives became apostates and left, were all abrogated by the verses of jihad or spoils, or by hadith. These rulings remained while the treaty remained; when the treaty ended, the rulings also ended. (Khazain-ul-Irfan, Al-Mumtahanah, under verse 11, p. 1018–1019, summarised.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O (Beloved) Prophet! When Muslim women are present in your august court to pledge an oath of allegiance upon this fact that they will neither ascribe any partner to Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their offspring, nor bring the fabrication that they carry between their hands and feet i.e. in their womb, nor disobey you in any righteous matter, so accept their allegiance and seek forgiveness from Allah for them; indeed, Allah is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.

blocks.text: The Noble Prophet ﷺ said, “I take your allegiance that you will not associate anything with Allah Almighty.” Sayyidatuna Hind raised her head and said, “You are taking from us a pledge that we did not see you take from the men.” On that day, the men had pledged only Islam and striving. The Noble Prophet ﷺ then said, “And you will not steal.” Sayyidatuna Hind رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا replied, “Sayyiduna Abu Sufyan رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ is a miserly man, and I have certainly taken some of his wealth. I do not know whether it was lawful for me.” Sayyiduna Abu Sufyan رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ was present and said, “Whatever you took before and whatever you take in future is lawful.” The Noble Prophet ﷺ smiled and said, “You are Hind bint Utbah.” She replied, “Yes. Please forgive whatever wrongs I committed.”

blocks.text: How the women pledged allegiance

runs.text: How the women pledged allegiance

blocks.text: When the Noble Prophet ﷺ took the women’s allegiance, he did not shake hands with them and did not allow the women to touch his blessed hand. Sayyidatuna Aishah رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا said: “By Allah, the hand of the Noble Prophet ﷺ did not touch the hand of any woman during the allegiance. He took their allegiance only through his words.” (Sahih Bukhari, Book of Tafsir, Surah Al-Mumtahanah, chapter on when believing women who emigrated come to you, 3/350, hadith 4891.)

blocks.text: It has also been reported that the Chief of the Messengers ﷺ placed his blessed hand into a large vessel of water, after which the women placed their hands into it. It has also been said that the allegiance was taken through a cloth. It is not unlikely that both methods were practised.

blocks.text: Lessons from “O Prophet! When Muslim women are present before you”

runs.text: Lessons from “O Prophet! When Muslim women are present before you”

blocks.text: Four matters are learned from this verse:

runs.text: Four matters are learned from this verse:

blocks.text:
1. When a spiritual guide makes someone a disciple, he should make him repent not only generally but also from the particular sins in which he is involved. For example, he should make one who does not pray specifically repent from abandoning prayer, and one who consumes interest repent specifically from consuming interest, and command him to remain firm upon this in future.
2. After taking allegiance, the spiritual guide should supplicate for his disciple’s forgiveness: “O Allah Almighty, forgive his previous sins.”
3. The command to repent oneself is one matter, and repenting at the hand of one of Allah Almighty’s accepted servants is another matter.
4. It is Sunnah for Muslims to pledge allegiance at the hands of spiritual guides, because these believing women pledged to the Noble Prophet ﷺ that they would avoid sins in future, and this is the purpose of allegiance to spiritual guides. There are four types of allegiance: the allegiance of Islam, the allegiance of the Caliphate, the allegiance of piety, and the allegiance of repentance. The allegiance taken today is the allegiance of repentance or piety. This verse and similar verses are its basis.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْا لَا تَتَوَلَّوْا قَوْمًا غَضِبَ اللّٰهُ عَلَیْهِمْ: O believers! blocks.text: It should be remembered that there are several other statements concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse. One of them is that it was revealed concerning the hypocrites who falsely promised the Muslims that they would help them. (Khazin, Surah As-Saff, under verse 2, 4/262) In this respect, it condemns the hypocrites, and addressing them as believers is because of their apparent faith. If the verse was revealed concerning the Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْهُمْ, then it is not a condemnation of them; rather, it is their instruction that making such claims is not correct, because no one knows what the future will bring. It is possible that, for some reason, they may then be unable to fulfil that claim.

blocks.text: There should be no contradiction between word and deed

runs.text: There should be no contradiction between word and deed

blocks.text: This verse teaches that there should be no contradiction between word and deed. One should act according to one's words. There are many forms of this contradiction, such as telling people good things while not acting upon them oneself, or promising someone to do something while already intending not to do it and making only a verbal promise. In other words, one says something but does not fulfil it. The ahadith particularly mention severe condemnation and warning concerning these matters.

His intestines will spill out in Hell, and he will revolve around them just as a donkey revolves around a millstone. The people of Hell will gather around him and say: ‘O so-and-so! What happened to you? You used to command us to do good and forbid us from evil.’ He will say: ‘I used to command you to do good, but I did not do good myself, and I used to forbid you from evil, but I did evil myself.’” (Bukhari, Book of the Beginning of Creation, chapter on the description of Hell and that it has been created, 2/396, hadith 3267)

blocks.text: Concerning those who break promises, it is narrated from Sayyiduna Ali al-Murtada کَرَّمَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی وَجْہَہُ الْکَرِیْم that whoever breaks a covenant with a Muslim is cursed by Allah Almighty, the angels and all people, and neither his obligatory nor his voluntary deeds will be accepted. blocks.text: Likewise, the verse can mean that one should not claim to do what one does not do. For example, a person does not help the poor but claims that he helps them greatly; this is merely a false claim. Or a person may claim that he will do something, while intending in his heart not to fulfil it. For example, he says that he will give such-and-such help to the poor of a particular place, while intending not to do so. Thus, he does not do what he says.

blocks.text: {اِنَّ اللّٰهَ یُحِبُّ الَّذِیْنَ: Verily, Allah befriends those people.} Allah Almighty states that He befriends those who fight in His path in rows as though they are a wall of molten lead: each one joined to the other, each firmly fixed in his place, and all of them like one body against the enemy. blocks.text: The purpose is that Allah Almighty likes brave fighters who stand firm against the disbelievers and do not turn their backs. Since rows were formed in jihad in that era, rows are mentioned here. In our time, jihad may be carried out by forming rows and by other methods. Every method that contains useful organisation and discipline, strengthens one another, and becomes a means of victory over others is included in this.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {وَ اِذْ قَالَ مُوْسٰى لِقَوْمِهٖ: And remember when Moosa said to his nation.} O Beloved ﷺ, mention before your nation the event when Sayyiduna Moosa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام said to his people: “O my people! blocks.text: Many ahadith and reports also mention the glad tidings given by Sayyiduna 'Eisa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام. Three of them are recorded below.

runs.text: Many ahadith and reports also mention the glad tidings given by Sayyiduna 'Eisa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام. Three of them are recorded below.

blocks.text: 1. Sayyiduna Abu Musa al-Ashari رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ states that the Noble Messenger ﷺ ordered us to go to the kingdom of the Negus. When we went to him, the Negus said: “I testify that Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah Almighty, and he is the very Messenger concerning whom Sayyiduna 'Eisa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام gave glad tidings. If I were not bound by the affairs of the kingdom, I would come into his presence and carry his shoes.” (Abu Dawud, Book of Funerals, chapter on praying over a Muslim who passes away in the land of polytheism, 3/285, hadith 3205)

blocks.text: Five matters related to this verse

وَ مَنْ اَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرٰى عَلَى اللّٰهِ الْكَذِبَ وَ هُوَ یُدْعٰۤى اِلَى الْاِسْلَامِؕ-وَ اللّٰهُ لَا یَهْدِی الْقَوْمَ الظّٰلِمِیْنَ(7)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And who is more unjust than the one who fabricates lie against Allah whilst he is being called towards Islam? And Allah does not guide the unjust.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
And who is more unjust than the one who fabricates lie against Allah whilst he is being called towards Islam? And Allah does not guide the unjust.

blocks.text: {وَ مَنْ اَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرٰى عَلَى اللّٰهِ الْكَذِبَ: And who is more unjust than the one who fabricates lie against Allah?} The meaning of this verse is: Who is more unjust than the one whose Lord عزوجل calls him, through the sacred tongue of His Beloved ﷺ, towards Islam, in which lies the prosperity of both worlds, but instead of accepting the invitation he calls the verses of Allah Almighty magic and fabricates lies against Him? Allah Almighty does not grant such unjust people the ability to be guided, because He knows through His eternal knowledge that they will remain disbelievers. (Khazin, Surah As-Saff, under verse 7, 4/263)

blocks.text: {هُوَ الَّذِیْۤ اَرْسَلَ رَسُوْلَهٗ بِالْهُدٰى وَ دِیْنِ الْحَقِّ: It is He Who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the true religion.} It means that He is the very Allah Almighty Who sent His Messenger Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ with the means of guidance towards the straight path, namely the Quran and miracles, and with the true religion which Allah Almighty chose for His Messenger and his Ummah, so that He may make it prevail over all religions, even if the polytheists dislike this dominance.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O believers! Shall I tell you of that trade which can save you from the painful punishment?

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
O believers! Shall I tell you of that trade which can save you from the painful punishment?

blocks.text: {یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْا: O believers!} The summary of this verse and the two verses after it is: O believers! Shall I tell you of that trade which can save you from the painful punishment? Listen: that trade is that you remain steadfast in believing in Allah Almighty and His Messenger ﷺ and strive in Allah Almighty's path with your wealth and your lives. If you knew your real benefit, remaining steadfast upon faith and striving would be better for you than your life, wealth and everything else. If you do this, Allah Almighty will forgive the sins you committed in the world and, on the Day of Judgement, admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow and into pure dwellings in the everlasting gardens. Receiving this reward is the great success. (Ruh-ul-Bayan, Surah As-Saff, under verses 10–11, 9/505–506; Khazin, Surah As-Saff, under verses 10–12, 4/263, excerpted)

runs.text: {یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْا: O believers!} The summary of this verse and the two verses after it is: O believers! Shall I tell you of that trade which can save you from the painful punishment? Listen: that trade is that you remain steadfast in believing in Allah Almighty and His Messenger ﷺ and strive in Allah Almighty's path with your wealth and your lives. If you knew your real benefit, remaining steadfast upon faith and striving would be better for you than your life, wealth and everything else. If you do this, Allah Almighty will forgive the sins you committed in the world and, on the Day of Judgement, admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow and into pure dwellings in the everlasting gardens. Receiving this reward is the great success. (Ruh-ul-Bayan, Surah As-Saff, under verses 10–11, 9/505–506; Khazin, Surah As-Saff, under verses 10–12, 4/263, excerpted)

blocks.text: Note: It should be remembered that prayer comes after faith in rank. However, because jihad was urgently needed at that time, jihad is mentioned here after faith.

blocks.text: Here, believing in Allah Almighty and striving with one's life and wealth in His path is called a trade because, just as profit is hoped for through trade, the greatest profit, namely Allah Almighty's pleasure, Paradise and salvation, is attained through these deeds.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And He will give you another favour which is dear to you; the help from Allah and a forthcoming victory (of Makkah, Persia and Rome, etc.); and O Beloved, give glad tidings to the Muslims.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
And He will give you another favour which is dear to you; the help from Allah and a forthcoming victory (of Makkah, Persia and Rome, etc.); and O Beloved, give glad tidings to the Muslims.

blocks.text: {وَ اُخْرٰى تُحِبُّوْنَهَا: And He will give you another favour which is dear to you.} O believers! In addition to the blessings of the Hereafter, forgiveness and reward, Allah Almighty will grant you another blessing in this world which you love. That blessing is Allah Almighty's help and a forthcoming victory. And, O Beloved ﷺ, give the Muslims glad tidings of victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. (Khazin, Surah As-Saff, under verse 13, 4/263; Madarik, Surah As-Saff, under verse 13, p. 1237, excerpted)

runs.text: {وَ اُخْرٰى تُحِبُّوْنَهَا: And He will give you another favour which is dear to you.} O believers! In addition to the blessings of the Hereafter, forgiveness and reward, Allah Almighty will grant you another blessing in this world which you love. That blessing is Allah Almighty's help and a forthcoming victory. And, O Beloved ﷺ, give the Muslims glad tidings of victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O believers! Become the helpers of Allah's religion.} This verse encourages Muslims to help the religion and strive against its opponents. Its summary is: O believers! Become the helpers of Allah Almighty's religion, just as the disciples of Sayyiduna 'Eisa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام helped Allah Almighty's religion when he said to them: “Who will help me whilst inclining towards Allah Almighty?” The disciples replied: “We are the helpers of Allah Almighty's religion.” Then one group among the Children of Israel believed in Sayyiduna 'Eisa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام and one group disbelieved. When the two groups fought, We helped the believers against their enemies, so the believers became dominant.

Become the helpers of Allah's religion.} This verse encourages Muslims to help the religion and strive against its opponents. Its summary is: O believers! Become the helpers of Allah Almighty's religion, just as the disciples of Sayyiduna 'Eisa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام helped Allah Almighty's religion when he said to them: “Who will help me whilst inclining towards Allah Almighty?” The disciples replied: “We are the helpers of Allah Almighty's religion.” Then one group among the Children of Israel believed in Sayyiduna 'Eisa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام and one group disbelieved. When the two groups fought, We helped the believers against their enemies, so the believers became dominant.

blocks.text: It has also been stated in the explanation of the final part of the verse that when Sayyiduna 'Eisa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام was raised to the heavens, his nation divided into three sects. One sect said concerning Sayyiduna 'Eisa عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام: “He was Allah and has gone to the heavens.” Another said: “He was the son of Allah Almighty, and He called him to Himself.” The third said: “He was the bondsman and Messenger of Allah Almighty; He raised him.” The people of this third sect were believers. They fought the other two sects, but the disbelieving groups remained dominant over them until the Leader of the Prophets, Muhammad Mustafa ﷺ, appeared. At that time, the believing group became dominant over the disbelievers.

blocks.text: {وَ الشَّمْسِ وَ ضُحٰىهَا: By the oath of the sun and its light.} That is, by the sun when its light becomes manifest. In this Surah, Allah Almighty has sworn by several things in order to manifest the greatness of His Power and His Oneness in being worthy of worship. These are things upon which great benefits for creation depend, and by pondering over them, every person can learn about the Power and Oneness of Allah Almighty. (Khazin, Ash-Shams, under verse 1, 4/381; Sawi, Ash-Shams, under verse 1, 6/2369; Tafsir Kabir, Ash-Shams, under verse 1, 11/173, excerpted)

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {وَ النَّهَارِ اِذَا جَلّٰىهَا: And by the day, when it brightens it.} One meaning of this verse is: by the day when it makes the sun clearly visible. Since day is the name of the sun's light, the brighter the day, the more manifest the sun becomes, because the strength and perfection of an effect indicate the strength and perfection of the one producing the effect. Thus, the day makes the sun manifest. The second meaning is: by the day when it illuminates the world or the earth, or removes the darkness of night. (Tafsir Kabir, Ash-Shams, under verse 3, 11/174–175; Khazin, Ash-Shams, under verse 3, 4/381, excerpted)

runs.text: {وَ الَّیْلِ اِذَا یَغْشٰىهَا: And by the night when it hides it (i.e. hides the sun).} One meaning of this verse is: by the night when it hides the sun and the edges of the sky become filled with darkness and gloom. The second meaning is: by the night when it covers the world.

blocks.text: The four things mentioned up to this point are, in reality, four qualities of the sun. Day exists because of the sun, and the light becomes clearly visible; night occurs when the sun sets, and the moon rises after it. Whoever ponders over the sun even a little and observes, with the eye of the heart, its structure, creation and other matters will come to know the greatness of its Creator. (Khazin, Ash-Shams, under verse 4, 4/381–382; Tafsir Kabir, Ash-Shams, under verse 4, 11/175, excerpted)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: The (nation of) Thamood denied (their Prophet Saalih) with their rebelliousness.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
The (nation of) Thamood denied (their Prophet Saalih) with their rebelliousness.

blocks.text: {كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُوْدُ بِطَغْوٰىهَا: The (nation of) Thamood denied (their Prophet Saalih) with their rebelliousness.} In the previous verses, the success of the obedient and the failure of the disobedient were described through several oaths. Here, Allah Almighty describes the state of one of His Messengers and those who disobeyed him, so that it would become clear to the disbelievers of Makkah that just as the nation of Sayyiduna Salih عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام was destroyed because of disobeying him, they too could be destroyed because of disobeying the Noble Messenger ﷺ. The summary of this verse and the four verses after it is that the nation of Thamood, in its rebellion, denied their Messenger, Sayyiduna Salih عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام, when their most wretched man, Qudar ibn Salif, rose with the agreement of all of them to cut the camel's legs. Allah's Messenger, Sayyiduna Salih عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام, said to them: “Beware of pursuing the she-camel of Allah, and do not take water on the day appointed for her to drink, so that punishment does not befall you.” They denied Sayyiduna Salih عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام and then cut the camel's legs. Their Lord, عزَّوَجَلَّ, therefore caused destruction to them because of their sin and levelled their settlement, killing them all; not one of them remained. Allah Almighty does not fear pursuing them, as kings do, because He is the King of all kings. He does whatever He wills, and no one has the power to oppose Him. (Sawi, Ash-Shams, under verses 11–15, 6/2370–2371; Abu Saud, Ash-Shams, under verses 11–15, 5/875–876; Khazin, Ash-Shams, under verses 11–15, 4/382–383, excerpted)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: By the oath of the sky, and by the one that comes at night.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
By the oath of the sky, and by the one that comes at night.

blocks.text: {وَ السَّمَآءِ وَ الطَّارِقِ: By the oath of the sky, and by the one that comes at night.} One night, Abu Talib brought some food as a gift to the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ. While the Radiant Prophet ﷺ was consuming it, a star fell and the entire atmosphere filled with fire. Abu Talib became frightened and asked what it was. The Noble Prophet ﷺ said, “It is a star by which devils are struck, and it is among the signs of Allah Almighty’s power.” Abu Talib was amazed by this, so Allah Almighty revealed these verses in confirmation of His Beloved ﷺ.

runs.text: {وَ السَّمَآءِ وَ الطَّارِقِ: By the oath of the sky, and by the one that comes at night.} One night, Abu Talib brought some food as a gift to the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ. While the Radiant Prophet ﷺ was consuming it, a star fell and the entire atmosphere filled with fire. Abu Talib became frightened and asked what it was. The Noble Prophet ﷺ said, “It is a star by which devils are struck, and it is among the signs of Allah Almighty’s power.” Abu Talib was amazed by this, so Allah Almighty revealed these verses in confirmation of His Beloved ﷺ.

blocks.text: The summary of this verse and the three verses after it is that Allah Almighty mentioned an oath by the sky and by the brightly shining star that appears at night, and stated that every soul has a guardian appointed by its Lord عزَّوَجَلَّ. He guards its deeds and records all its good and bad deeds. Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Abbas رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا said that the guardian here refers to angels. (Khazin, At-Tariq, under verses 1–4, 4/368.)

blocks.text: Two matters learned from “There is no soul that does not have a guardian over it”

runs.text: Two matters learned from “There is no soul that does not have a guardian over it”

blocks.text:
1. Although Allah Almighty has power to protect everyone in every way Himself, the established practice is that this work is carried out by the angels appointed by Him.
2. Some of Allah Almighty’s names may be given to His servants. One of Allah Almighty’s names is Hafiz, meaning Guardian, and the angels have been called guardians in this verse. Therefore, we may say that Allah Almighty and His Beloved ﷺ are our guardians and helpers.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: So, man should ponder what thing he has been created from.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {فَلْیَنْظُرِ الْاِنْسَانُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ: So, man should ponder what thing he has been created from.} In the preceding verses, Allah Almighty mentioned an oath and stated that a guardian is appointed over every soul, who guards and records its deeds. In this verse, man is commanded to ponder his beginning of creation, so that he may know that the One Who created him the first time is also able to resurrect him after his passing away in order to recompense him. Therefore, man should perform deeds for the day on which he will be resurrected and recompensed. (Madarik, At-Tariq, under verse 5, p. 1338.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Created from a spurting (drop of) fluid.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {خُلِقَ مِنْ مَّآءٍ دَافِقٍ: Created from a spurting (drop of) fluid.} This verse explains the substance from which Allah Almighty created man. The summary of this verse and the one after it is that Allah Almighty created man from spurting fluid, meaning the fluids of the man and woman which combine in the woman’s womb and become one. This fluid emerges from between the man’s backbone and the woman’s chest.

runs.text: {خُلِقَ مِنْ مَّآءٍ دَافِقٍ: Created from a spurting (drop of) fluid.} This verse explains the substance from which Allah Almighty created man. The summary of this verse and the one after it is that Allah Almighty created man from spurting fluid, meaning the fluids of the man and woman which combine in the woman’s womb and become one. This fluid emerges from between the man’s backbone and the woman’s chest.

blocks.text: Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Abbas رَضِیَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا said that this fluid emerges from the place on the woman’s chest where a necklace is worn. It is also narrated from him that it emerges from between the woman’s two breasts. It has also been said that semen emerges from all of man’s organs: most of it comes from the brain through the man’s back, while a great deal comes from the many veins in the front part of the woman’s body that are located at the chest. This is why both places were mentioned specifically here. (Madarik, At-Tariq, under verses 6–7, p. 1338; Khazin, At-Tariq, under verses 6–7, 4/368, excerpted.)

blocks.text: {یَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَآىٕرُ: The Day when secrets will be examined.} The summary of this verse and the one after it is that, on the day when hidden matters are exposed, the person who denies resurrection after passing away will possess neither such strength as could repel the punishment nor such a helper as could save him from it. Hidden matters means beliefs, intentions and deeds which a person conceals; Allah Almighty will expose all of them on the Day of Judgement. (Madarik, At-Tariq, under verses 9–10, pp. 1338–1339; Khazin, At-Tariq, under verses 9–10, 4/369, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: By the oath of the sky from which comes down the rain.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

blocks.text: {وَ السَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ الرَّجْعِ: By the oath of the sky from which comes down the rain.} After presenting proofs of Divine Oneness and resurrection, Allah Almighty mentions an oath by the earth and sky and explains the reality of the Holy Quran. The summary of this verse and the three verses after it is that, by the sky from which rain descends repeatedly and by the earth which is split so that vegetation may emerge, the Holy Quran is certainly a decisive Word. It distinguishes truth from falsehood, and the Quran is not an amusement or a useless, meaningless matter. (Tafsir Kabir, At-Tariq, under verses 11–14, 11/122–123; Khazin, At-Tariq, under verses 11–14, 4/369, excerpted.)

runs.text: {وَ السَّمَآءِ ذَاتِ الرَّجْعِ: By the oath of the sky from which comes down the rain.} After presenting proofs of Divine Oneness and resurrection, Allah Almighty mentions an oath by the earth and sky and explains the reality of the Holy Quran. The summary of this verse and the three verses after it is that, by the sky from which rain descends repeatedly and by the earth which is split so that vegetation may emerge, the Holy Quran is certainly a decisive Word. It distinguishes truth from falsehood, and the Quran is not an amusement or a useless, meaningless matter. (Tafsir Kabir, At-Tariq, under verses 11–14, 11/122–123; Khazin, At-Tariq, under verses 11–14, 4/369, excerpted.)

blocks.text: These verses also indicate that the sky from which rain repeatedly descends is like a father to the earth’s produce, vegetation and trees, while the earth that is split is like a mother to vegetation. Both are among Allah Almighty’s wondrous blessings, and countless signs of His power appear in them. By pondering over them, a person finds many proofs of being resurrected after passing away. (Ruh-ul-Bayan, At-Tariq, under verse 12, 10/400, abridged.)

blocks.text: The Quran is a decisive Word

runs.text: The Quran is a decisive Word

blocks.text: Regarding this quality of the Holy Quran and its other qualities, Sayyiduna Ali al-Murtada كَرَّمَ اللّٰہُ تَعَالٰی وَجْہَہُ الْکَرِیْم said: I heard the Noble Messenger ﷺ say, “A tribulation will soon arise.” I asked, “O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, what will be the way to remain safe from it?” He ﷺ said, “The Book of Allah Almighty, in which are the accounts of those before you and those after you, and the judgments between you. The Quran is decisive, and it is not an amusement. Whoever abandons it while being unjust, Allah Almighty will destroy him; and whoever seeks guidance in other than it, Allah Almighty will misguide him. It is the strong rope of Allah Almighty and the wise reminder. It is the straight path.

The Quran is decisive, and it is not an amusement. Whoever abandons it while being unjust, Allah Almighty will destroy him; and whoever seeks guidance in other than it, Allah Almighty will misguide him. It is the strong rope of Allah Almighty and the wise reminder. It is the straight path.

blocks.text: “The Quran is that through whose blessing desires do not become corrupt, and with which other tongues cannot make it doubtful and ambiguous. Scholars never become satiated with it, it does not grow old through repeated recitation, and its wonders never end. When the jinn heard it, they could not help saying, ‘We have heard a wondrous Quran which guides towards goodness, so we believed in it.’ Whoever speaks in accordance with the Quran is truthful; whoever acts upon it will receive reward; whoever judges according to it will be just; and whoever calls towards it calls towards the straight path.” (Tirmidhi, Book of the Virtues of the Quran, chapter on what has been narrated concerning the excellence of the Quran, 4/414, hadith 2915.)

blocks.text: {اِنَّهُمْ یَكِیْدُوْنَ كَیْدًا: Indeed, the disbelievers carry out their (evil) scheme.} The summary of this verse and the two verses after it is that the disbelievers of Makkah are making various schemes to erase the religion of Allah Almighty, extinguish the light of truth and cause pain to the Crown of Messengership ﷺ. Allah Almighty is making a hidden plan of His own, of which they have no knowledge. Therefore, O Beloved ﷺ, do not supplicate for the destruction of the disbelievers; rather, give them respite and allow them a little time, because they will soon be destroyed. This is exactly what happened: at the Battle of Badr, Allah Almighty’s punishment seized them. (Khazin, At-Tariq, under verses 15–17, 4/369; Madarik, At-Tariq, under verses 15–17, p. 1339, excerpted.)

(Khazin, At-Tariq, under verses 15–17, 4/369; Madarik, At-Tariq, under verses 15–17, p. 1339, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Arabic: یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْا لَا تُقَدِّمُوْا بَیْنَ یَدَیِ اللّٰهِ وَ رَسُوْلِهٖ وَ اتَّقُوا اللّٰهَؕ-اِنَّ اللّٰهَ سَمِیْعٌ عَلِیْمٌ(1)

runs.text: Arabic:
یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْا لَا تُقَدِّمُوْا بَیْنَ یَدَیِ اللّٰهِ وَ رَسُوْلِهٖ وَ اتَّقُوا اللّٰهَؕ-اِنَّ اللّٰهَ سَمِیْعٌ عَلِیْمٌ(1)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O believers! Do not advance yourselves before (the command of) Allah and His (Beloved) Messenger, and fear Allah; indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
O believers! Do not advance yourselves before (the command of) Allah and His (Beloved) Messenger, and fear Allah; indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

blocks.text: {یٰۤاَیُّهَا الَّذِیْنَ اٰمَنُوْا: O believers!} This verse teaches the believers to observe the manners and respect of the Beloved of Allah Almighty, the Noble Prophet صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ. The summary of the verse is: O believers! It is necessary for you not to precede Allah Almighty and His Messenger صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ in any word or deed at all, without their permission, because going ahead of the Noble Messenger صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ is contrary to his reverence and respect, while humility and observance of manners are necessary in the august court of Prophethood. Fear Allah Almighty in all your words and deeds, because if you fear Allah Almighty, this fear will prevent you from going ahead. In any case, Allah Almighty hears all your words and knows all your deeds. The right of the One whose attribute this is, is that He be feared. (Khazin, Al-Hujurat, under verse 1, 4/163–164; Jalalayn, Al-Hujurat, under verse 1, p. 426; Madarik, Al-Hujurat, under verse 1, pp. 1149–1150, excerpted.)

blocks.text: There are various reports concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse. Two of them are given below.

runs.text: There are various reports concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse. Two of them are given below.

blocks.text: (1) A few people performed their sacrifice before the Sovereign of Both Worlds صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ on the day of Eid al-Adha, so they were commanded to sacrifice again.

runs.text: (1) A few people performed their sacrifice before the Sovereign of Both Worlds صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ on the day of Eid al-Adha, so they were commanded to sacrifice again.

blocks.text: (2) It is narrated from Sayyidatuna Aishah رَضِیَ اللہ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا that some people would begin fasting one day before Ramadan. This verse was revealed concerning them, and they were commanded not to go ahead of their Prophet صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ in beginning the fast. (Khazin, Al-Hujurat, under verse 1, 4/163–164; Jalalayn, Al-Hujurat, under verse 1, p. 426; Madarik, Al-Hujurat, under verse 1, pp. 1149–1150, excerpted.)

runs.text: (2) It is narrated from Sayyidatuna Aishah رَضِیَ اللہ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا that some people would begin fasting one day before Ramadan. This verse was revealed concerning them, and they were commanded not to go ahead of their Prophet صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ in beginning the fast. (Khazin, Al-Hujurat, under verse 1, 4/163–164; Jalalayn, Al-Hujurat, under verse 1, p. 426; Madarik, Al-Hujurat, under verse 1, pp. 1149–1150, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Mufti Ahmad Yar Khan Naeemi رَحْمَۃُاللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ says: “Whatever the occasion of revelation may have been, this command is general for everyone. It is forbidden to be ahead of the Noble Prophet عَلَیْہِ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام in any matter or deed. If one is travelling along with the Noble Prophet عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام, it is forbidden to walk ahead of him, except in the capacity of a servant or after obtaining permission for a need; in that case, walking ahead is not forbidden. If one is eating with him, it is unlawful to begin eating first. Similarly, giving one’s own intellect and opinion precedence over the opinion of the Noble Prophet عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام is forbidden.” (Shan-e-Habib al-Rahman, p. 224.)

If one is eating with him, it is unlawful to begin eating first. Similarly, giving one’s own intellect and opinion precedence over the opinion of the Noble Prophet عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام is forbidden.” (Shan-e-Habib al-Rahman, p. 224.)

blocks.text: The verse mentions Allah Almighty and His Messenger صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ together, although being ahead of Allah Almighty is impossible, because He is not confined to time or place, and being ahead occurs either in time or in place. It is therefore known that the purpose of the verse is that you must not go ahead of the Noble Messenger صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ; disrespect towards him is, in reality, disrespect towards Allah Almighty. Going ahead of him after obtaining permission, in the capacity of a servant, or because of a need is not included in this prohibition. Therefore, the reports in which some Companions رَضِیَ اللہ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ are mentioned as walking ahead of the Noble Prophet صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ do not fall under this verse, because they walked in the capacity of servants. Similarly, Sayyiduna Abu Bakr Siddiq رَضِیَ اللہ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ leading the prayer is not included in this prohibition, because he did so with the permission of the Noble Prophet صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ.

blocks.text: Allamah Ismail Haqqi رَحْمَۃُاللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ says: The honourable scholars are heirs of the Noble Prophets عَلَیْہِمُ الصَّلٰوۃُ وَالسَّلَام, so going ahead of them is also included in this prohibition. Its proof is the narration reported from Sayyiduna Abu Darda رَضِیَ اللہ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, in which he says: The Noble Prophet صَلَّی اللہ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْہِ وَاٰلِہٖ وَسَلَّمَ saw me walking ahead of Sayyiduna Abu Bakr Siddiq رَضِیَ اللہ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, so he said: “O Abu Darda! runs.text: Here are five matters related to this verse:

blocks.text: Arabic: وَ اِنْ طَآىٕفَتٰنِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِیْنَ اقْتَتَلُوْا فَاَصْلِحُوْا بَیْنَهُمَاۚ-فَاِنْۢ بَغَتْ اِحْدٰىهُمَا عَلَى الْاُخْرٰى فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِیْ تَبْغِیْ حَتّٰى تَفِیْٓءَ اِلٰۤى اَمْرِ اللّٰهِۚ-فَاِنْ فَآءَتْ فَاَصْلِحُوْا بَیْنَهُمَا بِالْعَدْلِ وَ اَقْسِطُوْاؕ-اِنَّ اللّٰهَ یُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِیْنَ(9)

runs.text: Arabic:

وَ اِنْ طَآىٕفَتٰنِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِیْنَ اقْتَتَلُوْا فَاَصْلِحُوْا بَیْنَهُمَاۚ-فَاِنْۢ بَغَتْ اِحْدٰىهُمَا عَلَى الْاُخْرٰى فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِیْ تَبْغِیْ حَتّٰى تَفِیْٓءَ اِلٰۤى اَمْرِ اللّٰهِۚ-فَاِنْ فَآءَتْ فَاَصْلِحُوْا بَیْنَهُمَا بِالْعَدْلِ وَ اَقْسِطُوْاؕ-اِنَّ اللّٰهَ یُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِیْنَ(9)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And if two groups of Muslims fight each other, so (O Muslims) make peace between them. Then if one oppresses the other, so fight with that oppressing group, until it reverts to the command of Allah. Then if it reverts, so reconcile between them with justice, and act justly (in every issue); indeed, Allah loves the just ones.

blocks.text: The occasion of revelation was that the Noble Prophet ﷺ was travelling on a donkey and paused near a gathering of the Ansar. The donkey urinated, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy held his nose. Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Rawahah رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ said, “The urine of the donkey of the Noble Prophet ﷺ is more fragrant than your musk.” The two exchanged words after the Noble Prophet ﷺ departed, their peoples fought and the matter reached blows. When the Noble Prophet ﷺ learned of it, he returned and made peace, and this verse was revealed. (Jalalayn with Sawi, 5/1992–1993; Madarik, p. 1153; Ruh al-Bayan, 9/73–76, excerpted.)

blocks.text: If two groups of believers fight, the Muslims must reconcile them. If one transgresses and refuses reconciliation, they must fight the transgressing group in support of the oppressed until it returns to Allah Almighty’s command. When it returns, the two groups must be reconciled with justice, without destroying the transgressing group; the purpose is to bring it firmly back to the straight path. Justice must be observed in every matter, and Allah Almighty loves the just.

blocks.text: Five matters follow: (1) Fighting and disputing are sins, but both parties were called believers, showing that sin is not disbelief. (2) Reconciling Muslims is a Sunnah of the Noble Prophet ﷺ and a high form of worship. (3) One who opposes or fights the Islamic ruler because of a misunderstanding is not a disbeliever or fasiq, but a believer. (4) The Islamic ruler must fight rebels until they stop their rebellion. (5) This fighting is not jihad; the rebels’ property is not spoils and their captives are not made slaves. Their strength is broken and they are treated as brothers.

blocks.text: The Quran and hadith repeatedly command reconciliation. Allah Almighty says: وَ اِنِ امْرَاَةٌ خَافَتْ مِنْۢ بَعْلِهَا نُشُوْزًا اَوْ اِعْرَاضًا فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَیْهِمَاۤ اَنْ یُّصْلِحَا بَیْنَهُمَا صُلْحًاؕ-وَ الصُّلْحُ خَیْرٌ (Al-Nisa: 128), meaning that if a woman fears her husband’s ill-treatment or aversion, there is no blame if they make reconciliation, and reconciliation is better. He says: یَسْــٴَـلُوْنَكَ عَنِ الْاَنْفَالِؕ -قُلِ الْاَنْفَالُ لِلّٰهِ وَ الرَّسُوْلِۚ-فَاتَّقُوا اللّٰهَ وَ اَصْلِحُوْا ذَاتَ بَیْنِكُمْ (Al-Anfal: 1), commanding mutual reconciliation. He says: لَا خَیْرَ فِیْ كَثِیْرٍ مِّنْ نَّجْوٰىهُمْ اِلَّا مَنْ اَمَرَ بِصَدَقَةٍ اَوْ مَعْرُوْفٍ اَوْ اِصْلَاحٍۭ بَیْنَ النَّاسِ (Al-Nisa: 114), promising a great reward to one who reconciles people for Allah’s pleasure.

blocks.text: Sayyidatuna Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا reports that the Chief of the Messengers ﷺ said: “The one who reconciles people is not a liar: he conveys or says good.” (Bukhari, Kitab al-Sulh, 2/210, hadith 2692.) Sayyiduna Abu Darda رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked whether he should tell them of an action better in rank than fasting, prayer and charity. When they said yes, he said: “Reconciling relations with one another.” (Abu Dawud, 4/365, hadith 4919.)

blocks.text: Reconciliation is permitted only within the limits of the Shariah. A settlement which makes the unlawful lawful or the lawful unlawful is not permitted. Three divorces make a woman unlawful for her former husband; merely making peace cannot make the unlawful lawful. Those who encourage such a settlement share in the sin of the unlawful relationship. May Allah Almighty grant Muslims sound understanding and the ability to reconcile within the limits of the Shariah.

blocks.text: Islam protects rights and social peace by commanding people to stop an oppressor and by warning the oppressor. Sayyiduna Anas رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ reports: “Help your brother whether he is an oppressor or oppressed.” When asked how to help an oppressor, the Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “Stop him from oppression; that is helping him.” (Bukhari, 4/389, hadith 6952.) Sayyiduna Ali al-Murtadha کَرَّمَ اللہ تَعَالٰی وَجْہَہُ الْکَرِیْم reports: “Beware the supplication of the oppressed; he asks Allah Almighty for his right, and Allah Almighty does not withhold the right of one entitled to it.” (Shu‘ab al-Iman, 6/49, hadith 7464.) Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ reports that whoever has wronged his Muslim brother in honour or anything else should seek his pardon today, before the Day when there will be no dinar or dirham: his good deeds will be taken according to his wrongdoing, and if he has no good deeds, the oppressed person’s sins will be placed upon him. (Bukhari, 2/128, hadith 2449; Mishkat, 2/235, hadith 5126.)

blocks.text: Two virtues of supporting the oppressed are mentioned: Sayyiduna Anas reports that Allah Almighty writes seventy-three kinds of forgiveness for the one who answers the plea of an oppressed person; one repairs all his affairs and seventy-two raise his rank on the Day of Judgement. (Shu‘ab al-Iman, 6/120, hadith 7670.) Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Umar reports that whoever goes with an oppressed person to help him will be given firmness on the day when feet slip. (Hilyat al-Awliya, Malik ibn Anas, 6/383, hadith 9012.)

blocks.text: Eight matters about the Companions and their apparent disagreements are important: (1) No saint of the Ummah, from the Tabi‘in until the Day of Judgement, can reach the rank of even the least-ranking Companion. (2) The nearness which the Companions possess in the court of Allah Almighty and the high ranks they will receive are unavailable to other Muslims. (3) Ahl al-Sunnat regard all Companions as exceptionally righteous and pious and consider investigating the details of who did what to whom and why to be impermissible. (4) If an action is reported which seems low in the eyes of the short-sighted, scholars explain it favourably and attribute it to sincere intention, remembering Allah’s true declaration رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ عَنْهُمْ rather than filling the heart with suspicion.

(2) The nearness which the Companions possess in the court of Allah Almighty and the high ranks they will receive are unavailable to other Muslims. (3) Ahl al-Sunnat regard all Companions as exceptionally righteous and pious and consider investigating the details of who did what to whom and why to be impermissible. (4) If an action is reported which seems low in the eyes of the short-sighted, scholars explain it favourably and attribute it to sincere intention, remembering Allah’s true declaration

rather than filling the heart with suspicion.

blocks.text: (5) Their rank is beyond our reason, so we cannot judge their matters. We must not favour one by insulting another or call one party worldly; all sought the welfare of the religion and the elevation of Islam and Muslims. They were also mujtahids: each followed the judgement which appeared more beneficial for Allah’s religion, the Shariah of the Noble Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims. Even when a judgement was mistaken, all remain deserving of respect, just as the mujtahids of Ahl al-Sunnat differ in subsidiary matters. (6) Muslims must not call the Companions misguided or fasiq because of these disputes and must not become enemies of any of them. All were devoted servants of the Noble Prophet ﷺ, honoured in the courts of Allah Almighty and His Messenger ﷺ and shining stars of guidance. (7) They were not Prophets or angels, so they were not protected from every human slip, but objecting to them in a manner contrary to the commands of Allah Almighty and His Messenger ﷺ is forbidden. (8) Allah Almighty promised good to both groups of Companions: those who spent and fought before the conquest and those who spent and fought afterwards. The first group had fewer resources and endured greater hardship, so it has greater rank, but Allah promised good to both. He says: كُلًّا وَّعَدَ اللّٰهُ الْحُسْنٰى. He also says that they are kept far from Hell, do not hear even its sound, remain in what their souls desire, are not saddened by the greatest terror, and are welcomed by the angels: اُولٰٓىٕكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُوْنَ, لَا یَسْمَعُوْنَ حَسِیْسَهَا, وَ هُمْ فِیْ مَا اشْتَهَتْ اَنْفُسُهُمْ خٰلِدُوْنَ, لَا یَحْزُنُهُمُ الْفَزَعُ الْاَكْبَرُ, وَ تَتَلَقّٰىهُمُ الْمَلٰٓىٕكَةُ, هٰذَا یَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِیْ كُنْتُمْ تُوْعَدُوْنَ (Al-Anbiya: 101–103). Allah Almighty knows what they did and nevertheless promised them Paradise without punishment and honour and reward without reckoning. (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 29/357–363, excerpted.)

اُولٰٓىٕكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُوْنَ
لَا یَسْمَعُوْنَ حَسِیْسَهَا
وَ هُمْ فِیْ مَا اشْتَهَتْ اَنْفُسُهُمْ خٰلِدُوْنَ
لَا یَحْزُنُهُمُ الْفَزَعُ الْاَكْبَرُ
وَ تَتَلَقّٰىهُمُ الْمَلٰٓىٕكَةُ
هٰذَا یَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِیْ كُنْتُمْ تُوْعَدُوْنَ

(Al-Anbiya: 101–103). Allah Almighty knows what they did and nevertheless promised them Paradise without punishment and honour and reward without reckoning. (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 29/357–363, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: The Muslims are brothers (to each other), therefore make peace between your two brothers, and fear Allah, that you may attain mercy.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
The Muslims are brothers (to each other), therefore make peace between your two brothers, and fear Allah, that you may attain mercy.

blocks.text: Muslims are brothers because they are joined by religious connection and Islamic love, and this bond is stronger than worldly relationships. When two brothers quarrel, reconcile them and fear Allah Almighty, so that you may receive mercy. Piety produces love and affection among believers, and Allah’s mercy is upon the one who fears Him. (Khazin, 4/168; Madarik, p. 1153, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Three hadith about Muslim brotherhood: (1) Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Umar رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ reports that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim: he neither oppresses him nor disgraces him. Whoever remains occupied fulfilling his brother’s need, Allah fulfils his need. Whoever removes a hardship from a Muslim, Allah removes one of his hardships on the Day of Judgement. Whoever conceals a Muslim’s fault, Allah will conceal his fault on the Day of Judgement.” (Bukhari, 2/126, hadith 2442.) (2) Sayyiduna Nu‘man ibn Bashir رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ reports: “All Muslims are like one person: when his eye suffers, the whole body suffers, and when his head aches, the whole body aches.” (Muslim, p. 1396, hadith 67 (2586).) (3) Sayyiduna Abu Musa Ash‘ari رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ reports: “A Muslim is to another Muslim like a building whose one brick strengthens another.” (Muslim, p. 1396, hadith 65 (2585).) May Allah Almighty grant Muslims understanding of their mutual relationship and the ability to fulfil its requirements.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O believers! Men must not ridicule other men, it is likely that the ridiculed are better than the mockers; nor must the women ridicule other women, it is likely that the ridiculed women may be better than the mockers; and do not taunt one another, nor give evil nicknames. What a bad name it is to be called an evildoer after being a Muslim. And whoever does not repent, it is they who are the unjust.

blocks.text: The parts of this verse were revealed on different occasions. Sayyiduna Thabit ibn Qays رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ had weak hearing, so the Companions made space for him near the Noble Prophet ﷺ. One day he came late, moved people aside saying “Make room,” and reached near the Noble Prophet ﷺ. One man told him to sit where he had found a place. Thabit became angry, sat behind him, and later asked his name. When he named himself, Thabit called him “son of such-and-such woman,” a phrase then used to shame people, and this verse was revealed. It was also revealed concerning people of Banu Tamim who mocked poor Companions such as Ammar, Khabbab, Bilal, Suhayb, Salman and Salim. Wealthy people must not mock the poor, the well-born those of another lineage, the healthy the disabled, or the sighted one whose eye has a defect; the mocked person may be better in sincerity before Allah Almighty. (Khazin, 4/169.)

blocks.text: The signs of poverty are not a reason to mock anyone; the poor person may be superior in religion. Sayyiduna Anas reports that many people with dishevelled, dusty hair and only two worn garments have such rank before Allah Almighty that if they swear by Allah, Allah fulfils their oath. (Tirmidhi, 5/459, hadith 3880.) Sayyiduna Harith ibn Wahb al-Khuza‘i reports that the people of Paradise include every weak person whom people consider low; if he swears by Allah, Allah fulfils his oath. (Tirmidhi, 4/272, hadith 2614.)

blocks.text: The women’s part was revealed, according to one report, concerning the purified wives of the Noble Prophet ﷺ when they shamed Sayyidatuna Umm Salamah رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا for her short stature. Another report says it concerned Sayyidatuna Safiyyah رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا when a purified wife called her the daughter of a Jew. Safiyyah wept; the Noble Prophet ﷺ told her that she was the daughter of a Prophet, the niece of a Prophet and the wife of a Prophet, and asked Sayyidatuna Hafsah رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا to fear Allah Almighty. (Tirmidhi, 5/474, hadith 3920.) Women’s joking with one another is not absolutely forbidden, but it is permitted only when it contains no obscenity, harm, disrespect to elders, rudeness to younger people, inappropriateness of time or place, or excess. (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 23/194.)

blocks.text: Mocking a Muslim through words, gestures, imitation or any other means, with the purpose of humiliation, is unlawful and sinful, because it humiliates and harms a Muslim and leads to Hell. (Jahannam ke Khatrat, p. 173.) The Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “Do not quarrel with your brother, mock him, or make a promise to him which you will break.” (Tirmidhi, 3/400, hadith 2002.) Sayyidatuna Aishah رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا reports that he did not like imitating anyone, even in exchange for great wealth. (Abu Dawud, 4/353, hadith 4875.) Sayyiduna Hasan reports that on the Day of Judgement a door of Paradise will be opened for the one who mocked people and he will be called to enter; when he reaches it, it will close, and this will continue until, when it opens and he is called, he will not go because of despair. (Mawsu‘at Ibn Abi Dunya, 7/183, hadith 287.)

blocks.text: Mockery includes exposing faults, imitating a person, taunting him, shaming him, laughing at him, and using hurtful names. Those who belittle poor people and use insulting titles because of wealth or social status must repent, or they will be fasiq and deserving of Hell. A harmless joke which makes a person happy is permitted and can sometimes be Sunnah. The Noble Prophet ﷺ sometimes joked but always spoke the truth. Imam Ghazali says that permissible joking must contain only truth, must not hurt anyone, must not exceed limits and must not become a profession; excessive and constant joking produces excessive laughter, hardens the heart, may create hatred, and removes dignity. The Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “I also joke, but I speak only the truth.” (Mu‘jam al-Awsat, 1/283, hadith 995.) Joking merely to make people laugh can cause a person to fall into Hell farther than the Pleiades. (Musnad Ahmad, 3/366, hadith 9231; Ihya, 3/158.)

blocks.text: Four examples of the Noble Prophet’s ﷺ gentle humour are mentioned. Sayyidatuna Umm Ayman رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہَا said that her husband was calling him. He asked, “Who, the one with whiteness in his eye?” She denied that her husband had it, so he explained that every eye has whiteness around its black centre. (Subul al-Huda, 7/114.) He used to mix with the people and said to Sayyiduna Anas’s young brother, “O Abu Umayr, what did the little bird do?” (Bukhari, 4/134, hadith 6129.) When a man asked for a riding animal, he said, “We will give you the child of a she-camel.” The man asked what he would do with a she-camel’s child, and the Noble Prophet ﷺ replied that every camel is born from a she-camel. (Tirmidhi, 3/399, hadith 1999.) He told an old woman that no old woman would enter Paradise; when she became anxious, he recited اِنَّاۤ اَنْشَاْنٰهُنَّ اِنْشَآءًۙ(۳۵) فَجَعَلْنٰهُنَّ اَبْكَارًا (Al-Waqi‘ah: 35–36), meaning: “Indeed, We have created the women of Paradise in a special manner, and made them virgins.” (Mishkat, 2/200, hadith 4888.)

blocks.text: Taunting is condemned. The Noble Prophet ﷺ said that those who frequently curse will be neither witnesses nor intercessors on the Day of Judgement, and that a believer is not one who taunts, curses, speaks obscenely or uses foul language. (Muslim, p. 1400, hadith 85 (2598); Tirmidhi, 3/393, hadith 1984.) Giving evil nicknames includes shaming a person after he has repented from a sin, calling a Muslim a dog, donkey or pig, and using a title which reveals his defect and which he dislikes. True honourable titles such as Siddiq’s ‘Atiq, Umar’s Faruq, Uthman’s Dhu al-Nurayn, Ali’s Abu Turab and Khalid’s Sayf Allah are not forbidden; nor are established names such as A‘mash and A‘raj when their bearers do not dislike them. (Khazin, 4/170.) Calling oneself a fasiq after Islam by mocking, fault-finding or corrupting names is an evil name, and those who do not repent are unjust.

blocks.text: Three rulings follow: (1) No group of Muslims is contemptible; every believer has honour. (2) Greatness depends not merely on lineage but on piety. (3) Insulting a Muslim brother through lineage is unlawful and the way of the polytheists; this disease is widespread, especially among women, and they should learn that the one who is better before Allah Almighty is unknown to them.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O believers! Avoid much suspicions; indeed, some suspicions become sin. And do not search for (hidden) faults, do not backbite one another; would any one amongst you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? So, you will not tolerate this. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is the Great Acceptor of repentance, Ever Merciful.

blocks.text: Believers must avoid excessive suspicion, because some suspicion is sin. Suspicion may be obligatory, recommended, forbidden or permissible: good opinion of Allah Almighty is obligatory; good opinion of a righteous believer is recommended; bad opinion of Allah Almighty or a believer is forbidden; and judging an openly sinful person according to his known conduct is permissible. Sayyiduna Sufyan Thawri رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ said that one suspicion is expressed in the heart and on the tongue, and is sinful when it is evil towards a Muslim; another arises in the heart without being spoken, which is not itself a sin but should still be removed. Imam Razi explains that suspicion causes fault-finding and other evil deeds, while an apparently bad action may have a valid explanation. (Ibn Kathir, 7/352; Tafsir Kabir, 10/110; Baydawi, 5/218; Khazin, 4/170–171.)

blocks.text: Bad opinion of a Muslim is unlawful unless there is legal proof. As far as possible, his words and deeds must be interpreted correctly. If a clear indication establishes the suspected matter, it is no longer sinful to hold that view; one who repeatedly enters a place of accusation is responsible for exposing himself to suspicion. A righteous believer’s words must not be given a corrupt meaning when a sound meaning exists and his condition supports it. (Fatawa Razawiyyah, 6/486 and 20/278; Fatawa Amjadiyyah, 1/123; Khazain al-Irfan, p. 950.)

blocks.text: The Noble Prophet ﷺ said: “Avoid suspicion, for suspicion is the worst of lies. Do not search for one another’s outward or inward faults, do not be greedy, jealous or hateful, and do not turn away from one another; become brothers, O servants of Allah.” (Muslim, p. 1386, hadith 28 (2563).) Suspicion causes four religious harms: it may hurt the person if expressed before him; expressing it in his absence becomes backbiting; it leads to searching for faults; and it produces hatred and jealousy. Its worldly harms include enmity between brothers, hostility between mother-in-law and daughter-in-law, loss of trust and eventual divorce between spouses, broken sibling relationships, and the destruction of a peaceful home. A report cited in the source says that hostile thoughts, mental stress and anger increase the risk of heart disease and stroke by 86 percent. Imam Ghazali says that even if the smell of wine comes from someone, one must not punish him merely on that basis, because he may have rinsed his mouth after one sip or may have been forced to drink it; do not make Satan happy by confirming suspicion in the heart. (Ihya Ulum al-Din, 3/186, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Do not spy or search for hidden faults which Allah Almighty has concealed. The Noble Prophet ﷺ warned those whose tongues profess faith but whose hearts do not contain it: whoever searches out his Muslim brother’s hidden fault, Allah Almighty will search out his hidden fault and disgrace him, even inside his home. (Abu Dawud, 4/354, hadith 4880.) Searching for faults is a trait of hypocrites and ends in disgrace; whoever searches for another’s fault should fear that Allah Almighty may expose his own hidden faults.

blocks.text: Two virtues of concealing faults are mentioned: whoever conceals a Muslim’s fault, Allah conceals his faults on the Day of Judgement; and whoever sees something which should be concealed and conceals it is like one who gives life to a buried infant girl. (Bukhari, 2/126, hadith 2442; Abu Dawud, 4/357, hadith 4819.) A person should search for and correct his own faults rather than those of others. The Noble Prophet ﷺ said that a person sees a splinter in his brother’s eye while forgetting the branch in his own eye. Sayyiduna Ibn Abbas said that when intending to mention a companion’s fault, remember your own faults. (Shu‘ab al-Iman, 5/311, ahadith 6761 and 6758.)

blocks.text: Islam greatly values human honour, especially the honour of a Muslim. It forbids seeking out faults and displaying them without a Shariah-permitted need. Backbiting is to mention, in a person’s absence, a defect which he dislikes, even if it is true; if it is false, it is slander. The dead brother’s flesh is used as an example because cutting flesh causes pain just as disparaging a person causes pain to his heart, while honour is dearer than flesh. The occasion of revelation involved Sayyiduna Salman رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, who had been assigned to serve two wealthy men. When he slept and could not prepare food, they sent him to the Noble Prophet’s ﷺ kitchen; Sayyiduna Usamah رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ said he had no food. The two men said that Usamah had been miserly. When they came to the Noble Prophet ﷺ, he said, “I see the colour of meat in your mouths.” They said they had eaten no meat, and he said, “You backbit your brother; whoever backbites a Muslim eats his flesh.” (Khazin, 4/170–171, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Four hadith condemn backbiting. The Noble Prophet ﷺ defined it as mentioning about one’s brother what he dislikes; if the defect exists, it is backbiting, and if it does not exist, it is slander. (Muslim, p. 1397, hadith 70 (2589).) He said that backbiting is more severe than adultery: an adulterer may repent and Allah accepts his repentance, but the backbiter is not forgiven until the wronged person forgives him. (Shu‘ab al-Iman, 5/306, hadith 6741.) During the Ascension he saw people with copper nails tearing their faces and chests; Jibril عَلَیْہِ السَّلَام said that they were those who ate people’s flesh and violated their honour. (Abu Dawud, 4/353, hadith 4878.) Whoever ate his brother’s flesh in the world will be brought his brother’s flesh on the Day of Judgement and told to eat living flesh as he ate dead flesh; he will eat it screaming and distorting his face. (Mu‘jam al-Awsat, 1/450, hadith 1656.)

blocks.text: Backbiting can occur by speech, action, clear statement, insinuation, writing, head movements, eyes, lips, eyebrows, tongue or hands. Imitating a lame person’s walk or another person’s manner is also backbiting and may be worse because it vividly conveys the defect. Mentioning a deceased Muslim’s defect is backbiting, while insulting a protected non-Muslim is also impermissible; insulting a hostile disbeliever is not backbiting. Criticising someone to his face is even more unlawful when it harms him. Whoever hears backbiting must reject it verbally; if he fears harm, he must reject it in his heart, leave the gathering if possible, or change the subject, otherwise he shares the sin. (Bahar-e-Shariat, part 16, 3/532, 536–538.)

blocks.text: If the person who was backbitten learns of it, the backbiter must seek his pardon and specify what he said, then repent. If he did not learn of it, repentance and regret are sufficient. Scholars differ on the case where the person learns after repentance; in either case, slander requires repentance and correcting the falsehood before those who heard it. Seeking pardon should include sincere praise and showing affection to remove the pain from the person’s heart. If the apology was merely outward and insincere, there may still be accountability. If the wronged person has died or is absent, Imam Ghazali advises performing many good deeds, so that even if they are transferred for the backbiting, some remain. See also the books Badgumani and Ghibat ki Tabahkariyan. ([1], [2])

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the august court of Allah's (Beloved) Messenger, they are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety; for them is forgiveness and great reward.

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:
Indeed, those who lower their voices in the august court of Allah's (Beloved) Messenger, they are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety; for them is forgiveness and great reward.

blocks.text: {Indeed, those who lower their voices in the august court of Allah's Messenger:} When the verse, “O believers! Do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet” was revealed, Sayyiduna Abu Bakr Siddiq, Sayyiduna Umar Farooq and some other Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ adopted great caution and spoke very softly in the august presence of the Sovereign of both worlds ﷺ, as mentioned above. This verse was revealed concerning them, and their conduct was praised: Indeed, those who lower their voices in the august court of Allah Almighty’s Messenger ﷺ out of respect and reverence are the very people whose hearts Allah Almighty has tested for piety and made the piety within them apparent; for them there is forgiveness and a great reward in the Hereafter. (Jalalayn with Sawi, Al-Hujurat, under verse 3, 5/1987–1988.)

blocks.text: Five lessons from the verse “Indeed, those who lower their voices”:

runs.text: Five lessons from the verse “Indeed, those who lower their voices”:

blocks.text: (1) All other acts of worship are the piety of the body, while showing respect to the Noble Prophet ﷺ is the piety of the heart.

runs.text: (1) All other acts of worship are the piety of the body, while showing respect to the Noble Prophet ﷺ is the piety of the heart.

blocks.text: (2) Allah Almighty has tested the hearts of the Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ for piety. Therefore, the person who, Allah forbid, considers them sinful is a denier of this verse.

runs.text: (2) Allah Almighty has tested the hearts of the Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ for piety. Therefore, the person who, Allah forbid, considers them sinful is a denier of this verse.

blocks.text: (3) The Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ were extremely pious and greatly fearful of Allah Almighty. Whoever believed the Noble Prophet ﷺ to be Allah Almighty’s Messenger and honoured him so greatly that he would not even raise his voice before him out of fear that his deeds might be ruined by raising his voice, must have had immense reverence and fear of Allah Almighty in his heart.

runs.text: (3) The Companions رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمْ were extremely pious and greatly fearful of Allah Almighty. Whoever believed the Noble Prophet ﷺ to be Allah Almighty’s Messenger and honoured him so greatly that he would not even raise his voice before him out of fear that his deeds might be ruined by raising his voice, must have had immense reverence and fear of Allah Almighty in his heart.

blocks.text: (4) The forgiveness of Sayyiduna Abu Bakr Siddiq and Sayyiduna Umar Farooq رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا is certain, because Allah Almighty has announced their forgiveness.

runs.text: (4) The forgiveness of Sayyiduna Abu Bakr Siddiq and Sayyiduna Umar Farooq رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا is certain, because Allah Almighty has announced their forgiveness.

blocks.text: (5) The reward of these two revered personalities is beyond our imagination, because Allah Almighty has described it as great.

blocks.text: The rank of Sayyiduna Thabit رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ:

runs.text: The rank of Sayyiduna Thabit رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ:

blocks.text: Despite his disability, Sayyiduna Thabit رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ made it binding upon himself that he would never raise his voice above the voice of the Noble Prophet ﷺ. Sayyiduna Anas رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ says: We used to see a man from the people of Paradise walking before us. When the battle against Musaylimah took place at Yamamah, Sayyiduna Thabit رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ saw that a group of Muslims had been defeated and said, “How regrettable these people are!” He then said to Sayyiduna Salim رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, the freed slave of Sayyiduna Hudhayfah رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, “We did not fight the enemies of Allah in this manner alongside the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” They both stood firm and continued fighting until they were martyred.

blocks.text: After Sayyiduna Thabit رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ was martyred, a Companion saw him in a dream. He said, “Such-and-such a person removed my armour and placed it beneath a stone cooking pot near a horse at the corner of the army camp. Go to Sayyiduna Khalid ibn Walid رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ and inform him so that he may recover my armour. Then go to the Caliph of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Sayyiduna Abu Bakr Siddiq رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, and tell him that I have a debt, so that he may pay it, and that such-and-such of my slaves is free.” The Companion informed Sayyiduna Khalid ibn Walid رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, who found the armour and the horse exactly as Sayyiduna Thabit رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ had described. He took the armour and informed Sayyiduna Abu Bakr Siddiq رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ of the dream. Sayyiduna Abu Bakr Siddiq رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ carried out Sayyiduna Thabit’s bequest.

blocks.text: The occasion of revelation was that several people from Banu Tamim came to serve the Noble Prophet ﷺ at midday, while the Noble Prophet ﷺ was resting. It described the exalted rank of the Chief of the Messengers ﷺ and declared that calling him in this manner in his august court was ignorance and lack of sense. blocks.text: {And had they been patient:} This verse teaches those people manners: instead of calling the Noble Prophet ﷺ, they should have exercised patience and waited until the Noble Prophet ﷺ himself came out of the sacred room to them and then they presented their request. Had they observed this obligatory etiquette, it would have been better for them. If those from whom this disrespect occurred repent, Allah Almighty is Forgiving towards them and Merciful to them. (Khazin, Al-Hujurat, under verse 5, 4/166; Ruh al-Bayan, Al-Hujurat, under verse 5, 9/68, excerpted.)

blocks.text: An etiquette when visiting scholars and teachers:

runs.text: An etiquette when visiting scholars and teachers:

blocks.text: This verse indicates that when one visits the close servants of Allah Almighty and practising scholars, one should not show haste by knocking at the door of their residence. Rather, one should wait so that they may come out according to their usual routine. This was the practice of our righteous predecessors. The eminent scholar Sayyiduna Abu Ubayd رَحْمَۃُ اللّٰهِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْهِ used to say: I never knocked at the door of any teacher. I continued waiting for him, and when he himself came out, I benefited from him.

runs.text: This verse indicates that when one visits the close servants of Allah Almighty and practising scholars, one should not show haste by knocking at the door of their residence. Rather, one should wait so that they may come out according to their usual routine. This was the practice of our righteous predecessors. The eminent scholar Sayyiduna Abu Ubayd رَحْمَۃُ اللّٰهِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْهِ used to say: I never knocked at the door of any teacher. I continued waiting for him, and when he himself came out, I benefited from him.

blocks.text: Similarly, when Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Abbas رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا went to the home of Sayyiduna Ubayy ibn Ka'b رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ to learn the Holy Quran from him, he would stand near the door and would not knock. Rather, he would silently wait until Sayyiduna Ubayy ibn Ka'b came out according to his usual routine. This conduct displeased Sayyiduna Ubayy ibn Ka'b, so he said to him, “Why did you not knock at the door, so that I could come out immediately and you would not have had to bear the difficulty of waiting?” Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Abbas رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُمَا replied, “A scholar among his people is like a Prophet among his nation,” meaning that a scholar is the heir of a Prophet. Since Allah Almighty said regarding His Noble Prophet ﷺ, “And had they been patient until you yourself would come out to them, so it would have been better for them,” I therefore waited for you to come out yourself instead of knocking at the door.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: O believers! If any sinner brings you some news, so you must investigate (it) in case you unknowingly cause suffering to some people then (later on) remain regretful for what you have done.
