blocks.text: {O believers! If any sinner brings you some news, so you must investigate:} Allah Almighty says: O believers! If a fasiq brings you some report containing a complaint against someone, do not rely only upon his statement; rather, investigate whether it is true or not. The one who does not refrain from fisq will not refrain from lying either. Investigate, lest you unknowingly cause harm to a people and then, when their innocence becomes clear, have to regret what you did.

blocks.text: The commentators have stated this occasion of revelation: The Noble Prophet ﷺ sent Sayyiduna Walid ibn Uqbah رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ to collect charity from Banu Mustaliq. There had been enmity between them in the era of ignorance. When Sayyiduna Walid رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ came near their territory and the people learned of his arrival, many of them came out to welcome him, thinking that he had been sent by the Noble Prophet ﷺ and wishing to honour him. Sayyiduna Walid رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ, however, thought that they had come to kill him because of the old enmity. He therefore returned and reported to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, according to his assumption, “They have refused to give charity and intend to kill me.” The Noble Prophet ﷺ sent Sayyiduna Khalid ibn Walid رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ to investigate the situation. Sayyiduna Khalid رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ saw that the people were calling the Adhan, performing prayer and had presented their charity. He brought the charity to the august presence and related what had happened. Thereupon this noble verse was revealed. (Khazin, Al-Hujurat, under verse 6, 4/166–167; Madarik, Al-Hujurat, under verse 6, p. 1152; Ruh al-Bayan, Al-Hujurat, under verse 6, 9/70–71, excerpted.)

blocks.text: Sayyiduna Walid رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ was a Companion, and none of the Companions is a fasiq:

runs.text: Sayyiduna Walid رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ was a Companion, and none of the Companions is a fasiq:

blocks.text: It should be remembered that this verse does not specifically call Sayyiduna Walid رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ a fasiq. Rather, it states an Islamic law. Therefore, he cannot be called a fasiq on the basis of this verse. Allamah Ahmad Sawi رَحْمَۃُ اللّٰهِ تَعَالٰی عَلَیْهِ says: Although the incident of Sayyiduna Walid رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ was the cause of this verse’s revelation, the word fasiq does not specifically refer to him, because he was not a fasiq but a great Companion. (Sawi, Al-Hujurat, under verse 6, 5/1990–1991, excerpted.)

blocks.text: The summary is that although the incident of Sayyiduna Walid ibn Uqbah رَضِیَ اللّٰهُ تَعَالٰی عَنْہُ was indeed the cause of this verse’s revelation, the verse does not specifically call him a fasiq. This is because no action had issued from him, in this incident or before it, which would justify calling him a fasiq. In this incident too, he attributed something to Banu Mustaliq because he believed, according to his assumption, that it was true, although it was actually incorrect. This is not something for which a person can be declared a fasiq.

blocks.text: Islam’s role in making society a cradle of peace:

runs.text: Islam’s role in making society a cradle of peace:

blocks.text: This verse teaches that Islam prevents actions which obstruct social peace and commands actions through which society becomes a cradle of peace and tranquillity. If we keep the principle stated in this verse before us today, our society can become a cradle of peace. Fights and disorder occur among us for this very reason: when someone receives information, he does not verify it but immediately becomes angry and does something which leaves him troubled for the rest of his life. The family disputes among us are of the same nature, whether they concern a mother-in-law and daughter-in-law or a husband and wife: the matter is not verified and fighting begins.

blocks.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation: And know that Allah's (Beloved) Messenger is amongst you; if he acts according to your liking in many of your matters, so you would certainly be in trouble. But Allah has made faith dear to you and has beautified it in your hearts, and has made disbelief, and disobedience, and sinning detested to you. The very same people are on the path (of guidance).

runs.text: Kanz-ul-Iman English translation:

And know that Allah's (Beloved) Messenger is amongst you; if he acts according to your liking in many of your matters, so you would certainly be in trouble. But Allah has made faith dear to you and has beautified it in your hearts, and has made disbelief, and disobedience, and sinning detested to you. The very same people are on the path (of guidance).

blocks.text: وَ اعْلَمُوْۤا اَنَّ فِیْكُمْ رَسُوْلَ اللّٰهِ: Know that Allah Almighty's Messenger is present among you. If any of you tells him a lie, Allah Almighty will inform him, and he will expose your condition by His command and disgrace you. Therefore, do not tell him anything false. Remember that if he were to follow your advice in many of the matters you present to him and issue rulings according to your opinion, you would certainly fall into hardship. However, Allah Almighty, out of mercy for you, protected him from this, placed the love of faith in your hearts and adorned it within your hearts. Through its blessing, you do not disobey the Noble Prophet ﷺ. He made disbelief, disobedience and sin detestable to you, causing you to turn away from disobedience. Such people are rightly guided and remain firm upon the straight path through the grace and favour of Allah Almighty. The attribute of Allah Almighty is that He knows their conditions and is Wise in bestowing favours upon them. (Madarik, Al-Hujurat, under verses 7–8, p. 1152–1153; Khazin, Al-Hujurat, under verses 7–8, 4/167; Jalalayn with Sawi, Al-Hujurat, under verses 7–8, 5/1991–1992, excerpted.)
